Suddenly, Sarah saw a figure standing in front of her. He said in a deep voice, "I am the Fake Number. I will give you anything you want in exchange for your soul". Sarah was scared and said, "No, I do not want to trade my soul". 

But the Fake Number refused to leave. He said, "I will not leave until you turn the number one more time. Then our deal will be done". 

Sarah was too scared to move. But when she heard the Fake Number threatening to take her soul if she refused to turn the number, she decided to do it. 

Sadness and fear filled her heart as she slowly turned the number one last time. The Fake Number grabbed her soul and flew away. Sarah never saw him again. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Maggie. Every night, she would write a letter to her mom and tell her how much she loved her. Each day, Maggie would take her letters to the post office and mail them.

One day, as Maggie was walking to the post office, it started to rain. Maggie was running, but she couldn't keep the letter dry. By the time she arrived, the envelope had a leak!

Maggie was so upset. She told the postman, "I want to write a letter to my mom but the envelope has a leak. What should I do?"

The postman smiled and said, "Maggie, sometimes it's better to pick a tougher, yet cheaper way than taking the easy one. This time, use a plastic sleeve for your letter so it won't get wet. That way, your mom will still get your letter as long as you mail it in time".

Maggie smiled and took the postman's advice. Every night, she would write a letter, place it in an envelope and put it in a cheap, plastic sleeve for protection. Now, Maggie's letters always made it to her mom.

Moral of the story: Always take the tougher, yet cheaper way to get something done and you'll save time and effort in the long run.

"Sure, Max!" said Bella. "I love twisty paths!"

As they walked and talked, Max felt a pain in his heel. He stopped and looked at his foot. There was a small stone stuck in his heel. Bella saw Max's hurt face and asked, "What's wrong, Max?"

"My heel hurts," said Max. "There's a stone in it."

Bella helped Max take out the stone. They continued walking on the twisty path, happy and smiling. They were glad to have each other as friends, and they had a fun day together.

Timmy was sad, and his mommy said, "Always listen to me, and be careful with sharp things. Otherwise, bad things can happen." Timmy learned his lesson and promised to be careful.

After they were done, they decided to make some pasta for dinner. But when they opened the box, they found out that it was very old and had bugs in it. Lily's mom got upset and said they couldn't eat it.

In the end, they made a delicious salad and had a fun dinner together. Lily was happy that she could help her mom and come up with a solution to their problem.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly woman who lived in a small house with her dog. One day, the woman and her dog went for a walk in the park. It was very cold outside and the woman told her dog to stay close to her.

As they were walking, they saw a pond with ice on it. The woman warned her dog not to go near it because the ice could break and he could fall in. Suddenly, the dog saw a squirrel and ran towards it. He didn't listen to the woman and went onto the ice. Suddenly, the ice broke and the dog fell in. He was very cold and started to freeze.

The woman quickly called for help and some kind people came to rescue the dog. They wrapped him in a warm blanket and took him to the vet. Luckily, the dog was okay and learned his lesson to always listen to his owner. From that day on, the woman and her dog never went near frozen ponds again.

Flutter told Buggy about a beautiful garden with lots of colorful flowers and tasty nectar. Buggy was so excited to visit this garden and see all the pretty flowers. 

So, Buggy and Flutter set off on their adventure. They traveled through fields and forests until they finally arrived at the garden. Buggy was amazed by the large and colorful flowers and was so happy that he got to travel and see them with his new friend.

From that day on, she learned that being patient and observing can help her overcome her fears.

The little boy listened and understood what the man said. He realized that guns are not popular toys to play with. From that day on, the boy never touched a gun again and always remembered what the man told him.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very small, but he dreamed of finding treasure. One day, Timmy went to the beach with his mom. He saw a tall ship sailing in the sea. 

Timmy: "Mommy, look at that tall ship! Can we go see it?"

Mommy: "Sure, Timmy. Let's go."

When they got closer, they saw a pirate on the ship. The pirate had a treasure chest!

Timmy: "Wow, I want to find treasure too!"

Pirate: "Arrr, ye want treasure, do ye? Well, ye have to be a brave sailor to find it!"

Timmy: "I can sail! I can be brave!"

So, Timmy and his mom set sail with the pirate to find treasure. They faced many challenges, but in the end, they found the treasure chest. Timmy was so happy!

Timmy: "Mommy, we found treasure! I'm a brave sailor!"

Mommy: "Yes, you are, Timmy. And you're also very smart to have found the treasure."

"Thank you, thank you!" Sam said. "You saved me!"

Sam and Tom learned a lesson. They said sorry to the man and to each other. They promised to be more respectful and not to go on boats without permission. They hugged and went home. They were happy to be safe and to have a good friend.

Timmy said goodbye to his friends and started to pack up his toys. His backpack was so heavy that he had to ask his dad for help. "Dad, can you help me carry my backpack? It's too heavy for me," Timmy said.

His dad smiled and said, "Sure thing, Timmy. Let's go home." And with that, they walked home together, Timmy's heavy backpack safely on his dad's back.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she went to the park to play. She saw her friend Timmy there.

"Hi Timmy!" Lily said.

"Hi Lily!" Timmy said.

"Do you want to play with me?" Lily asked.

"Yes, let's play!" Timmy said.

They played on the swings and the slide. Then, they sat down on the grass.

"I can spell my name," Lily said.

"Wow, that's great!" Timmy said.

"Can you spell your name?" Lily asked.

"Um... no," Timmy said.

"That's okay, you can stay here and I'll teach you," Lily said.

And they stayed there all afternoon, practicing how to spell their names. It was a jolly good time!

Once upon a time, there was a little ant named Andy. Andy was very eager to explore the world outside his ant hill. One day, he asked his mom if he could go outside, but his mom said, "Not yet, Andy. You're still too little."

Andy felt sad, but he didn't give up. He kept asking his mom every day until finally, she said, "Okay, Andy. You can go outside, but be careful."

Excitedly, Andy crawled out of the ant hill and explored the grass. Suddenly, he saw a big piece of candy. He tried to carry it back to his ant hill, but it was too heavy. Just then, a friendly grasshopper came by and offered to help.

"Thank you so much!" said Andy. "I'll give you a reward when we get back to the ant hill."

The grasshopper smiled and said, "No need for a reward, Andy. Helping friends is its own reward."

From that day on, Andy and the grasshopper were the best of friends, and Andy never forgot the lesson he learned about the value of helping others.

One hot day, the sun shone and shone. The rays made the cross feel so hot that it started to melt. The cross became a tiny, yellow puddle.

The people were very sad. They loved the cross, but knew it couldn't stay melted forever.

They wanted to fix it, so they took the puddle and put it in a bucket. They added some cold water and mixed it together. When they took it out, it was back to normal - cool and strong!

The people were happy again and made sure to keep the cross away from the sunshine so it wouldn't melt again. And they all lived happily ever after!

But as he was playing with his car again, Timmy accidentally hit his little sister's toy and broke it. She started crying and Timmy felt bad. He knew he had to make it up to her. So he gave her his favorite car to play with and they both zoomed around the room together, happy once again.

Suddenly, the vine started to separate from the ground and fall towards Tweet. She closed her eyes and waited for it to hit her, but it landed just beside her. Tweet was very scared and didn't know what to do. 

Just then, a kind, old man came to the garden and saw Tweet. He gently picked her up and took her to a safe place. The man saw the fallen vine and knew what to do. He got his tools and fixed the vine so it would never separate again. Tweet was happy to have a new friend and a safe place to play in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little clown. The clown was very frightened of the dark. He lived in a small house with his mom and dad. One day, his mom and dad went out. They told the clown to be brave and not be scared.

At night, the little clown heard a noise. He was so frightened. He wanted to turn on the light. But he could not reach the light switch. So, he called out, "Who is there? Please help me turn on the light."

A big, scary monster came into his room. The monster said, "I will help you turn on the light." The little clown was even more frightened. He did not want the monster to help him. But the monster turned on the light anyway.

The little clown saw that the monster was not so scary after all. He was just a big, friendly dog. The dog said, "I am here to play with you." But the little clown was still frightened. He wanted his mom and dad to come home.

But his mom and dad did not come home. The little clown was so sad and scared. He cried and cried. The big, friendly dog tried to make him feel better. But the little clown just wanted his mom and dad. And they never came back.

But then, they saw a big scary shadow. It was a big bear! Bobo and his friends were scared. They ran away very fast. The bear did not chase them. Bobo and his friends were safe. They went back to their homes and told their families about their adventure.

One day, she was drawing a flower. She wanted to make it yellow and pink. But she picked up a green crayon by mistake and drew on the petals. She saw the green and cried. She did not like the green. She wanted to erase it, but she did not have an eraser.

She looked around and saw her thumb. She had an idea. She licked her thumb and tried to wipe the green off the paper. She rubbed hard and hoped the green would go away. But it did not. It only made the paper wet and wrinkled. She cried louder and threw the paper on the floor.

Her mom heard her cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw the paper and the crayons and the wet thumb. She hugged Sara and said, "It's okay, sweetie. You don't have to be perfect. You can make mistakes. That's how you learn and grow. And you can always start again with a new paper."

She gave Sara a tissue and helped her wipe her thumb and her tears. She gave her a new paper and a new crayon. She said, "You can draw anything you want. I love your pictures. They are beautiful and creative. And I love you, no matter what."

So, Otto and his friends went down the slide slowly and safely. Otto was no longer anxious, he was happy again. From that day on, Otto knew that he could always count on his friends to help him when he was feeling scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bun. Bun had soft fur that was fun to touch. One day, Bun's friend, a wise owl, came to visit. Owl said, "Bun, I recommend we go on an adventure!" Bun thought that sounded interesting, so they set off into the forest.

As they walked, they saw many things. They saw tall trees, colorful flowers, and squirrels scurrying about. Owl told Bun interesting stories about the forest and its creatures. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise! It was a bear! Bun was scared, but Owl said, "Don't worry, I know what to do." Owl recommended that they climb a nearby tree. They climbed up high and watched as the bear walked by.

After the bear was gone, Bun and Owl continued their adventure. They found a beautiful waterfall and a field of wildflowers. It was the most interesting day Bun had ever had! When they got back to Bun's burrow, Bun's mom asked how their day was. Bun said, "It was so much fun! Owl recommended we go on an adventure and we saw so many interesting things!"

Once upon a time, there was a clever bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety saw a cup on the ground. Tweety thought it would be fun to play with the cup, so he picked it up with his beak and flew away.

As Tweety was flying, he saw a group of animals who were very thirsty. They asked Tweety if he had any water to share. Tweety felt bad because he didn't have any water, but then he remembered the cup he was carrying. He filled the cup with water and gave it to the animals. They were very grateful and thanked Tweety.

From that day on, Tweety always carried the cup with him when he flew. Whenever he saw someone who needed water, he would fill the cup and share it with them. Tweety learned that it's important to help others and that even small things like a cup of water can make a big difference. And so, Tweety lived happily ever after, flying and helping others along the way.

"Thank you for saving me," said Lily. "You're the best knight in the world."

Lily was curious and wanted to see what was inside the shell. She took the shell from Tom and tried to open it. But the shell was very hard and she could not open it.

"Let me help you," Tom said. He took the shell and tried to break it with a rock. He hit the shell hard and it cracked.

"Stop, Tom, stop!" Lily cried. "You are hurting the shell and the thing inside. It is not nice to break someone's home. Maybe the thing inside is scared and sad."

Tom stopped and looked at Lily. He felt sorry for what he did. He saw a small creature peeking out of the shell. It had a round body, a long tail and two big eyes. It was cute and looked afraid.

Lily did not know what it was, but she smiled and said, "It is a shell-friend. We can encourage it to come out and play with us. Maybe it is lonely and needs some friends. We can be gentle and kind to it."

The moral of the story is: We should not break or harm other people's homes or things. We should be curious and friendly, but also respectful and gentle. We can make new friends and learn new things if we encourage and help each other.

Tom and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were cooking. Tom had a big pot and Lily had a small spoon. They filled the pot with water from the tap and put it on the stove. The stove was not hot, because Mom had turned it off.

"Look, Lily, I am making soup!" Tom said. He stirred the water with his spoon. He added some salt and pepper from the jars. He smelled the water. "Mmm, it smells good!"

"Can I try?" Lily asked. She reached for the pot with her spoon. But the pot was too heavy for her. She tipped it over and the water spilled out. It made a big splash on the floor and on Tom and Lily.

"Uh-oh!" Tom and Lily said. They were wet and cold. They looked at the mess they had made. They heard Mom coming.

"What happened here?" Mom asked. She saw the water, the salt, the pepper, and the pot. She saw Tom and Lily's wet clothes and faces. She was not happy.

"Sorry, Mom," Tom and Lily said. They felt bad. They knew they had done something wrong.

Mom sighed. She was not angry, but she was not pleased. She took a towel and dried Tom and Lily. She took another towel and wiped the floor and the stove. She put the pot and the spoon in the sink. She hugged Tom and Lily.

"Next time, be more careful," Mom said. "And don't play with the stove. It can be dangerous. If you want to cook, ask me first. I can help you."

"Okay, Mom," Tom and Lily said. They learned their lesson. They thanked Mom for being gentle. They went to play with their toys in the living room. They did not splash anymore.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had many toys of different colors and shapes. Anna liked to sort the toys by color. She put the red toys in one pile, the blue toys in another pile, and so on. Ben liked to sort the toys by shape. He put the round toys in one pile, the square toys in another pile, and so on.

"Look, Anna, I sorted the toys by shape. Do you like it?" Ben asked.

"Yes, Ben, it looks nice. But I sorted the toys by color. Do you like it?" Anna asked.

"Yes, Anna, it looks nice. But I like shape better than color. Can we play with my pile?" Ben asked.

"No, Ben, I like color better than shape. Can we play with my pile?" Anna asked.

They started to argue about whose pile was better. They did not want to share or mix the toys. They raised their voices and made a lot of noise.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the toys sorted in two piles and the children fighting. She was not happy.

"Anna and Ben, what are you doing? Why are you fighting?" Mom asked.

"Mom, we sorted the toys, but we don't agree. I like color and she likes shape. We want to play with our own pile," Ben said.

"Mom, we sorted the toys, but we don't agree. I like shape and he likes color. We want to play with our own pile," Anna said.

Mom sighed. She had an idea.

"Anna and Ben, I have a snack for you. Do you want some?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom, we want some," Anna and Ben said. They were hungry and curious.

Mom brought a tray with some cookies and fruits. She put the tray on the table.

"Look, Anna and Ben, I sorted the snack for you. I put the cookies in one pile and the fruits in another pile. Do you like it?" Mom asked.

Anna and Ben looked at the snack. They saw that the cookies were of different colors and shapes. They saw that the fruits were of different colors and shapes. They realized that they could sort the snack in different ways.

"Yes, Mom, we like it. But can we sort the snack in our own way?" Anna and Ben asked.

"Sure, you can. But you have to share and take turns. And you have to eat some of both. OK?" Mom said.

"OK, Mom. Thank you," Anna and Ben said.

They stopped fighting and started to sort the snack in their own way. They shared and took turns. They ate some of both. They were happy and full.

Mom smiled. She was glad that they learned to sort, share and enjoy. She was not anxious anymore.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a fat cat on a bench. The cat is black and white and has a red collar.

"Look, a fat cat!" Lily says. "Can we pet it?"

Ben nods. "Yes, but we have to be gentle. Maybe it will let us play with it."

They skip to the bench and sit next to the cat. The cat looks at them and purrs. Lily and Ben smile and stroke its fur.

"Hello, fat cat. What is your name?" Lily asks.

The cat meows and rubs its head against Lily's hand. Ben sees a tag on the collar. It says "Molly".

"Her name is Molly. She is a nice cat." Ben says.

Lily and Ben play with Molly for a while. They tickle her ears and scratch her chin. Molly rolls over and shows her belly.

"She likes us. Can we take her home?" Lily asks.

Ben shakes his head. "No, we can't. She belongs to someone else. See, she has a collar. That means she has a home and a family. We have to leave her here."

Lily frowns. "But I want to play with her more. She is so soft and cute."

Ben hugs Lily. "I know, me too. But we have to be fair. How would you feel if someone took your toy or your doll?"

Lily thinks. She does not like it when someone takes her things. She loves her toy and her doll. She nods. "You are right. We have to be fair. But can we come back and see her again?"

Ben smiles. "Of course we can. We can come back tomorrow. And the next day. And the next day. We can be her friends. But we have to make a promise."

Lily holds out her pinky. "A promise? What is a promise?"

Ben wraps his pinky around hers. "A promise is when you say something and you mean it. And you don't break it. Ever. We promise to be nice to Molly and not take her away. And we promise to come back and play with her. OK?"

Lily nods. "OK. I promise. Pinky promise."

They kiss their pinkies and smile. Then they say goodbye to Molly and skip back to their parents. They are happy. They have a new friend. And they have a promise.

"Can I write in your lab, dad?" Tom asks.

"Sure, son, but you have to be careful. There are some things in the lab that are not for writing. They are for testing and measuring and mixing. They can be dangerous or break if you touch them." His dad says.

Tom nods and follows his dad to the lab. He sees many machines and bottles and tubes. He also sees a big white board where his dad writes some words and numbers. Tom thinks the board looks fun. He wants to write on it too.

He picks up a marker and starts to write his name on the board. He writes T-O-M in big letters. He is proud of his writing. He smiles and shows his dad.

"Look, dad, I can write on the board!" Tom says.

But his dad is not happy. He is sad and angry. He sees that Tom has written over some of his important notes. He has erased some of his data. He has ruined some of his work.

"Tom, what have you done? You can't write on the board! This is not for writing. This is for my research. You have messed up everything!" His dad says.

Tom is scared and confused. He does not understand why his dad is mad. He does not know what research is. He just wanted to write and show his dad.

"I'm sorry, dad, I didn't know. I just wanted to write like you. I like to write. Please don't be mad at me." Tom says.

His dad sighs and calms down. He sees that Tom did not mean to cause trouble. He sees that Tom is sad and sorry. He hugs Tom and says:

"I'm sorry too, son. I know you like to write. And I'm glad you do. But you have to learn where and when you can write. Some places are not for writing. Some places are for other things. You have to ask before you write on something that is not yours. Do you understand?" His dad says.

Tom nods and says:

"I understand, dad. I'm sorry I wrote on your board. Can I write somewhere else?" Tom says.

His dad smiles and says:

"Of course, son. You can write in your book. Or you can write on this paper. Or you can write on the wall in your room. Just not on the board in the lab. OK?" His dad says.

Tom says:

"OK, dad. Thank you. I love you." Tom says.

His dad says:

"I love you too, son. And I love your writing. You are a good writer. Keep writing, but be careful." His dad says.

They hug and go home. Tom writes a new story in his book. He writes about his dad and the lab and the board. He writes that he learned a lesson. He writes that he is happy.

Tom and Sue were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see the birds.

"Can we climb the tree, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Be careful, children. The tree is very high and the branches are thin. You might fall and hurt yourself," Mom said.

Tom and Sue nodded. They held each other's hands and started to climb. They saw a nest with three eggs. They saw a squirrel with a nut. They saw a hat on a branch.

"Look, a hat!" Sue said. "Who left it here?"

"Maybe it belongs to a giant," Tom said. "Maybe he will come back and eat us."

Sue was scared. She wanted to go down. But Tom was curious. He reached for the hat. He wanted to see how big it was.

Suddenly, a loud noise came from the hat. It was a snake. It was hiding in the hat. It was angry that Tom touched its home. It hissed and showed its teeth.

Tom and Sue screamed. They let go of the hat and the branch. They fell to the ground. Mom ran to them and hugged them.

"Are you okay, children?" Mom asked.

"We are okay, Mom. But there was a snake in the hat. It was scary," Tom said.

"It was harmless, children. It was a garter snake. It does not bite or poison. It was just scared of you," Mom said.

"But why did it shut in the hat?" Sue asked.

"Maybe it was cold or sleepy. Maybe it liked the hat. Maybe it was its friend," Mom said.

Tom and Sue looked at the hat. The snake was still in it. It peeked out and winked at them.

"Maybe it was harmless, Mom. But we don't want to play with it. We don't like snakes in hats," Tom and Sue said.

They ran to the swings and left the snake and the hat alone. They had enough adventure for one day.

Tim smiled and said, "I made it with your cream. Do you like it?" His dad said, "I do, but you know what? I like your face better without it. Let me help you wash it off."

He took a wet towel and wiped Tim's face gently. The shaving cream came off and Tim's face was clean again. His dad said, "There, now you look like my handsome son again. But you know what? You can still have a mustache if you want. Come here." He lifted Tim up and gave him a big kiss on his cheek. He said, "There, now you have a mustache made of love. And that's the most impressive mustache of all." Tim giggled and hugged his dad. He said, "I love you, dad. And I love your mustache too."

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play with boats. They had many boats of different colors and sizes. They liked to make them sail on the pond in the park.

One day, they decided to perform a show with their boats for their parents. They practiced hard and made their boats do tricks and races. They were very excited and proud of their show.

They invited their parents to come and watch them at the pond. Their parents came and sat on a bench. Lily and Tom started their show. They made their boats go fast and slow, turn and spin, and jump over sticks. Their parents clapped and cheered.

But then, a big dog came running to the pond. He saw the boats and wanted to play with them. He barked and jumped into the water. He splashed and chased the boats. He bit and tore them. He ruined the show.

Lily and Tom were very sad and angry. They cried and shouted at the dog. "Go away, bad dog! You broke our boats! You spoiled our show!" But the dog did not listen. He kept playing with the boats.

Their parents came and tried to get the dog away. But the dog was too strong and fast. He ran away with the boats in his mouth. Lily and Tom were left with no boats and no show. They hugged each other and sobbed. They had a bad ending.

Ben was a baby who liked to crawl. He crawled on the floor, on the sofa, on the rug. He crawled to his toys, to his books, to his mom. He crawled everywhere he could, except for his crib. His crib was too high and too boring. He did not want to crawl in his crib.

One day, Ben saw something interesting on the shelf above his crib. It was a shiny ball that made a funny sound when he shook it. He wanted to play with the ball, but he could not reach it. He tried to stand up, but he fell down. He tried to jump, but he was too small. He tried to climb, but he slipped. He was sad and mad. He cried and cried.

Mom heard Ben crying and came to his room. She saw him on the floor, looking at the ball. She picked him up and hugged him. She said, "What's wrong, Ben? Why are you crying?"

Ben pointed at the ball and said, "Ball! Ball! Want ball!"

Mom smiled and said, "Oh, you want the ball? It's a nice ball, but it's not for babies. It's too hard and too loud. It might hurt you or scare you. I have a better ball for you. A soft ball that is colorful and squeaky. Do you want to see it?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes! Yes! Ball!"

Mom took him to his crib and showed him the soft ball. She put it in his crib and said, "Here you go, Ben. This is your ball. You can crawl in your crib and play with it. It's fun and safe. Do you like it?"

Ben looked at the soft ball and smiled. He touched it and heard it squeak. He liked the sound. He threw it and saw it bounce. He liked the movement. He crawled in his crib and chased it. He liked the game. He laughed and laughed.

Mom watched him and said, "I'm glad you like your ball, Ben. You are a good crawler and a good player. Now, it's time for a nap. You must be tired after all that crawling. Do you want to sleep with your ball?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes! Yes! Ball!"

Mom tucked him in and gave him a kiss. She said, "Good night, Ben. Sweet dreams. I love you."

Ben hugged his ball and said, "Love you, Mom. Love ball."

He closed his eyes and fell asleep. He had a happy dream about his ball. He was a happy baby.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play soccer. They had a big trophy that they won at a soccer game. They put the trophy on a shelf in their room and looked at it every day.

One day, Ben and Lily were playing soccer in the backyard. They kicked the ball very hard and had fun. But then, the ball flew over the fence and hit the window of their room. They heard a loud crash and ran to see what happened.

"Oh no!" Ben said. "The trophy is broken!"

They saw the trophy on the floor, with a big crack and a piece missing. The window was also broken, with thick glass everywhere.

"What do we do?" Lily asked. "Mom and Dad will be mad!"

Ben thought for a moment. He had an idea.

"Let's replace the trophy with something else!" he said. "Maybe they won't notice!"

He looked around the room and saw a stuffed bear on his bed. He grabbed the bear and put it on the shelf where the trophy was.

"There!" he said. "Now it looks like we have a bear trophy!"

Lily looked at the bear and shook her head.

"Ben, that's silly!" she said. "A bear is not a trophy! Mom and Dad will know!"

Ben shrugged.

"Well, it's better than nothing!" he said. "Maybe they will think it's cute!"

They heard the door open and their parents come home. They ran downstairs to greet them, hoping they wouldn't go to their room. But they were not so lucky.

"Hey, kids, we have a surprise for you!" their mom said. "We bought you a new soccer ball!"

"Wow, thanks, Mom and Dad!" Ben and Lily said.

They took the ball and went to the backyard. They were happy to have a new ball, but they were also nervous about the trophy.

"Maybe we should tell them the truth," Lily whispered to Ben.

"Maybe later," Ben whispered back.

They played with the ball, but they also looked at the window, wondering when their parents would find out. They hoped they wouldn't be too angry. They hoped they would understand. They hoped they would still love them.

One day, Sara and Ben go to the town with their mom. They see a lot of shops, cars, people and animals. They also see a cute toy store. It has many dolls, cars, trains, puzzles and books. Sara and Ben want to go inside and look.

"Sure, but we don't have much time. You can look, but you can't buy anything today," Mom says.

Then they see something else. They see a shelf with small boxes. Each box has a picture of a different thing. There are boxes with animals, fruits, flowers, letters and numbers. Sara and Ben are curious. They pick up a box and open it. Inside, there are many tiny things that match the picture. They are like miniatures of the real things.

"Wow, look at these!" Sara says.

"They are so cute and small!" Ben says.

They open more boxes and see more things. They see a tiny elephant, a tiny apple, a tiny rose, a tiny A and a tiny 1. They are amazed.

"Mom, look at these!" Sara and Ben call.

Mom comes and sees the boxes. She smiles.

"Those are collectibles. They are things you can collect and keep. They are very cute, but they are also very expensive. You can't have them today," Mom says.

Sara and Ben are sad. They like the collectibles. They want to have them.

"Can we have them another day?" Sara asks.

"Maybe, if you save your money and behave well. But you have to be careful with them. They are very small and fragile. You can lose them or break them easily," Mom says.

Sara and Ben understand. They put the boxes back on the shelf. They say goodbye to the toy store and the collectibles. They hope they can have them someday. They think they would make a great addition to their collections.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing and run. But then they saw a big dog coming towards them. The dog was barking and growling. Tom and Lily were frightened.

"Mom, mom, help!" they cried. "The dog is scary!"

Mom heard them and hurried to them. She picked them up and hugged them.

"Don't worry, my loves. The dog won't hurt you. He is just playing too. See, his owner is calling him. He is a good dog."

She pointed to a man who was waving and whistling. The dog ran back to him and licked his face.

"Sorry, he got away from me. He is very friendly, but he likes to chase things. He didn't mean to scare you," the man said.

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay. We understand. He is a beautiful dog. What is his name?"

"His name is Zipper. He is very fast and he has a zipper on his chest. See?" the man said. He showed them the white stripe on the dog's fur.

Tom and Lily looked at Zipper. He wagged his tail and sniffed them. They saw that he was not scary. He was just curious.

"Hi, Zipper. You are a nice dog. Can we pet you?" Tom asked.

"Sure, he loves that. He is very gentle," the man said.

Tom and Lily petted Zipper. He licked their hands and nuzzled their faces. They giggled and smiled.

"Zipper, you are a good dog. We are not frightened of you anymore. We want to be your friends," Lily said.

Zipper barked and wagged his tail. He was happy too. He had made new friends.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a pair of scissors in the drawer. They do not know what scissors are for. They think they are fun.

"Look, Kim, I can cut this paper with scissors!" Tim says. He makes a snip-snip sound.

"Wow, Tim, that is cool! Let me try!" Kim says. She takes the scissors and cuts another paper.

They cut many papers with scissors. They make shapes and animals. They are happy.

But then, Mom comes in. She sees the papers and the scissors. She is angry.

"Tim and Kim, what are you doing? You should not play with scissors! Scissors are sharp and dangerous! You can hurt yourself or others!" Mom says.

"Sorry, Mom, we did not know. We just wanted to have fun," Tim and Kim say.

Mom sighs. She takes the scissors and puts them away. She hugs Tim and Kim.

"I know you did not know, but you should always ask before you use unknown things. Unknown things can be good or bad. You should be careful and curious. Do you understand?" Mom says.

"Yes, Mom, we understand. We will ask next time. We love you, Mom," Tim and Kim say.

Mom smiles. She loves them too. She gives them some crayons and paper. They can draw with them. They are safe and creative.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to be careful and curious, and to ask before using unknown things. It also shows the importance of listening to parents and apologizing for mistakes.

"No, Tom, it is my car. You have your own cars. Go away," Sam said.

It honked and braked, but it was too late. It hit Tom and the car. Tom and the car flew in the air and landed on the ground.

Sam heard the noise and ran outside. He saw Tom and the car. They were broken and bloody. He screamed and cried. He ran to Tom and the car. He tried to rub them and make them better. But they did not move. They did not talk. They were gone. Sam was alone. He wished he had shared his car with Tom. He wished he had been nice to Tom. He wished he had not been greedy. But it was too late. He had lost his brother and his car. He had nothing. He was very sorry.

Tom and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with toys and run in the park. One day, they found a gun in a trash can. It was big and shiny and had a red button.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "It looks like a space gun. Let's play with it."

Sam was scared. He knew guns were bad and dangerous. He did not want to touch it. He said, "No, Tom, we should not play with it. It is not a toy. It can hurt us or someone else. We should tell a grown-up."

Tom did not listen. He wanted to have fun. He said, "Don't be a baby, Sam. It is just a game. I will be the hero and you will be the villain. I will match you with my gun and save the world."

He picked up the gun and pointed it at Sam. He pressed the red button. But nothing happened. The gun did not make a sound or a light. It was broken.

Tom was angry. He threw the gun on the ground. He said, "This gun is stupid. It does not work. It is no fun at all."

Sam was relieved. He was glad the gun did not work. He said, "Tom, you were wrong. You should not play with guns. They are not for games. They are for grown-ups who know how to use them. You could have hurt yourself or me or someone else. You should be ashamed."

Tom felt bad. He realized he made a mistake. He said, "You are right, Sam. I am sorry. I was silly and foolish. I should not have played with the gun. I should have listened to you. I am ashamed."

He hugged Sam and said, "You are a good friend, Sam. You are smart and brave. Will you forgive me?"

Sam hugged Tom and said, "Of course, I forgive you, Tom. You are a good friend, too. You are kind and sorry. Let's go and find a grown-up and tell them about the gun. Maybe they can take it away and make it safe."

They held hands and walked away from the trash can. They left the gun behind. They never played with guns again. They learned a lesson. They were happy.

"Come on, Lily, let's go to the west!" he said.

"Let's go look at the van," Tim said to Lily. "Maybe they have some fun things for us."

"Who are you?" he asks the snake.

"I'm a scale," says the snake. "I'm here to weigh you and tell you how big you are."

The lion is curious and stops chasing the other animals. He wants to know how big he is.

"Really?" he says. "How do you weigh me?"

"Easy," says the snake. "You just have to stand still and let me squeeze you. The tighter I squeeze, the bigger you are."

The lion agrees and stands still. The snake squeezes him harder and harder, making him feel uncomfortable.

"Ouch!" says the lion. "That hurts! How big am I?"

"You are very big," says the snake. "You are the biggest animal in the world!"

The lion is happy and proud. He thinks he is the best.

"Wow!" he says. "I'm the biggest animal in the world! Thank you, scale!"

The snake smiles and lets go of the lion's tail. He realizes that he has tricked the lion and saved the other animals.

"You're welcome," he says. "But you're not a scale. You're a snake!"

The lion is surprised and angry. He looks at the snake and sees his fangs and his tongue.

"What?" he says. "You're a snake? You lied to me! You're not a scale! You're a sneaky snake!"

The snake laughs and slithers away. He joins the zebra and the giraffe, who are happy and grateful.

"Thank you, snake!" they say. "You're very clever! You fooled the lion and saved us!"

The lion is sad and ashamed. He realizes that he has been fooled and that he is not the biggest animal in the world. He walks away, feeling silly and small.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She was brave and adventurous. One day Anna was walking in the woods and she stumbled over a big black boot. Anna was curious and decided to pick it up. She carefully pulled the boot out of the mud. 

Anna said: "What's this?"

Suddenly, a voice answered her: "It's my boot! I was looking for it everywhere."

Anna looked around and saw an old man. He was smiling. Anna asked: "What were you doing with your boot?"

The old man replied: "Well, I was on an adventure in the woods and I stumbled, so I lost my boot! I'm glad you found it. Thank you!"
 
Anna smiled and gave the boot back to the old man. She said: "You're welcome! Now be careful next time you go on an adventure!" 

The old man thanked her again and continued his journey. Anna watched him go and then continued on her own adventure.

The fox said, "I finished all of the tomatoes. I'm so hungry!"

"Oh no!" said the bunny.

The bunny felt very sorry for his friend so he said, "Wait here. I'll find you some more tomatoes!"

He hopped away and started searching the garden. He searched and searched, but he couldn't find any tomatoes. The bunny looked everywhere, but it was too late.

The fox got very mad. He shouted, "You careless bunny! I'm still hungry!" Then, he trotted away, leaving the bunny all alone.

The bunny felt sad. He had been trying to help but his carelessness had caused his friend to be angry. 

The bunny learned a valuable lesson about being careful. He knew that mistake would never happen again.

Lily looked at Ben and saw that he was sincere. She said, "Ben, I forgive you. But you have to promise me that you will not break my models again. And you have to help me fix them. They are very cold now. They need some love and care."

Ben nodded and said, "I promise, Lily. I will help you fix your models. And I will play nicely with them. And I will also play with your blocks and make some models with you. Maybe we can make a car and a train model together."

Sam does not like to lose. He does not yield. He pushes his truck harder. He wants to pass Ben's car. He uses all his muscle. But he pushes too hard. His truck bumps into Ben's car. Both toys fly off the track and crash into the wall.

"Hey, watch out!" Ben cries. "You broke my car!"

Sam looks at Ben's car. It has a dent and a scratch. He feels sorry. He looks at his truck. It is fine. He knows he was wrong.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Sam says. "I did not mean to break your car. I was just trying to win."

Ben is angry, but he loves his brother. He knows Sam is sorry. He says, "It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. But next time, you have to yield when I say so. And don't push so hard. You could hurt yourself or me."

Sam nods. He says, "I promise, Ben. I will be more careful. And I will yield when you say so. Can we still be friends?"

Ben smiles. He says, "Of course we can. You are my brother. And you have a rare truck. It is very cool. Can I try it?"

Sam smiles too. He says, "Sure, you can. And I can try your car. Maybe we can fix it together."

They hug and swap their toys. They start a new race. They play nicely and have fun. They are happy.

Mom and Dad heard their cries. They ran to the tent. They saw the clown on the floor. They saw Lila and Sam crying.

"The clown, the clown, he fell down," Lila and Sam said. They pointed to the clown.

The clown was not a real clown. He was a bad man. He had a knife. He wanted to hurt the children. He wanted to take their money. He was not funny. He was mean.

But he was not smart. He did not see the knife in the box. He did not know it was sharp. He did not know it would cut him. He did not know it would kill him.

He was not fine. He was dead.

They took them away from the tent. They took them away from the festival. They took them home.

One day, the snake said to the bird, "Can I see your eggs? They look so cool and shiny. I want to touch them and feel them."

The bird said, "No, you cannot see my eggs. They are mine and I love them. You might hurt them or take them away. You are a snake and snakes are bad."

The snake said, "No, I am not bad. I am your friend. You can trust me. I will not hurt your eggs or take them away. I just want to see them for a little while. Please, let me see your eggs."

The bird thought for a moment. She wanted to be a good friend and she liked the snake. She said, "Okay, you can see my eggs. But you have to be very careful and gentle. And you have to give them back to me soon."

The snake said, "Thank you, thank you. You are a very good friend. I will be very careful and gentle. And I will give them back to you soon."

The bird flew away to find some food. The snake climbed up to the nest and saw the eggs. They were so cool and shiny. He wanted to touch them and feel them. He reached out his head and opened his mouth. He bit one of the eggs and swallowed it. He bit another egg and swallowed it. He bit the last egg and swallowed it. He felt very full and happy.

The bird came back and saw the nest. There were no eggs. She saw the snake with a big belly. She said, "Where are my eggs? What did you do to my eggs?"

The snake said, "I ate your eggs. They were so cool and shiny. And they were so tasty and yummy. I could not resist. I am sorry, but I am a snake and snakes are bad."

She flew away and never talked to the snake again. The snake felt sorry, but he could not change what he had done. He learned that trust is very important and that he should not be greedy and selfish.

The moral of the story is: Do not lie to your friends and do not take what is not yours. Trust is very precious and hard to earn, but easy to lose. Be honest and kind to your friends and they will be honest and kind to you.

One day, they decided to play hide and seek again. Anna was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Anna counted to ten and then went to look for Ben. She looked under the bed, behind the curtains, in the closet, but she could not find him. She wondered where he was.

She remembered the wardrobe and thought he might be there. She opened the door and saw a light at the end of the wardrobe. She was curious and walked towards the light. She saw that the light came from a window in another room. She had never seen this room before. It was full of toys and books and animals. She was amazed and excited.

She heard a voice behind her. It was Ben. He had followed her into the wardrobe and found the secret room too. He said, "Anna, look at this! It's like a magic place! We can play here all day!"

This is my old room from when I was a child. You are not supposed to be here. Come out right now!"

Anna and Ben heard their mother's voice and felt scared. They knew they were in trouble. They dropped their toys and books and animals and ran towards the wardrobe door. They said, "Sorry, Mommy, we didn't know. We were just playing hide and seek. Please don't be mad at us."

Their mother sighed and said, "I'm not mad at you. I'm just worried about you. This room is not safe for you. It has many things that can hurt you or break. You have to promise me that you will never come here again. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "We understand, Mommy. We promise. We won't come here again."

Anna and Ben said, "OK, Mommy. We love you."

And that the bird found a cozy spot in one of the coats. And that the bird was happy and free in its secret place.

Jake said, "Yes, Mom, but I was just curious. I wanted to see what she writes."

Mom said, "Jake, that is not okay. Lily's journal is her private property. You have to respect her privacy and her feelings. You have to give it back to her and say sorry."

Jake said, "But Mom, it is just a journal. It is not a big deal."

Mom said, "It is a big deal to Lily. She writes in her journal to express herself and to have fun. She has the right to protect her journal from anyone who wants to read it without her permission. How would you feel if someone took your video game or your comic book and looked at it without asking you?"

Jake thought for a moment. He realized that he would not like that. He said, "I guess I would feel mad and sad."

Mom said, "Exactly. So, you have to apologize to Lily and give her back her journal. And you have to promise not to do it again."

Jake said, "Okay, Mom. I am sorry, Lily. Here is your journal. I will not take it again. I will not read it. I will respect your privacy."

Lily said, "Thank you, Jake. I forgive you. But you have to promise me something too."

Jake said, "What is it?"

Lily said, "You have to promise to protect my journal from anyone else who wants to read it. You have to be my big brother and help me keep it safe."

Jake said, "Okay, Lily. I promise. I will protect your journal. I will be your big brother and help you keep it safe."

Lily smiled and hugged Jake. She said, "Thank you, Jake. You are a good big brother. I love you."

Jake smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are a good little sister. I love you too."

The old lady said, "Would you like some help counting? I can show you how to count the knot properly."

When she was done, the old lady gave her a special smile and said, "That was very good counting. You are very clever!"

Bob flew up and down and round the flower, buzzing with delight. He was so happy and he started collecting some of the petal that had fallen off. He rolled them around in his beeswax, so that he had his own little ball of petals, as yellow as gold.

Bob flew away and soon returned with a drop of oil, he placed it on the petals and said: "There you go".

The flower smiled and said: "Thank you, Bob you're a real hero. Now I can bloom even more and spread the yummy smell everywhere!"

Once upon a time, there was a painter. He was rushing around his house, getting ready for his next job. All of a sudden, he noticed that he was running out of paint! He quickly grabbed his paintbrush and rushed to the store.

When he got there, he saw that the shelves were almost empty, but he did manage to find one can of thick paint. He smiled, grabbed it, and rushed back to his house. 

When he got back, he opened the can of paint. But when he started to dip the brush in, he noticed that the paint was too thick. He tried to stir it but it wouldn't budge. 

"Oh no!" he said. "What should I do?! How can I make this paint thinner?" 

Just then, his house's dog, Spot, came limping in.

"Ah ha!" said the painter. "Spot, come here! I have a job for you!"

Spot happily rushed over and the painter grabbed some water and poured it in the can. As Spot stirred the water and paint together, the painter smiled. 

It worked! In no time, the painter had just the right amount of thick paint to finish his job. 

The painter gave Spot a big hug and the happy duo went back to work. And they all lived happily ever after!

His mom wasn't mad, but she knew Benny needed to learn to be more careful. "Let's clean this up together," she said.

Benny helped his mom clean up the broken pieces and they talked about how to be more careful in the future. Benny learned his lesson and promised to be more careful. From that day on, he was more mindful of his actions and never knocked anything over again. The end.

Lily looked around and saw a big, scary wolf coming towards them. She tried to run away, but the wolf was too fast. The wolf ate Lily and her friend, the bird. It was a very sad ending. But we can still admire Lily's bravery for trying to protect her friend.

He wanted to remember this special day, so he asked Lily to help him print a picture of them together. They had a great time making the picture and Fin was so happy to have a special memory of his adventure.

One day, Lily saw a chicken in the yard. It was brown and fluffy and had a red thing on its head. Lily wanted to play with the chicken. She skipped to the chicken and said, "Hello, chicken. Do you want to skip with me?"

The chicken did not want to skip with Lily. It clucked and ran away. Lily followed the chicken. She skipped faster and faster. She did not see the fence in front of her. She skipped right into the fence and fell down. She hurt her knee and cried.

Mom heard Lily cry and came to the yard. She saw Lily on the ground and the chicken on the other side of the fence. She picked up Lily and hugged her. She said, "Oh, Lily, you should not chase the chicken. The chicken is scared of you. You are too big and loud for the chicken. The chicken likes to peck and scratch, not to skip."

Lily sniffed and said, "But I like to skip. Skipping is fun and easy."

Mom smiled and said, "I know, Lily. Skipping is fun and easy for you. But not for everyone. Some animals like to do different things. And that's okay. You can skip with your friends, or with me, or by yourself. But you should leave the chicken alone. The chicken is happy in its own way."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. I'm sorry, chicken. I won't bother you anymore."

Mom kissed Lily's knee and said, "That's good, Lily. Now let's go inside and get a band-aid. And maybe a cookie."

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. Can I skip to the house?"

Mom laughed and said, "Sure, Lily. You can skip to the house. But be careful of the fence."

Lily said, "I will, Mom. I will." And she skipped to the house with Mom.

But the tree was strong and it didn't fall. The animals were very happy and they thanked the tree for doing such a good job. From that day on, the tree became even taller and stronger because it knew it had an important job to do.

But the man was not a nice man. He took Timmy away from his mom and sailed far away. Timmy was scared and cried for his mom. The man did not care and kept sailing. 

Eventually, Timmy's mom found the boat and rescued him. Timmy learned a valuable lesson to never follow strangers, even if they promise gifts or show shiny anchors.

As he was hopping, Benny saw a big carrot and he wanted to eat it. But the carrot was on the other side of a big river. Benny didn't know how to cross the river, so he asked his friend, a wise old owl, for help. The owl told Benny to follow the sound of the river and he would find a bridge.

Benny followed the sound of the river and soon he found the bridge. He was so happy and he crossed the bridge to get the carrot. But when he bit into the carrot, it was bitter and he didn't like it at all. Benny realized that he should have listened to his mom and stayed close to home where he knew the carrots were sweet.

The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents and not to follow things blindly, because they might not be as good as they seem.

And Maria knew this was true.

"Yes dear," her mom said with a warm smile. "Be gentle with it."

The little girl was so excited she didn't hear her mom's warning. She picked up the book, flipping through the pages as quickly as she could. Nothing looked very interesting, though - just plain words, neither inviting nor magical. 

But then, the little girl noticed a small key tucked in between the pages. It glowed a soft yellow and felt gentle in her hands. She quickly put the key in her pocket and continued to look through the book.

Suddenly there was a loud noise, like a roar. The little girl jumped back in fright. The roar got louder and louder until it filled the room.

The little girl had accidentally released an evil spirit from the book. She noticed a dark figure with a large red coat and yellow eyes. It was angry that the little girl had taken the key. It waved its arms menacingly, and the little girl ran away as fast as she could.

The little girl was never heard from again. In the end, she had to pay the price for examining the gentle book without being careful.

Suddenly, the bird stopped and opened its mouth. It took a deep breath and with all its might, it filled its lungs and screeched at Max.

"What was that?!" Max asked.

Max realized the bird had warned him of the storm, and it had been perfect. From then on, Max always paid attention to the birds in the sky, for they were his perfect guides!

But Lily still did not answer. She did not laugh. She did not come out. Tom got worried. He opened the box. He saw Lily. She was not joking. She was not laughing. She was not breathing. She was hurt by the stick. She was gone.

Tom was sad. He was scared. He was sorry. He did not mean to hurt Lily. He did not know the box had a hole. He did not know the stick was sharp. He did not know his joke was bad. He did not know it was the last time to joke.

Mia and Leo were playing hide and seek in the park. Mia was the seeker and Leo was the hider. Mia counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around and saw a big tree with many leaves. She thought Leo might be hiding behind the tree. She ran to the tree and shouted, "I found you!"

But when she reached the tree, she did not see Leo. She only saw a pretty bird with blue and yellow feathers. The bird was sitting on a branch and singing a song. Mia was surprised and smiled. She liked the bird. She said, "Hello, bird. You are very pretty. What is your name?"

The bird stopped singing and looked at Mia. It said, "My name is Coco. I am not Leo. Leo is hiding somewhere else. He told me to reveal his hiding spot if you give me a seed."

Mia was amazed. She did not know that birds could talk. She wanted to find Leo, but she also wanted to talk to Coco. She said, "Where can I find a seed?"

Coco said, "There is a bag of seeds on the bench. Leo left it there. He likes to feed me and my friends. He is very kind. But he is also very sneaky. He likes to hide in tricky places."

Mia ran to the bench and grabbed the bag of seeds. She opened it and took out a seed. She ran back to the tree and gave the seed to Coco. Coco took the seed and ate it. He said, "Thank you, Mia. You are very nice. Now I will tell you where Leo is. He is hiding under the slide. He thinks you will not look there. But you are very smart. You will find him."

Mia thanked Coco and ran to the slide. She looked under it and saw Leo. He was lying on the ground and holding his breath. He did not see Mia. Mia said, "I found you, Leo! You are a good hider, but Coco is a better revealer. He told me where you are."

Leo jumped up and gasped. He saw Mia and Coco. He said, "Oh, no! Coco, you betrayed me! How could you?"

Coco said, "I did not betray you, Leo. I made a deal with Mia. She gave me a seed and I gave her a clue. It was fair and fun. You should not be mad. You should be happy. You have a good friend and a good game."

Leo looked at Mia and Coco. He felt a little sad and a little happy. He said, "You are right, Coco. You are a clever bird and a good friend. And Mia, you are a great seeker and a good friend. I am sorry I was mad. Can we play again?"

Mia and Coco smiled and nodded. They said, "Yes, we can play again. But first, let us listen to Coco's song. He has a pretty voice and a good lecture. He can teach us many things about birds and parks and games."

Lily was scared. She screamed and held Anna tight. She hoped the dog would go away. She hoped her mom would come back. She hoped Anna's hair would be safe. She wished she had not filled it with so many things. She wished she had left it soft and simple.

"Hey, stop that!" Ben shouted. "You are hurting the fish!"

The mean boy did not listen. He sprayed more water at the fish. The fish were scared and hid under the water.

Lily was brave. She ran to the mean boy and grabbed his water gun. She sprayed him with water in the face.

"Ow! That hurts!" the mean boy cried. He dropped the water gun and ran away.

Lily and Ben cheered. They picked up the water gun and threw it in the trash. They went back to the pond and fed the fish some more bread.

"Good job, Lily. You are very brave," Ben said.

"Thank you, Ben. You are very kind," Lily said.

Mom hugged them both. She was proud of them. She said they were good friends to the fish.

One day, Lily got a new train that was shiny and black. It ran on coal, not batteries. Lily was very happy and showed it to Ben. Ben was jealous. He wanted a coal train too. He said to Lily, "Your train is not good. It is dirty and noisy. My trains are better. They are clean and quiet."

Lily was hurt by Ben's words. She said, "My train is good. It is not dirty and noisy. It is special and fun. You are not nice. You are mean."

They stopped playing and turned away from each other. They were both sad and angry.

The next day, they saw a big train at the park. It was a real train that ran on coal. It was shiny and black, like Lily's toy train. It had a whistle and a smokestack. It was very exciting.

Lily and Ben ran to see the train. They wanted to ride it. But there was a problem. The train only had one ticket left. The ticket seller said, "Who wants the last ticket? You have to decide quickly."

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They both wanted the ticket. But they also remembered their fight. They felt sorry for being mean to each other. They missed being friends.

Lily said to Ben, "You can have the ticket. I know you like coal trains. I'm sorry for being rude to you. You are my friend."

Ben said to Lily, "No, you can have the ticket. I know you like coal trains too. I'm sorry for being jealous of you. You are my friend."

The ticket seller smiled. He said, "You are both very kind and generous. You have succeeded in being good friends. You can both ride the train. I have another ticket for you."

Lily and Ben hugged each other. They were very happy. They thanked the ticket seller and boarded the train. They had a wonderful time together.

The moral of the story is: Don't be jealous of what others have. Be happy with what you have. And always be nice to your friends.

They put their dough animals on a tray and went to show their mom. Mom was busy making bread in the oven. She smiled and said, "Wow, you made such nice dough animals. But you have to be careful. Don't put them too close to the oven. They might get hot and melt."

Sara and Ben nodded and went back to the kitchen. They saw a marker on the table. Sara had an idea. She said, "Let's mark our dough animals. We can draw eyes and noses and mouths on them. Then they will look more real." Ben agreed and said, "That sounds fun. Let's do it."

They took the marker and started to mark their dough animals. They drew eyes and noses and mouths on the bear and the snake. They also drew spots and stripes and patterns on them. They were very happy with their work. They said, "Look, our dough animals are so pretty. They have faces and colors. They are our friends."

But then they heard a loud beep. It was the oven. Mom said, "The bread is ready. I have to take it out. Can you help me, Sara and Ben?" Sara and Ben ran to help their mom. They forgot about their dough animals on the tray. They left them on the table, near the oven.

The oven was very hot. The heat reached the tray. The dough animals started to feel warm. They started to melt. Their eyes and noses and mouths started to fade. Their spots and stripes and patterns started to blur. They looked very sad. They said, "Oh no, we are melting. We are poor dough animals. We were so happy. Now we are gone."

The end.

Tom and Lily liked to fish with their dad. They had a big pond near their house, where they could catch many fish. They each had a pole, a hook, and a worm. They were happy and careful when they fished.

One day, a nosy duck came to the pond. It saw the worms on the hooks and wanted to eat them. It swam close to Tom and Lily and tried to grab their worms. Tom and Lily shouted at the duck and waved their poles. "Go away, duck! These are our worms! You have your own food!"

But the duck did not listen. It was greedy and sneaky. It waited until Tom and Lily looked away, and then it snatched Tom's worm with its beak. Tom felt a tug on his pole and thought he had a fish. He pulled hard, but the duck pulled harder. The duck flew away with Tom's worm and his hook. Tom was sad and angry. He had lost his hook and his worm.

Lily felt sorry for Tom. She decided to share her worm with him. She cut it in half and gave one half to Tom. She said, "Here, Tom. You can have half of my worm. We can still fish together. Maybe we can catch a big fish and share it too."

Tom smiled and thanked Lily. He was glad to have a kind sister. He put the half worm on his hook and cast his pole again. He said, "You are very nice, Lily. Thank you for sharing with me. I will share with you too. And I will be more careful with my pole and my hook. I don't want to lose them again."

The duck watched them from a distance. It felt ashamed of what it had done. It realized that it had been rude and selfish. It wished it had not taken Tom's worm and hook. It learned a lesson. It decided to leave Tom and Lily alone and to find its own food.

The moral of the story is: Don't be nosy and greedy. Be kind and share.

"Bee can hurt you. Bee has a sharp thing on its back. It can make you cry," Lily said.

"I don't care. I want to see the bee. It is pretty and makes a nice sound," Tom said. He moved his hand closer to the flower.

"Tom, stop! Listen to me!" Lily said. She was scared for Tom.

But Tom did not listen. He touched the bee. The bee did not like that. The bee used its sharp thing on Tom's hand. Tom felt a big pain. He screamed and let go of the bee. He looked at his hand. It was red and swollen. He cried and cried.

Lily ran to Tom and hugged him. She was sorry for Tom. She wanted to help him. She said, "Tom, I told you not to touch the bee. Now you are hurt. We have to go home and tell mom. She can make you feel better."

But Tom was angry and sad. He did not want to go home. He did not want to talk to Lily. He said, "Go away, Lily. You are not my friend. You made the bee hurt me. I don't like you. I miss the bee. The bee was my friend."

Lily was shocked and hurt. She did not make the bee hurt Tom. She tried to warn him. She loved Tom. She was his sister. She said, "Tom, don't say that. I am your friend. I love you. The bee was not your friend. The bee was scared of you. You made the bee angry. You have to be careful with bees. They are not toys."

He did not see the other bees. The other bees were angry too. They saw Tom hurt their friend. They wanted to hurt Tom back. They flew to Tom and used their sharp things on him. Tom felt more pain. He screamed and screamed.

Lily saw what happened. She was terrified. She wanted to help Tom. She wanted to make the bees go away. But she was too late. The bees were too many. They covered Tom with their sharp things. Tom stopped screaming. He stopped moving. He stopped breathing.

Lily cried and cried. She missed Tom. She missed her brother. She missed her friend. She wished she could go back in time. She wished Tom had listened to her. She wished the bee had not hurt him. She wished the other bees had not killed him. She wished she could hug him and say sorry. She wished he could hug her and say he loved her. But she could not. Tom was gone. And Lily was alone.

"Look, Ben, I found a crab!" Lila said, holding a stick. She saw a small red crab hiding under a rock.

"Can I see?" Ben asked, curious. He ran over to Lila and looked at the crab.

"Be careful, it might pinch you!" Lila warned. She poked the crab gently with her stick. The crab moved its claws and eyes.

"Wow, it's so funny!" Ben said, laughing. He wanted to poke the crab too. He took another stick and poked the crab from the other side.

The crab did not like being poked. It was scared and angry. It snapped its claws at the sticks and made a clicking sound.

"Ouch!" Lila and Ben said at the same time. They dropped their sticks and backed away. The crab crawled out from under the rock and ran to the water.

"Sorry, crab, we didn't mean to hurt you!" Lila and Ben said, feeling sorry. They watched the crab disappear into the waves.

"Let's find something else to poke," Ben said, looking around.

"OK, but be nice," Lila said, picking up her stick.

They went back to playing on the beach, poking sand and shells and having fun.

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. Sara found a big spoon and a small spoon. She gave the small spoon to Ben and said, "Here, you can stir the soup with this."

Ben took the small spoon and looked at the pot on the stove. It was full of water and some green things. He did not know what they were, but they smelled funny. He stirred the water and the green things with the spoon. He wondered if it would taste good.

Sara saw a red apron hanging on the wall. She wanted to wear it and look like a real chef. She reached for the apron, but it was too high for her. She jumped and stretched, but she could not get it. She said, "Ben, help me get the apron. It is too high for me."

Ben stopped stirring the soup and went to help Sara. He was taller than her, but not much. He also jumped and stretched, but he could not get the apron either. He said, "We need something to stand on. Maybe a chair or a stool."

Sara looked around and saw a stool near the table. She ran to get it and brought it to the wall. She put it under the apron and climbed on it. She reached for the apron again, and this time she got it. She was happy and said, "Yay, I got it! Now I can wear it and be a chef."

She put the apron on and tied it around her waist. She looked at Ben and said, "You can wear the hat. It is on the shelf." She pointed to a white hat with a fluffy top. Ben saw the hat and smiled. He went to get it and put it on his head. He said, "Now we look like chefs. Let's taste the soup and see if it is ready."

They went back to the stove and looked at the pot. The water and the green things were boiling and bubbling. Sara took the big spoon and scooped some soup into a bowl. She blew on it to cool it down and said, "Here, you can try it first." She gave the bowl and the big spoon to Ben.

Ben took the bowl and the big spoon and said, "Thank you." He put the spoon in his mouth and tasted the soup. He made a face and spat it out. He said, "Yuck, this is bitter. It is not yummy at all. What are these green things?"

Sara looked at the soup and said, "I don't know. I found them in the fridge. They looked like leaves. Maybe they are salad."

Ben said, "No, they are not salad. They are something else. Something bad. Maybe they are poison."

Sara said, "Oh no, poison. We should not eat them. We should throw them away."

They took the pot and the bowl and ran to the trash can. They dumped the soup and the green things in the trash can. They said, "Bye bye, bitter soup. We don't like you."

They washed the spoons and the pot and the bowl. They took off the apron and the hat and hung them on the wall. They said, "We are sorry, apron and hat. We are not good chefs. We made bad soup. Maybe we can try again another day."

They left the kitchen and went to play something else. They hoped their mom would not be mad at them for making a mess. They also hoped she would not notice the missing green things. They did not know they were parsley, and that mom needed them for dinner.

They sit on the blanket and look at the book. It has pictures of animals and flowers. They think they are pretty.

They hear a noise outside. They peek through the door. They see a man with a beard and a hat. He has a bag and a stick. He is the owner of the hut.

"Hello, children," he says. "What are you doing here?"

Tom and Anna are scared. They run out of the hut and back to the woods. They think the man is angry.

They go home and tell their parents what they saw. Their parents say they should not go to the hut again. They say it is not safe.

Tom and Anna nod. They think they are right. They say they are sorry. They hug their parents and go to bed. They dream of the beautiful hut and the nice things inside. They wonder who the man is and what he does. They think they will never know.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play dress up. They had many clothes and hats and shoes in their big box. One day, they found a shiny bag in the box. It had money inside. Lots and lots of money.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "We are rich!"

"Let's dress up like kings and queens!" Lily said. "We can buy anything we want!"

They put on the fanciest clothes they could find. They wore crowns and jewels and fur. They felt very important and happy.

They decided to go outside and show off their money. They walked down the street, waving and smiling. They saw a shop that sold toys and candy. They wanted to buy everything.

"Hello, can we have all these things?" Tom asked the shopkeeper.

The shopkeeper looked at them and frowned. He saw their money and recognized it. It was not real money. It was play money. He was angry.

"Hey, you can't use this money here!" he shouted. "This is fake money! You are trying to cheat me!"

He grabbed the money from their hands and threw it away. He also took their clothes and hats and shoes. He said they had to pay for them.

"But these are ours!" Lily cried. "We found them in our box!"

The shopkeeper did not believe them. He said they were liars and thieves. He called the police. The police came and took Tom and Lily away. They were scared and sad.

They wished they had never played with the money. They wished they had stayed home and played dress up. They learned a hard lesson. Money is not a toy.

Lily was a very independent girl. She liked to do things by herself, without help from anyone. She liked to dress herself, brush her teeth, and make her own breakfast. She also liked to match her clothes, so they looked nice and colorful.

One morning, she decided to wear her yellow dress, her yellow shoes, and her yellow hat. She thought she looked like a sunflower. She went to the kitchen and saw a jar of honey on the table. She loved honey, and thought it would match her outfit. She opened the jar and poured some honey on her toast. Then she poured some more on her hat. And some more on her dress. And some more on her shoes. She was very happy.

But then her mom came in and saw the mess. She was not happy. She said, "Lily, what have you done? You have ruined your clothes and wasted the honey! Honey is not for matching, honey is for eating. And honey is sticky and messy. You need to take a bath and change your clothes right now!"

Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "But mom, I like honey. And I like matching. I am independent. I can do what I want!"

Mom said, "No, Lily, you are not independent. You are a little girl who needs to listen to her mom. You can match your clothes, but not with honey. And you can eat honey, but not on your clothes. Honey is not a toy, honey is food. Now come with me and let's clean you up."

Lily did not want to go with mom. She wanted to stay with her honey. But mom took her by the hand and led her to the bathroom. Lily cried and said, "I don't like you, mom. You are mean. You don't let me match."

Mom said, "I love you, Lily. But I also need to teach you. Matching is fun, but honey is not for matching. Maybe later we can find something else that matches your yellow dress. Something that is not sticky and messy. Something that is pretty and nice. Would you like that?"

Lily sniffed and said, "Maybe. But I still like honey."

Mom said, "I know, honey. And I like honey too. But honey is for eating, not for matching. Remember that, okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I will remember."

Mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, honey. I forgive you. Now let's get you clean and ready for the day. And maybe we can have some honey on our toast later. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled and said, "That sounds good, mom. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, honey. You are my sunflower."

Lily does not listen. She runs to the table and takes a big bite of the cake. It is sweet and soft. She smiles.

"Come on, Tom, it is so good!" she says.

Tom is scared. He does not want to be bad. But he also wants to try the cake. He walks to the table and takes a small bite. It is good, too.

But then they hear a loud voice.

"Hey, who ate my cake?" the voice says.

Lily and Tom are scared. They run away. They do not feel happy anymore. They feel sorry.

Anna liked to draw with pastels. She had many colors of pastels. She could make pink flowers, blue sky, green grass, and yellow sun. She was happy when she drew.

One day, Anna wanted to draw a big cake. She used brown pastels for the cake, white pastels for the cream, and red pastels for the cherries. She made the cake look very yummy. She was proud of her drawing.

She showed her drawing to her brother Tom. Tom was older than Anna. He liked to tease her. He said, "That is not a cake. That is a pile of mud. It looks disgusting. You are a bad drawer."

Anna felt sad. She did not like what Tom said. She said, "No, it is a cake. It is a nice cake. You are a mean brother."

Tom said, "Prove it. If it is a cake, you can eat it. Go on, eat your pastels. They are delicious."

Anna did not want to eat her pastels. She knew they were not food. She knew they were for drawing. She said, "No, I will not eat them. You eat them. You are silly."

Tom said, "Fine, I will eat them. Watch me." He picked up a brown pastel and put it in his mouth. He bit it hard. He made a face. He spit it out. He said, "Blech! That is disgusting. That is not a cake. That is a pastel. You tricked me."

Anna laughed. She said, "I did not trick you. You tricked yourself. You should not eat pastels. You should learn to be nice. And you should learn to draw better."

Tom felt sorry. He said, "You are right. I am sorry. I was rude. Your drawing is good. Can you teach me how to draw with pastels?"

Anna smiled. She said, "Yes, I can teach you. But first, you have to wash your mouth. And say sorry to my pastels. They are not for eating. They are for making art."

Sara and Ben love to help Mom in the garden. They dig and water and plant seeds. Mom says they are great helpers. They like to see the flowers bloom in the sun. They are red and yellow and pink and blue. They smell nice too.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play hide and seek. One day, they play in the park near their homes. Ben is the seeker. He counts to ten. Mia runs to find a good spot.

She sees a big tree. She runs behind it. She thinks Ben will not see her there. She is hidden. She waits for Ben to find her.

Ben opens his eyes. He looks around. He sees the swings, the slide, the sandbox. He does not see Mia. He walks around the park. He calls her name. "Mia, where are you? I want to find you!"

Mia hears Ben. She smiles. She is good at hiding. She stays quiet. She does not answer.

Ben walks to the gate. He looks at the street. He sees cars, bikes, people. He does not see Mia. He is sad. He thinks Mia is not in the park. He thinks she went home. He says, "Mia, are you there? Please come back!"

Mia hears Ben. She feels sorry. She does not want Ben to be sad. She wants to play with him. She runs out from behind the tree. She waves at Ben. She says, "Ben, I am here! I was hidden behind the tree. You did not see me!"

Ben sees Mia. He is happy. He runs to her. He says, "Mia, I found you! You are very good at hiding. But I am glad you came out. I missed you!"

Mia hugs Ben. She says, "Ben, I missed you too. You are a good seeker. But I had fun hiding. Can we play again?"

Ben nods. He says, "Yes, we can play again. But this time, I will hide and you will seek. OK?"

Mia agrees. She says, "OK, Ben. You hide and I will seek. But do not go to the street. It is not safe. Stay in the park. OK?"

Ben says, "OK, Mia. I will stay in the park. I will not go to the street. I will find a good spot. You count to ten. Ready, set, go!"

Mia covers her eyes. She counts to ten. Ben runs to find a good spot. He sees a bench. He runs behind it. He thinks Mia will not see him there. He is hidden. He waits for Mia to find him.
