Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They saw a big sunflower that was taller than them. They wanted to see how it looked up close.

"Let's crawl to the sunflower," Lily said. "Maybe we can find some bees or butterflies."

"OK," Max agreed. "But be careful, the grass might tickle us."

They crawled on their hands and knees, making funny noises. They pretended they were lions and tigers, hunting for their prey. They reached the sunflower and looked up. It was bright and yellow, with many seeds in the middle.

"Wow, it's so pretty," Lily said. "Can we touch it?"

"Sure, but gently," Max said. "We don't want to hurt it."

They reached out their hands and felt the soft petals and the rough stem. They saw a bee buzzing around the flower, collecting pollen. They heard it make a loud sound.

"Bzzz, bzzz, bzzz," the bee said.

"Hello, bee," Lily said. "What are you doing?"

"I'm making honey," the bee said. "This sunflower has a lot of sweet nectar. Do you want to try some?"

"No, thank you," Max said. "We don't like honey. It's sticky and yucky."

"That's silly," the bee said. "Honey is delicious and good for you. But if you don't want any, that's fine. I have to go now. Bye-bye."

"Bye-bye, bee," Lily and Max said.

They waved to the bee as it flew away. They smiled at each other and hugged the sunflower.

"We like sunflowers," they said. "They are big and beautiful and friendly."

"Yuck, Lily, that beetle is weird! It has too many legs and eyes. Throw it away!" Max said.

Lily felt sad. She liked the beetle. She thought it was special and interesting. She did not want to throw it away.

"No, Max, the beetle is not weird. It is different. Different is good. Different means you can learn new things and have fun. The beetle is my friend. You should not be mean to it." Lily said.

Max thought about what Lily said. He realized he was being rude and unfair. He did not know much about beetles. Maybe they were not so bad. Maybe he could learn something from them.

"Sorry, Lily, you are right. The beetle is different, not weird. Can I see it again? Maybe we can play with it together." Max said.

Lily smiled and handed the beetle to Max. They looked at it closely and gently. They saw how it moved its legs and antennae. They heard how it made a tiny sound. They learned its name was a jewel beetle. They had fun with it.

Lily and Max learned that being different is not weird. It is a good thing. It makes the world more colorful and exciting. They learned to respect and appreciate the beetle and other bugs. They learned to be kind and curious. They found a new friend and a new hobby.

Sam was a lazy boy and did not want to do any work. He said to his mom, "Work is boring. I want to swim. I don't care about the house. It is always dirty anyway." He ran away from his mom and went to the lake. He took the boat and rowed to the middle of the lake. He jumped into the water and laughed.

But Sam did not know that the water was very cold that day. He felt a bitter chill in his body. He shivered and cried. He wanted to go back to the boat, but he could not find it. He had forgotten to tie it to a rock. The boat had drifted away with the wind. He was scared and alone.

Tim heard his brother's cries and ran to the lake. He saw Sam in the water and the boat far away. He was worried and brave. He jumped into the water and swam to his brother. He grabbed his hand and pulled him to the shore. He wrapped him in a warm towel and hugged him.

Sam was sorry and ashamed. He said to Tim, "Thank you for saving me. You are a good brother. I was a bad boy. I did not listen to mom and I did not help with the work. I was selfish and rude. I will never do that again. I will be a good boy like you."

Tim smiled and said, "I forgive you, Sam. I love you, brother. We can swim together, but only after we do our work. Work is not boring. It is important. It makes our mom happy and our house clean. It also makes us strong and smart. Work is good."

Sam nodded and said, "You are right, Tim. Work is good. And so is swim. But swim is better when we do it together." They hugged and went back to their mom. She was proud and happy. She gave them a big kiss and a cookie. They ate the cookie and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best." They lived happily ever after.

Tim and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But their favorite thing was to ride the big red bike.

The big red bike was impressive. It had two seats, two wheels and two pedals. Tim and Lily could ride it together. They felt very fast and strong. They pretended they were going to different places, like the zoo, the beach and the moon.

One day, they met a new boy in the park. His name was Sam. He had a small blue bike. He wanted to play with Tim and Lily. He asked them if he could ride the big red bike with them.

"Sorry, Sam, but this is our bike," Tim said. "We don't share it with anyone. It's too special."

Lily nodded. She agreed with Tim. She didn't want to let Sam ride the big red bike. She thought he might break it or lose it.

Sam felt sad. He said, "But I don't have a friend to ride with. And my bike is not impressive. It's old and small. Can't we be friends and share the bike?"

Tim and Lily looked at each other. They thought about what Sam said. They realized that he was lonely and wanted to have fun. They remembered that they liked to make new friends and try new things. They decided to be nice and let Sam ride the big red bike with them.

"Okay, Sam, you can ride with us," Lily said. "But you have to be careful and follow the rules. And you have to take turns with us."

Sam smiled. He said, "Thank you, Tim and Lily. You are very kind. I will be careful and follow the rules. And I will take turns with you."

They all got on the big red bike. Tim sat in the front, Lily sat in the middle and Sam sat in the back. They started to pedal and steer. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and shouted. They had a wonderful ride.

They learned that riding the big red bike was fun, but sharing it with a new friend was even more fun. They learned that life was better when they were generous and friendly. They learned that impressive things were not as important as impressive feelings.

Sara's mom hears her weep. She comes to see what is wrong. She hugs Sara and asks her why she is weeping. Sara tells her mom about the fight with Ben. Sara's mom says that fighting is not nice. She says that Sara and Ben should say sorry to each other and share the toys.

One day, Ben kicks the ball too hard and it hits Mia's toe. Mia cries and holds her toe. It hurts a lot. Ben runs to her and says he is sorry.

"Are you okay, Mia?" Ben asks.

"No, my toe is hard and red. It feels bad," Mia says.

Ben looks at her toe and sees a bump. He thinks of something that might help. He runs to his backpack and gets a bag of ice. He puts the ice on Mia's toe and says, "This will make your toe feel better. It will make the bump go away."

Mia feels the cold ice on her toe and says, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. The ice helps a little."

Ben smiles and says, "You're welcome, Mia. I hope your toe improves soon. Then we can play soccer again."

Mia smiles back and says, "Me too, Ben. I like playing soccer with you. You are a good player."

They hug and sit on the grass, waiting for Mia's toe to heal. They talk about their favorite soccer players and how they want to improve their skills. They are happy to have each other.

Tom and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw many birds, flowers and dogs. They were happy and had fun.

But then, they saw something new. It was a big, shiny saw. It was on the grass, near a tree. Tom and Mia were curious. They wanted to touch it.

"Look, Mia, a saw!" Tom said. "Let's go and see it!"

"No, Tom, don't!" Mia said. "It can hurt you! It is sharp and dangerous!"

But Tom did not listen. He ran to the saw and picked it up. He felt the blade. It was cold and hard. He tried to cut the tree with it. He pushed and pulled.

"Ow!" Tom cried. He dropped the saw. He had cut his finger. It was bleeding. He felt pain and fear. He ran to Mia and hugged her.

"I'm sorry, Mia, you were right!" Tom said. "The saw is bad! It hurt me!"

"It's okay, Tom, I'm here!" Mia said. "Let me see your finger. We need to put a band-aid on it."

She took out a band-aid from her pocket and wrapped it around Tom's finger. She kissed it gently.

"There, does it feel better?" Mia asked.

"Yes, thank you, Mia!" Tom said. "You are a good friend. You are kind and smart. Can I kiss you too?"

"Sure, Tom, you can!" Mia said. "But only on the cheek!"

They kissed each other on the cheek and smiled. They were still friends. They were tired from playing. They decided to go home and have a nap. They held hands and walked to their moms. They said goodbye to the park and the saw. They did not want to see it again.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the farm with his mom. He liked to see the animals, especially the sheep. They were white and fluffy and made funny sounds. Tom wanted to pet them, but his mom said he had to be careful and gentle.

"Can I feed them, mom?" Tom asked.

"Sure, honey. Here, take this bucket of grass and follow me," his mom said. She led him to a fence where some sheep were grazing. Tom saw one sheep that was different from the others. It was orange, not white.

"Mom, look! An orange sheep!" Tom exclaimed.

His mom smiled and said, "That's not a sheep, Tom. That's a goat. He likes to eat grass too, but he also likes to eat other things, like clothes and shoes. He's very naughty sometimes."

Tom was curious and wanted to see the goat closer. He climbed over the fence and walked towards the orange animal. The goat saw him and ran to him, wagging his tail. Tom thought he wanted to play, so he reached out his hand to touch him. But the goat had other plans. He opened his mouth and bit Tom's sleeve, pulling it hard.

"Ow! Stop it!" Tom cried. He tried to pull his arm away, but the goat was stronger. He tore off a piece of Tom's shirt and chewed it happily.

"Tom, come back here!" his mom shouted. She ran to the fence and helped Tom get away from the goat. She checked his arm and saw that he was not hurt, only scared. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, honey. Are you okay?"

Tom nodded, but he was still upset. He looked at his shirt and saw a big hole in it. He felt ashamed and angry. He said, "I don't like the goat. He's mean and greedy. He ruined my shirt."

His mom said, "I know, honey. But you have to remember, he's not a sheep. He's a goat. He doesn't know any better. He just does what he likes. You have to be careful around him and respect his differences. Not all animals are the same, and not all people are the same. We have to learn to get along with everyone, even if they are not like us."

Tom thought about what his mom said. He realized that he was wrong to judge the goat by his color and to expect him to act like a sheep. He learned that he should not be too curious or too friendly with strangers, and that he should listen to his mom's advice. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I understand. Can we go see the other animals now?"

His mom smiled and said, "Of course, honey. Let's go. But first, let me fix your shirt. I have a needle and thread in my bag. Maybe we can make it look like a patchwork quilt."

Tom laughed and said, "That would be cool. Maybe the goat will like it too."

His mom said, "Maybe he will. But don't let him get too close. He might reveal his appetite again."

The end.

As the whale swam closer, he saw a big ship. The ship was striking the water with its big, strong sail. The whale wanted to play with the ship, but he was scared. He thought the ship might not like him because he was dull and slow.

But the whale was brave. He swam to the ship and said, "Hi, I want to play." The ship saw the whale and said, "Okay, let's play!" They played together, and the whale was very happy. The ship liked the whale even though he was dull and slow. In the end, they became best friends, and the whale learned that it is okay to be different.

From that day on, Penny was never careless again. She always looked where her ball was going when she played. And every time she saw the big tree, she would clap her hands and remember the funny-looking man who helped her.

"I thought he was lost forever, but Mommy helped me search and we found him!" Lily said.

"Oh, that's wonderful! I'm so glad you found your rubber duckie," Grandma said with a smile. "But Lily, did you know that I'm deaf? That means I can't hear very well."

Lily looked confused. "What's deaf?" she asked.

"It means I can't hear things like other people can. But that's okay, because I can still see and feel things, like your big hug for your rubber duckie," Grandma explained.

Lily smiled and gave her grandma a big hug too. She was happy to have her rubber duckie back and to have such a loving family.

"Wow, it is so big and round!" Lila says. She runs to the pumpkin. She wants to touch it.

"Be careful, Lila. It is not ours. It is for a contest." Tom says. He follows her.

Lila and Tom reach the pumpkin. They see a sign. The sign says: "Biggest Pumpkin Contest. Winner gets a prize."

"I wonder what the prize is." Lila says. She puts her hand on the pumpkin. It feels smooth and hard.

"Maybe it is a toy. Or a book. Or a cake." Tom says. He puts his hand on the pumpkin too.

Suddenly, the pumpkin starts to shake. Lila and Tom are scared. They let go of the pumpkin.

"What is happening?" Lila says.

The pumpkin lifts off the table. It flies in the air. It makes a loud noise. It sounds like a rocket.

"Wow, it is flying!" Tom says.

Lila and Tom watch the pumpkin fly. It goes higher and higher. It goes over the tent. It goes over the trees. It goes over the clouds.

"Bye, bye, pumpkin!" Lila and Tom say.

They laugh and clap. They think it is funny and amazing.

The end.

Tim and Sue were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big truck with a picture of ice cream on it. They ran to the truck and asked for ice cream.

"Can we have ice cream, please?" they said to the man in the truck.

"Sure, what kind do you want?" the man said.

Tim and Sue looked at the many flavors of ice cream. They wanted to try them all. They ordered one cone each, but they were not happy. They wanted more.

"Can we have another one, please?" they said to the man.

"Another one? Are you sure?" the man said.

"Yes, please!" Tim and Sue said.

The man gave them another cone each, but they still wanted more. They ordered one more, and then another, and then another. They ate the ice cream very fast, because they were afraid the man would run out.

Soon, they had eaten six cones each. They felt very full and sick. Their stomachs hurt and they could not run or play. They felt very slow and sad.

The man in the truck saw them and shook his head. He said, "You should not eat so much ice cream. It is not good for you. You should eat only a little, and enjoy it. Then you will feel happy and healthy."

Tim and Sue realized they had made a mistake. They said, "We are sorry, sir. You are right. We should not be greedy. We should be thankful for what we have."

They learned their lesson and never ordered so much ice cream again. They also said sorry to their mom and dad, who were worried about them. They promised to eat well and play well. They felt better and happier.

The bad people were crazy. They wanted to hurt everyone. They did not care about the boy or Tom. They only cared about their bomb.

Lena and Tom were friends. They liked to play with dolls and cars. One day, Lena had an idea. She said to Tom, "Let's play marriage. You be the husband and I be the wife. We can wrap this scarf around us and pretend it is a dress."

Tom did not like the idea. He said, "No, I don't want to play marriage. I want to play cars. Cars are fun and fast. Marriage is boring and slow."

But Lena was persistent. She said, "Please, Tom, please. It will be fun. We can have a cake and a party and a kiss. Please, please, please."

Tom did not want to make Lena sad. He said, "Okay, fine. But only for a little while. Then we play cars."

Lena was happy. She wrapped the scarf around them and said, "Now we are married. You have to do what I say. I say we go to the kitchen and get some cake."

Tom did not like cake. He liked cookies. He said, "No, I don't want cake. I want cookies. Cookies are yummy and crunchy. Cake is sticky and mushy."

But Lena was persistent. She said, "No, Tom, no. We have to have cake. Cake is what married people have. You have to do what I say. I say we go to the kitchen and get some cake."

Tom did not want to argue. He said, "Okay, fine. But only a little piece. Then we play cars."

Lena was happy. She dragged Tom to the kitchen and said, "Look, there is a big cake on the table. It is for us. We can have as much as we want."

Tom did not like the cake. He saw that it had nuts and raisins. He hated nuts and raisins. He said, "No, Lena, no. I don't like this cake. It has nuts and raisins. Nuts and raisins are yucky and hard. I want cookies. Cookies are yummy and crunchy."

But Lena was persistent. She said, "No, Tom, no. You have to eat the cake. It is our cake. You have to do what I say. I say you eat the cake."

Tom did not want to eat the cake. He said, "No, Lena, no. I don't want to eat the cake. I want to play cars. Cars are fun and fast. I don't want to play marriage. Marriage is boring and slow."

But Lena was persistent. She said, "No, Tom, no. You have to play marriage. You have to eat the cake. You have to kiss me. You have to do what I say. I say you do it now."

Tom did not want to do any of that. He said, "No, Lena, no. I don't want to do any of that. I want to go home. I don't want to be your friend. I don't want to be your husband. I don't want to be with you."

But Lena was persistent. She said, "No, Tom, no. You can't go home. You can't leave me. You are my friend. You are my husband. You are mine."

Tom was scared. He tried to run away. But Lena was faster. She grabbed him and pulled him back. She wrapped the scarf around them and said, "You are mine. You are mine. You are mine."

Tom cried. He cried and cried and cried. He wished he never played marriage. He wished he never met Lena. He wished he could play cars. He wished he could be free.

But Lena was persistent. She did not let him go. She did not let him cry. She did not let him wish. She only let him be hers.

The end.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were spies and look for clues. Tim had a toy gun that made a loud noise when he pressed a button. Lily had a magnifying glass that made things look bigger.

"Look, Tim, I found a clue!" Lily said, pointing to a shiny thing on the ground. "It's a ring with a letter on it. Maybe it belongs to the bad guy we are looking for."

Tim ran over to see the ring. He picked it up and looked at it. It had a letter B on it. "Maybe it's for Bob or Ben or Bill," he said. "Let's keep it and show it to mom and dad later. Maybe they can help us find the bad guy."

They put the ring in their pocket and continued to play. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. They decided to hide there and wait for the bad guy to come. They crawled inside the hole and peeked out.

Suddenly, they heard a loud bark. It was a big dog that was running towards them. It had a collar with a tag that said Rex. It looked angry and hungry.

"Help, Tim, help!" Lily screamed. "The dog is going to get us!"

Tim grabbed his toy gun and pressed the button. It made a loud noise. "Bang, bang, bang!" he shouted. "Go away, dog, go away!"

The dog stopped and looked at Tim. It tilted its head and wagged its tail. It was not angry and hungry. It was friendly and playful. It liked the noise that the toy gun made. It ran towards Tim and licked his face.

"Hey, stop it, dog, stop it!" Tim said, laughing. "You are tickling me!"

Lily came out of the hole and saw the dog. She was not scared anymore. She petted the dog and smiled. "He's a nice dog, Tim," she said. "He just wanted to play with us. Maybe he's the bad guy's dog and he ran away from him. Maybe he's looking for a new home."

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" the man said again. "This ring is very special to me. It was a gift from my wife. You are very kind and smart kids. You are like spies. You found my dog and my ring. You are amazing!"

After a while, the friend was able to fix the motorcycle. The man was so happy and thanked his friend. The nosy little dog was also happy to see the motorcycle fixed and barked happily. From that day on, the man made sure to take good care of his motorcycle so it wouldn't break down again.

As they walked home, they heard a loud noise. It was a threat! Max barked loudly and scared away the threat. Lily was so grateful to have such a brave friend.

Once upon a time, there was a green frog named Freddy. He lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Freddy saw a ship sailing in the pond. He was very excited and wanted to see it closely. 

Freddy went to his friend, a duck, and asked, "Have you seen the ship in the pond?" 

The duck replied, "Yes, I have seen it. It is big and covers a lot of space in the pond." 

Freddy was curious and wanted to see the ship. He went closer to the ship and saw that it was carrying many things. Freddy saw a green cloth on the ship and he wanted it. He went to the captain of the ship and asked, "Can I have the green cloth, please?" 

The captain replied, "Sure, you can have it. It's just a small piece of cloth." 

Freddy was very happy and took the green cloth with him. He covered himself with it and felt very cozy. From that day on, Freddy always covered himself with the green cloth whenever he slept.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear soft velvet dresses and play outside with her friends. One day, while she was playing, she found a shiny rock on the ground. 

She showed it to her friend, Timmy, and said, "Look! I found a pretty rock!" 

Timmy looked at the rock and said, "That's not just any rock, it's a diamond!" 

Lily's eyes widened with excitement. "Wow! Can I keep it?" 

Timmy thought for a moment and said, "I think we should take it to the teacher. She's honest and will know what to do." 

So they took the diamond to their teacher, who praised them for being honest and returning it. She also told them the story of how diamonds are formed and how valuable they are. 

Lily and Timmy learned that it's always better to be honest and do the right thing, even if it's hard. And that striking it rich with a diamond isn't as important as being a good person.

Lily was very happy to see her aunt at the door. She liked her aunt, who always brought her toys and candy. She ran to hug her aunt and said, "Hello, aunt! I missed you!"

Her aunt hugged her back and said, "Hello, Lily! I missed you too! Do you want to see what I brought you?" She took out a big box from her bag and opened it. Inside, there was a beautiful doll with long hair and a pink dress.

Lily gasped and said, "Wow! She is so pretty! Thank you, aunt!" She reached for the doll, but her aunt pulled it back.

"Not so fast, Lily. You have to do something for me first. You have to crawl on the floor like a dog and bark three times. Then you can have the doll."

Lily felt confused and sad. She did not want to crawl on the floor like a dog. She did not think that was fun. She thought that was rude. She looked at her aunt and said, "No, aunt. I don't want to do that. That is not nice. Please give me the doll."

Her aunt frowned and said, "No, Lily. You have to do what I say. You are a bad girl if you don't. Now crawl on the floor and bark, or I will take the doll away."

Lily felt scared and angry. She did not like her aunt anymore. She did not want her doll anymore. She wanted her mom. She started to cry and said, "No, aunt. You are rude. You are mean. I don't like you. Go away. Mom, help me!"

Her mom heard her cry and came to the door. She saw her aunt holding the doll and Lily crying on the floor. She understood what happened and said, "Aunt, what are you doing? Why are you making Lily cry? Why are you being so rude?"

Her aunt looked embarrassed and said, "I was just playing with her. I thought she would like it. It was a joke."

Her mom said, "That was not a joke. That was cruel. You should apologize to Lily and give her the doll. Or you can leave and never come back."

Her aunt said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, mom. I was wrong. Here, take the doll. I hope you forgive me."

Lily stopped crying and took the doll. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. I love the doll. But I don't love aunt."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a good girl. You don't have to love aunt. But you can be polite to her. Maybe she will learn to be nice too."

Her aunt said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I love you too. I will try to be nice to you. Can we be friends?"

Lily looked at her aunt and said, "Maybe. But you have to be nice. And you have to crawl on the floor like a dog and bark three times. Then we can be friends."

Her aunt said, "What? No, Lily. That is not fair. That is rude."

Lily said, "Yes, aunt. That is rude. Now you know how I felt. Do you want to be friends or not?"

Her aunt said, "Fine, Lily. I will do it. But only this once. And only because I love you."

Her aunt crawled on the floor like a dog and barked three times. Lily laughed and said, "Good, aunt. You are funny. Now we can be friends. But don't be rude again. Or I will make you do something else."

Her aunt said, "OK, Lily. I promise. I won't be rude again. Can I hug you?"

Lily said, "Yes, aunt. You can hug me. But be gentle. And don't take my doll."

Her aunt said, "OK, Lily. I won't take your doll. I will be gentle. And I will be nice."

They hugged and smiled. Her mom smiled too. She was glad they made up. She hoped they would be nice to each other from now on. She said, "Now, who wants some cookies?"

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big balloon in the sky. It is red and yellow and blue. It looks great.

"Wow, look at the balloon!" Tom says. "I want to go in it and fly."

"Me too," Jen says. "Let's search for it. Maybe we can find it and go in it."

They run after the balloon. They cross the street. They go into the woods. They do not see the balloon anymore. They are lost.

"Tom, I'm scared," Jen says. "Where are we? Where is the balloon?"

"I don't know," Tom says. "Maybe the balloon flew away. Maybe it ran out of gas. Gas makes the balloon fly."

They hear a loud noise. It is a car. It is their mom and dad. They are looking for them.

"Tom! Jen! Where are you?" Mom and Dad shout.

"Here we are!" Tom and Jen shout back. They run to the car. They hug Mom and Dad.

"We were so worried about you," Mom says. "Why did you run away?"

"We wanted to go in the balloon," Jen says. "It looked great."

"But you should not go away without telling us," Dad says. "You could get hurt. You could get lost. You should stay with us."

"We're sorry," Tom and Jen say. "We were silly. We won't do it again."

Mom and Dad smile. They take them back to the park. They see the balloon again. It is still in the sky.

"Look, there is the balloon," Tom says.

"It is still great," Jen says.

"But not as great as you," Mom and Dad say. They hug them again.

Tom and Jen learn a lesson. They learn that the balloon is not worth leaving their mom and dad. They learn that they should listen to them and stay safe. They learn that they are loved.

Lila was a fish who liked to swim in the reef. The reef was lovely, with many colors and shapes. Lila had many friends in the reef, like Bob the crab, Nia the starfish, and Sam the turtle.

One day, Lila saw a shiny thing in the water. It was a ring that a human had dropped. Lila wanted to have the ring, because it was shiny and pretty. She swam closer to the ring, but Bob the crab said, "Lila, don't touch that! It is not for fish, it is for humans. It might hurt you or make you sick."

Lila ignored Bob the crab. She thought he was just jealous of the ring. She swam closer and closer, until she could touch the ring with her fin. She felt a sharp pain, and saw blood in the water. The ring had a hook inside, and it had caught her fin.

Lila cried out, "Help, help! The ring is hurting me!" She tried to swim away, but the hook was stuck. She felt scared and sorry. She wished she had listened to Bob the crab.

Bob the crab heard Lila's cry, and he swam to help her. He used his claws to cut the line that held the hook. He freed Lila from the ring, and said, "Lila, are you okay? I told you not to touch the ring. It was a trap for fish, not a toy."

Lila felt ashamed and grateful. She said, "Bob, I'm sorry I ignored you. You were right, the ring was bad. Thank you for saving me. You are a good friend."

Bob the crab smiled, and said, "You're welcome, Lila. I'm glad you're safe. Come on, let's go back to the reef. The reef is lovely, and it has everything we need."

Lily nodded, and smiled. She said, "Yes, please. I want to meet the fairy, and I want to make a wish. I want to have fun, and I want to be happy." The voice said, "Then, hold my ribbon, and close your eyes. And believe, Lily. Believe with all your heart." Lily did as the voice said, and felt a warm and gentle breeze. She closed her eyes, and felt herself flying. She opened them again, and saw a bright and beautiful world, full of flowers and butterflies and rainbows. And there, in front of her, was the fairy, smiling and waving. She said, "Hello, Lily. I am your friend, and I am here to make your wish come true. Come with me, and let's have some fun." Lily reached out her hand, and took the fairy's hand. She felt happy and brave, and she said, "Thank you, magic book. Thank you, fairy. Let's go." And they flew away, to have fun adventures in the magic world. And Lily forgot about her fears, and her sadness, and her loneliness. And she had the best dream ever.

Lily was a little girl who liked to draw. She had many crayons and papers in her room. She drew flowers, stars, animals and people. One day, she wanted to draw an angel. She asked her mom, "Mom, what does an angel look like?"

Her mom smiled and said, "An angel is a beautiful person who has wings and a halo. They live in the sky and help God. They are kind and good and love everyone."

Lily nodded and said, "I want to draw an angel like that. Can you help me, mom?"

Her mom said, "Of course, I can help you. Let's go to your room and find some crayons and papers. You can use white for the wings and the halo, and any color you like for the clothes and the hair."

Lily and her mom went to her room and started to draw. Lily drew a big circle for the head, two small circles for the eyes, a line for the mouth, and a dot for the nose. She drew a long oval for the body, two sticks for the legs, and two more sticks for the arms. She drew two big curves for the wings, and a small circle for the halo. She colored the clothes pink, the hair yellow, and the wings and the halo white.

She showed her mom her drawing and said, "Look, mom, this is my angel. Do you like it?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "I love it, Lily. You are a very successful artist. Your angel is beautiful and happy. I'm sure God and the other angels like it too. You are a very smart and creative girl. I'm very proud of you."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best mom in the world. I love you."

They kissed and hugged and put the drawing on the wall. Lily felt happy and proud. She had drawn an angel.

They pull the tire and fight. They are not happy.

A dog comes to the park. He sees the tire. He thinks it is a toy. He runs to the tire and bites it. He makes a hole in the tire. The air comes out. The tire is flat.

Tom and Ben stop fighting. They look at the tire. They are sad.

"Look what you did," Tom says to Ben. He speaks mean and angry.

"I did not do it. The dog did it," Ben says to Tom. He speaks calm and honest.

They look at the dog. The dog wags his tail. He thinks they are his friends. He is loyal and happy.

Tom and Ben feel bad. They know they were wrong. They say sorry to each other. They hug and make up. They pet the dog and thank him. They are friends again.

The moral of the story is: Do not fight over things. Share and be kind. A loyal friend is better than a flat tire.

Tom and Ben are friends. They like to play and joke with each other. One day, they find a big box in the park. They want to see what is inside.

Tom says, "I have an idea. You go in the box and I will close it. Then I will open it and you will jump out and scare me. It will be funny."

Ben thinks it is a good joke. He goes in the box and Tom closes it. Tom waits for a few seconds and then opens the box. But Ben does not jump out. He does not move. He does not make any sound.

Tom is scared. He thinks Ben is dead. He cries and calls for help. He says, "I am sorry, Ben. I did not mean to hurt you. Please wake up."

A man hears Tom and comes to see what is wrong. He looks in the box and sees Ben. He says, "Don't worry, Tom. Ben is not dead. He is just sleeping. He must have been tired and fell asleep in the box. He will wake up soon."

Tom is happy and relieved. He hugs Ben and says, "I am sorry, Ben. I will never joke with you like that again. It was not funny. It was mean and dangerous. I love you, Ben. You are my best friend."

Ben wakes up and hears Tom. He says, "I love you too, Tom. You are my best friend. I am sorry, too. I did not mean to scare you. It was not a good joke. It was silly and stupid. We should never play with things we don't know. They might be bad or hurt us."

The man says, "You are right, boys. You should never play with things you don't know. You should always be careful and respectful. And you should always be kind and honest with your friends. Jokes are fun, but only when they are harmless and funny. Not when they are cruel and scary. Do you understand?"

Tom and Ben nod and say, "Yes, sir. We understand. Thank you for helping us. We are sorry for making trouble."

The man says, "You are welcome. I am glad you are okay. Now, go home and tell your parents what happened. And remember, friends don't joke with each other's lives. They joke with each other's sides. That is how you make each other laugh and happy."

Tom and Ben smile and say, "Yes, sir. We will. Thank you again. Goodbye."

They hold hands and walk home. They have learned a valuable lesson. They will never joke with each other's lives again. They will joke with each other's sides. And they will always be good friends.

Lily nodded and handed her mom the paper. Her mom looked at the painting and said, "You did a great job, Lily. You captured the colors and the shape of the marble very well. But what is this brown spot here?"

Lily looked at the paper and saw a brown spot near the edge. She frowned and said, "I don't know, mom. I didn't paint that."

Her mom looked closer and said, "Oh, I see. It's not paint, Lily. It's chocolate. Did you eat a yummy chocolate cookie before you painted?"

Lily remembered that she had a chocolate cookie for snack. She had licked her fingers and then touched the paper. She felt a little guilty and said, "Yes, mom. I'm sorry. I forgot to wash my hands."

Her mom laughed and said, "That's okay, Lily. It's not a big deal. It just adds some flavor to your painting. Maybe you can call it 'Marble with Chocolate'. I think it's very creative and original."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I like that name. Can I have another cookie?"

Her mom nodded and said, "Sure, Lily. But this time, remember to wash your hands before you paint again. And maybe don't paint with your mouth."

Lily giggled and said, "Okay, mom. I won't. I love you."

"I love you too, Lily. You're my little artist," her mom said, hugging her.

Tim and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs and worms. Sometimes they found other things, like rocks or seeds or coins.

One day, Tim found something big and round and brown. He showed it to Lily and said, "Look, what is this?"

Lily looked at it and said, "I think it is a potato. Mommy uses potatoes to make soup and fries. She says they grow under the ground."

Tim was surprised. He did not know that potatoes grew under the ground. He said, "Can we eat it?"

Lily said, "No, we have to wash it and cook it first. And we have to ask Mommy if we can have it. Maybe it belongs to someone else."

They decided to take the potato to Mommy and see what she would say. They ran to the house, holding the potato carefully. They were very alert and did not want to drop it or lose it.

They found Mommy in the kitchen. She was making a cake. They said, "Mommy, Mommy, look what we found!"

Mommy looked at the potato and smiled. She said, "Wow, that is a big potato. Where did you find it?"

Tim and Lily told her how they found it in the garden. They asked her if they could eat it.

Mommy said, "Of course you can eat it. It is a very nice potato. You can help me wash it and peel it and cut it. Then we can make some fries or mash it. What do you prefer?"

Tim and Lily were very happy. They said, "We like both. Can we have both?"

Mommy laughed and said, "Sure, why not? You are very lucky to find such a potato. You know, some people don't have enough potatoes to eat. We should be grateful and share what we have."

Tim and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, Mommy, we are grateful. And we will share. Can we mention the potato to our friends and invite them to have some too?"

Mommy said, "Of course you can mention the potato to your friends. And you can invite them to have some too. That is very kind and generous of you. I am proud of you."

Tim and Lily hugged Mommy and said, "Thank you, Mommy. We love you. And we love potatoes."

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, Lily invites Ben to her house. She says, "Do you want to come to my house? I have a pool. We can swim and have fun."

Ben is happy. He says, "Yes, I want to come to your house. I like to swim and have fun. Thank you for inviting me."

Lily and Ben go to Lily's house. They see the pool. It is big and blue. They put on their swimsuits and jump in the water. They splash and laugh. They have a lot of fun.

But then, Lily sees something. It is a hidden toy. It is a yellow duck. It is under the water. Lily likes the duck. She wants to have it. She swims to the duck and grabs it. She says, "Look, I found a duck. It is mine. It is a hidden toy."

Ben sees the duck too. He likes the duck. He wants to share it. He says, "Can I see the duck? Can we play with it together? It is a hidden toy."

But Lily does not want to share. She says, "No, you cannot see the duck. You cannot play with it. It is mine. I found it. Go away."

Ben is sad. He says, "But we are friends. Friends share. Sharing is good. Why are you mean to me?"

Lily does not listen. She holds the duck tight. She says, "Go away. I do not want to play with you. I only want the duck."

Ben feels hurt. He gets out of the pool. He says, "Okay, I will go away. I do not want to play with you either. You are not a good friend. You are selfish."

Lily does not care. She stays in the pool. She plays with the duck. She thinks she is happy.

But soon, she feels lonely. She looks around. She does not see Ben. She does not see anyone. She only sees the duck. She says, "Where is Ben? Where is everyone? Why am I alone?"

She realizes that she made a mistake. She was not nice to Ben. She did not share the duck. She lost her friend. She says, "I am sorry, Ben. I was wrong. I should have shared the duck. I should have been a good friend. Please come back. Please play with me."

But Ben is gone. He went home. He does not hear Lily. He does not see Lily. He does not want to talk to Lily.

Lily cries. She hugs the duck. She says, "I am sorry, duck. You are not a hidden toy. You are a bad toy. You made me lose my friend. I do not want you. I want Ben."

She throws the duck away. She gets out of the pool. She runs to her house. She hopes that Ben will forgive her. She hopes that they can be friends again.

The moral of the story is: Do not be selfish. Share what you have. Be a good friend. Friendship is more important than toys.

While Tim and Sam were busy with the acorns, they heard a loud crack. They looked up and saw the oak tree leaning towards them. It was falling down. They were scared and tried to run away. But it was too late. The oak tree fell on them and hurt them badly. They cried and screamed for help.

He said that they should respect nature and follow the rules. He said that they were lucky to be alive. He said that they learned a hard lesson.

The moral of the story is: Do not touch what you do not know. Be careful and obey the signs. Nature is amazing, but also powerful.

The park worker followed Ben to the hole. He saw Lily's head and heard her cry. He said, "Oh, dear. How did she get in there? This hole is not for children. It is for wires. There is a spider nest inside. She must have disturbed them. Don't worry, little girl. I will get you out. But first, I need to get rid of the spiders."

He used his tool to spray some water and air into the hole. The spiders came out and ran away. Lily felt them leave her face. She was relieved. The park worker then used his tool to make the hole bigger. He gently pulled Lily out. She was dirty and wet and scared. But she was free.

The park worker said, "There you go. You are out. Are you okay? Do you need a hug?"

Lily nodded and hugged him. She said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. You are very nice and brave. You saved me."

Ben hugged her too. He said, "I am sorry, Lily. I should have stopped you. I was right. It was too small and scary. You were wrong. There was a spider. A big spider. Are you mad at me?"

Lily shook her head. She said, "No, I am not mad. You are my friend. You tried to help me. You were right. I was wrong. I was silly. I will never go in there again. I learned my lesson."

The park worker smiled and said, "That's good. You learned your lesson. You should never go into places that are not for children. They might be dangerous or dirty or full of spiders. You should always listen to your friend. He cares about you. And you should always have fun in the park. But be careful and safe. Okay?"

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Okay."

They thanked the park worker again and went back to play. They decided to go on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But they avoided the big stand with many holes. They had enough adventure for one day.

But then, Lily had a clever idea. She saw the mist was getting thicker and decided to run into it. When Tommy finished counting, he couldn't see Lily anywhere. He looked and looked, but all he could see was the mist. 

Lily giggled as she watched Tommy search for her. Finally, she popped out from behind a bush and surprised him. Tommy was amazed at how clever Lily was to use the mist to hide. He was happy to have such a smart friend.

"I won't ruin them, Timmy," Lily said.

"I know," Timmy said. "I'll prevent you from touching them by putting them up high on my shelf."

Lily looked up at the stamps, with their red and blue colors. "Wow, they're so pretty," she said. 

Timmy smiled. "Yes, they are. But they're also very special to me. That's why I need to keep them safe." 

Lily nodded and went to play with her own toys. Timmy was happy that he found a way to keep his stamps safe and still make his sister happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their ball. But today it is dark and rainy. Mom says they cannot go out.

"Can we play inside, Mom?" Anna asks.

"Yes, you can, but be careful and quiet. Dad is working in his room," Mom says.

Anna and Ben go to their bedroom. They find some toys and books. They play with their cars and dolls. They read some stories. They have fun.

But after a while, they get bored. They want to do something else.

"Can we play hide and seek?" Ben asks.

"OK, but we have to be quiet," Anna says.

They decide that Ben will count and Anna will hide. Ben covers his eyes and counts to ten. Anna looks for a good hiding place. She sees a big closet. She opens the door and goes inside. She closes the door behind her.

Ben finishes counting and starts to look for Anna. He looks under the bed, behind the curtains, in the drawers. He cannot find her.

"Where are you, Anna?" he calls.

Anna hears him, but she does not answer. She wants to surprise him. She waits in the closet. But it is very dark and quiet in there. She starts to feel scared. She wishes she had not hidden there.

"Anna, where are you?" Ben calls again. He is getting worried. He does not like to play alone.

Anna wants to come out, but she cannot. The door is stuck. She pushes and pulls, but it does not move. She starts to cry.

"Help, Ben, help! I'm in the closet!" she shouts.

Ben hears her voice. He runs to the closet. He tries to open the door, but it is too hard for him. He does not know what to do.

"Mom, Mom, help!" he screams.

Mom hears him. She comes to the bedroom. She sees Ben crying and banging on the closet door.

"What's wrong, Ben? What's going on?" she asks.

"Anna is in the closet. She cannot come out. The door is stuck. Please help her, Mom," Ben says.

Mom sees the problem. She grabs a chair and a screwdriver. She climbs on the chair and unscrews the door knob. She opens the door and sees Anna. She is sobbing and shaking.

"Oh, Anna, I'm so sorry. Are you OK?" she says.

She hugs Anna and lifts her out of the closet. She puts her down and hugs Ben too.

"I'm sorry, Mom. It was my fault. I hid in the closet. I was scared. I could not get out," Anna says.

"It's OK, Anna. It was an accident. You are safe now. You are brave. I'm proud of you," Mom says.

She kisses Anna and Ben and smiles.

"Next time, let's play something else, OK?" she says.

"OK, Mom. We love you," Anna and Ben say.

They hug Mom and each other. They are happy again. They have learned a lesson. They will not hide in the dark closet again. They will ask Mom for help if they have a question or a problem. They will manage to play better and safer.

One day, they observe a new thing. It is a big truck. It has many boxes. The boxes have pictures of food. Anna and Ben are curious. They want to observe the food.

They run to the truck. They see a man. He is wearing a hat and a shirt. He is taking the boxes out of the truck. He puts them on a cart. He smiles at Anna and Ben.

"Hello, little ones. Do you want to observe my food?" he asks.

"Yes, please!" Anna and Ben say.

The man shows them the boxes. He opens one. He takes out a bag. The bag has cookies. He gives one to Anna and one to Ben.

"These are cookies. They are sweet and crunchy. Do you like them?" he asks.

Anna and Ben bite the cookies. They are delicious. They nod and smile.

"Yes, we like them. Thank you!" they say.

The man opens another box. He takes out a bottle. The bottle has juice. He gives one to Anna and one to Ben.

"This is juice. It is cold and fruity. Do you like it?" he asks.

Anna and Ben drink the juice. It is refreshing. They nod and smile.

"Yes, we like it. Thank you!" they say.

The man opens another box. He takes out a can. The can has soup. He opens the can. He pours the soup into a bowl. He heats it up. He gives it to Anna and Ben.

"This is soup. It is warm and tasty. Do you like it?" he asks.

Anna and Ben sip the soup. It is comforting. They nod and smile.

"Yes, we like it. Thank you!" they say.

The man is happy. He likes to share his food. He likes to see Anna and Ben observe and enjoy it.

"You are very welcome. You are good observers. And good eaters. Do you want more food?" he asks.

Anna and Ben are full. They shake their heads.

"No, thank you. We have enough food. We are comfortable." they say.

The man nods. He packs his boxes. He puts them back on the truck. He waves at Anna and Ben.

"Goodbye, little ones. Have a nice day. Keep observing!" he says.

Anna and Ben wave back.

"Goodbye, sir. Have a nice day. Thank you for the food!" they say.

They run back to their mom. They tell her about the food and the man. They are happy. They hug their mom. They are comfortable.

Ben and Lily were twins who lived on a big ranch with their mom and dad. They liked to play with the animals, ride the horses, and help with the chores. One day, they saw a new truck in the yard. It was shiny and red, and had a big sign on the side that said "Original Paintings by Bob".

"Who is Bob?" Ben asked.

"Bob is a friend of dad's. He is an artist. He makes pictures with paint and brushes," mom explained.

"Can we see his pictures?" Lily asked.

"Sure, let's go say hello to him," mom said.

They followed mom to the truck, where Bob was waiting with a smile. He opened the back of the truck and showed them his paintings. They were very colorful and bright, and had different shapes and patterns. Some looked like flowers, some looked like animals, and some looked like nothing Ben and Lily had ever seen before.

"Wow, these are amazing!" mom said.

"Thank you. I like to use my imagination and create original things," Bob said.

Ben and Lily stared at the paintings. They liked some of them, but some of them made them feel confused or scared. They did not understand what Bob was trying to say with his paint and brushes.

"Can we make our own pictures?" Ben asked.

"Of course you can. Here, I have some paper and crayons for you. You can use any colors and shapes you want," Bob said.

He gave them each a sheet of paper and a box of crayons. Ben and Lily started to draw. Ben drew a picture of the ranch, with the house, the barn, the animals, and the fence. He used brown, green, blue, and yellow. Lily drew a picture of a rainbow, with a unicorn, a fairy, and a star. She used pink, purple, white, and glitter.

They showed their pictures to Bob and mom. Bob and mom smiled and praised them.

"Very good, Ben and Lily. You are both very talented. You have your own original styles," Bob said.

Ben and Lily felt happy and proud. They thanked Bob for his paper and crayons, and asked if they could keep their pictures. Bob said yes, and gave them each a hug. He said he had to go to another place to show his paintings, but he would come back and visit them again. He said goodbye to mom and dad, and drove away in his shiny red truck.

Ben and Lily ran to their room and hung their pictures on the wall. They looked at them and smiled. They liked their own pictures better than Bob's. They decided they wanted to be artists when they grew up.

One day, they saw something shiny in the drain. They moved the cover and looked inside. They saw a necklace with a blue stone. It was very pretty.

"Wow, look at this!" Sam said. "Who do you think it belongs to?"

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it is from an unknown princess. Maybe she lost it when she was running away from a dragon."

"Or maybe it is from a pirate," Sam said. "Maybe he hid it here and forgot about it."

They both wanted to have the necklace. They both reached for it at the same time. They pulled and tugged and fought.

"Let go, it's mine!" Sam said.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said.

They were so busy fighting that they did not hear their mom calling them. She came to the garden and saw them by the drain.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "Why are you fighting?"

They both stopped and looked at her. They both held the necklace.

"We found this in the drain," Sam said. "We don't know who it belongs to."

Mom looked at the necklace. She smiled and shook her head.

"That's not from an unknown princess or a pirate," she said. "That's from your grandma. She gave it to me when I was little. I lost it when I was playing here with your uncle. I thought it was gone forever."

She took the necklace and put it around her neck. She hugged Sam and Lily.

"Thank you for finding it," she said. "It's very special to me. But you know what's more special? You two. You are my own treasures. And you should not fight over things. You should share and be kind to each other."

Sam and Lily felt sorry for fighting. They said sorry to each other and to mom. They decided to play something else. They left the drain alone. They did not want to find any more unknown things. They had enough of their own.

Tommy was a little boy who liked to learn new things. He learned how to count, how to draw, and how to ride a bike. But there was one thing he did not like to learn: how to sleep in his own bed.

Every night, Tommy would crawl into his parents' bed and snuggle with them. He felt safe and warm there. He did not like his own bed. It was too big, too cold, and too uncomfortable.

One night, his parents said, "Tommy, you are a big boy now. You need to learn how to sleep in your own bed. We love you, but we need some space too."

Tommy did not want to hear that. He cried and begged and said, "No, no, no! I want to sleep with you! Please, please, please!"

His parents were firm. They said, "No, Tommy, you have to sleep in your own bed. We will read you a story, we will give you a hug and a kiss, and we will leave the light on. But you have to stay in your own bed."

They did as they said. They read him a story, they gave him a hug and a kiss, and they left the light on. But Tommy still felt unhappy. He felt lonely and scared and uncomfortable. He missed his parents. He wanted to go to them.

He got out of his bed and tiptoed to their door. He opened it quietly and peeked inside. He saw his parents sleeping peacefully. He saw a little space between them. He thought, "Maybe I can squeeze in there. Maybe they won't notice. Maybe they won't mind."

He crept into their bed and tried to fit in. But he was too big. He bumped into his mom and dad. He made them wake up. They were not happy. They said, "Tommy, what are you doing here? We told you to sleep in your own bed. Go back to your room, now!"

Tommy felt sad and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I just wanted to be with you. I don't like my bed. It's uncomfortable."

His parents said, "We understand, Tommy, but you have to learn to sleep in your own bed. It's good for you. It will make you more independent and confident. It will also make us more rested and relaxed. We love you, but we need some boundaries."

They took him by the hand and led him back to his room. They tucked him in and said, "Good night, Tommy. We love you. You can do this. You are a brave boy. You can sleep in your own bed."

They kissed him and left. Tommy felt a little better. He thought, "Maybe they are right. Maybe I can do this. Maybe I can sleep in my own bed."

He closed his eyes and tried to sleep. He thought about the story they read him. He thought about the hug and the kiss they gave him. He thought about the light they left on. He felt a little warmer, a little safer, a little more comfortable.

He fell asleep and had a good dream. He learned how to sleep in his own bed. He was proud of himself. He was a big boy.

One day, a squirrel named Sam was looking for acorns in the forest. He saw a big tree with many acorns on its branches. He climbed up the tree and picked an acorn. He was very happy.

But then, he heard a loud noise. It was a woodpecker, who was pecking the tree. The woodpecker made the tree shake and the acorns fall. Sam was scared and uncomfortable. He did not like the noise and the shaking.

"Please, quit pecking the tree!" Sam shouted to the woodpecker. "You are making me lose my acorns!"

The woodpecker looked at Sam and said, "I am sorry, but I need to peck the tree. It is my home and I need to make a hole for my family. You can find other acorns in other trees."

Sam thought for a moment. He realized that the woodpecker was right. He had many other trees to look for acorns, but the woodpecker had only one tree to make his home. He decided to be kind and share the tree with the woodpecker.

"Okay, I understand," Sam said to the woodpecker. "You can peck the tree, but please be careful not to make too much noise and not to make too many acorns fall."

The woodpecker nodded and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good squirrel and a good friend. I will try to be quiet and not to waste too many acorns."

Sam smiled and said, "You are welcome, woodpecker. You are a good bird and a good friend. I will go to another tree and find more acorns."

Sam and the woodpecker waved goodbye to each other and went on with their tasks. They were both happy and comfortable in the forest. They learned to respect and help each other.

But then they saw a big dog. It was black and brown, and it had sharp teeth and a loud bark. It was not on a leash, and it ran towards them. Anna and Ben were scared. They did not know the dog, and they did not know if it was friendly or mean.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. They ran to the slide and climbed up. The dog followed them and jumped on the slide. It tried to bite them, but they kicked it away. They were in panic. They did not know what to do.

A man came running. He was the dog's owner. He was ignorant. He did not know that his dog was dangerous and that he should keep it on a leash. He shouted at the dog and grabbed its collar. He pulled it away from the slide and apologized to Anna and Ben.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry. He's just playful, he doesn't mean any harm. He likes children, really. He's a good dog, aren't you, boy?" he said to the dog.

Anna and Ben did not believe him. They were angry and hurt. They did not want to play with the dog or the man. They wanted to go home and tell their mom and dad what happened. They hoped they would never see the dog or the man again. They learned that some dogs and some people are not nice, and that they should be careful in the park.

"Yes, please!" Ben said.

"Yes, I can," Ben said.

Lisa showed Ben how to ask Luna. He had to put his hand in the water and make a circle. Luna saw Ben and came closer. She made a noise and touched his hand with her nose.

"Wow, she said yes!" Lisa said. "You can pet her gently now. She likes it when you scratch her head."

Ben smiled and petted Luna. He felt her skin. It was wet and soft. Luna made more noises and moved her tail. She was happy.

"OK, Frosty is a good name," Ben agreed. "But we have to be careful. The sun is very bright today. It might make him melt."

They decided to find a shady spot for Frosty. They looked around and saw a big hole in the ground. It was the entrance to a tunnel. They thought it would be a good place for Frosty to stay cool.

"Come on, Frosty, let's go underground," Lila said. She and Ben pushed Frosty towards the hole. It was hard work, but they managed to get him inside.

They followed Frosty into the tunnel. It was dark and cold. They could see their breath in the air. They felt the icy walls with their hands. They heard a strange noise.

"What's that?" Ben asked, scared.

"I don't know," Lila said, holding his hand. "Maybe it's a monster."

They wanted to go back, but they couldn't see the way out. They were lost and afraid. They wished they had never gone underground.

They started to cry. They hugged Frosty and each other. They hoped someone would find them soon.

They didn't know that their mom was looking for them. She saw their footprints in the snow. She followed them to the hole. She called their names.

"Lila! Ben! Where are you?"

They heard her voice. They were so happy. They shouted back.

"Mom! We're here! We're underground!"

She heard them. She found a flashlight. She went into the tunnel. She saw them with Frosty. She was relieved and angry.

"What are you doing here?" she asked. "This is very dangerous. You could have been hurt. You should never go underground without me."

She hugged them and scolded them. She helped them get out of the tunnel. She took them home. She made them hot chocolate. She told them to never do that again.

They said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They thanked her for saving them. They said goodbye to Frosty. They hoped he would be OK underground. They never forgot their icy adventure.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Ben found a big spider. He was not afraid of spiders. He wanted to show Lily.

"Look, Lily, a spider!" he said, holding it in his hand.

Lily did not like spiders. She was afraid of spiders. She screamed and ran away.

"Come back, Lily, it is not scary!" Ben said, following her.

But Lily did not listen. She ran into the house and slammed the door. She told Mom about the spider.

"Mom, Ben has a spider! He tried to show me! I don't like spiders!" she cried.

Mom came out of the kitchen. She saw Ben standing at the door with the spider.

"Ben, what are you doing with that spider?" she asked.

"I found it in the garden. It is cool. I wanted to show Lily, but she ran away," Ben said.

"Ben, you can't keep a spider as a pet. It belongs in the garden. You have to remove it from the house. It might bite you or Lily or spoil the food," Mom said.

"But I like it. It is my friend," Ben said.

"Ben, I know you like it, but it is not good for the spider either. It needs to live in its own home, not in ours. Please, remove it from the house and put it back in the garden. Then you can wash your hands and have a snack," Mom said.

Ben was sad. He did not want to remove the spider from the house. He wanted to keep it. But he knew Mom was right. He opened the door and went back to the garden. He found a nice spot for the spider and let it go.

"Bye, spider. I hope you are happy. Maybe I will see you again," he said.

He went back to the house and washed his hands. Mom gave him a cookie and a glass of milk. He felt better.

"Mom, can I have a different pet?" he asked.

"Maybe, Ben. What kind of pet do you want?" Mom asked.

Ben thought for a moment. He did not want a spider anymore. He wanted something fluffy and cute.

"A bunny," he said.

Mom smiled.

"Maybe, Ben. Maybe."

"Can I have some toast too?" Anna asked.

Tom looked at Anna and shook his head. "No, this is my toast. You have to make your own."

Anna felt sad and angry. That was not fair. Tom always took the best things for himself. She remembered how he took her favorite toy yesterday and did not share.

Anna had an idea. She saw the butter and the jam on the table. She took a big spoon and scooped some butter. She ran to Tom and threw the butter at his face.

"Hey!" Tom shouted. "What are you doing?"

Anna giggled. She took another spoon and scooped some jam. She ran to Tom and threw the jam at his hair.

"Stop it!" Tom cried. "You are making a mess!"

Anna laughed. She felt happy. She made Tom look funny. She did not care about his toast anymore.

Mom came to the kitchen and saw the mess. She saw Tom with butter and jam on his face and hair. She saw Anna with a big smile on her face.

"What is going on here?" Mom asked.

Anna and Tom looked at Mom. They did not know what to say. They knew they were in trouble.

One day, Lily goes to see her dad's office with her mom. They walk in the big building and say hello to the people. Lily sees many doors and windows and pictures on the walls. She wonders what is behind each door.

One day, Sara finds a scale in the bathroom. She does not know what it is. She thinks it is a toy. She puts it on the floor and steps on it. The scale makes a beep sound and shows a number. Sara does not know what the number means. She thinks it is a game.

She calls her mom. "Mom, look at this! I found a new toy. It makes a sound and shows a number. Can you play with me?"

Mom comes to the bathroom. She sees the scale and smiles. She explains to Sara what the scale is for. She says it is not a toy, but a tool. She says it tells how much you weigh. She says it is important to be healthy and strong.

Sara is curious. She asks her mom to weigh herself. Mom steps on the scale. The scale makes a beep sound and shows a different number. Sara looks at the number and says, "Wow, mom, you are so hard!"

Mom laughs. She hugs Sara and says, "No, sweetie, I am not hard. I am heavy. Hard means something else. Hard means something that is not soft or easy. Like a rock, or a puzzle, or a word you don't know."

Sara nods. She thinks for a moment. She says, "I see. So, writing is hard for me, because I don't know many words. But I like writing, because it is fun and I can learn new words. And you are heavy, but you are not hard, because you are soft and kind and you help me learn."

Mom smiles. She kisses Sara and says, "That's right, my love. You are very smart and brave. And I am very proud of you. Now, let's put the scale away and go back to your book. Maybe you can write a story about the scale and what you learned today."

Lily was a little bird who wanted to fly. She had two wings, but they were not ready yet. They were too small and weak. Lily had to eat a lot of seeds and worms to grow and weigh more.

Every day, Lily watched the other birds fly in the sky. She wished she could join them. She asked her mom, "When can I fly, mom?"

Her mom said, "Soon, Lily, soon. You have to be patient and practice. Flap your wings every day and you will get stronger."

Lily did what her mom said. She flapped her wings every day, even when it was hard and tiring. She ate a lot of seeds and worms, even when she was full and bored. She grew and weighed more every day.

One day, Lily felt something different. Her wings felt ready. They felt big and strong. She flapped them and felt a breeze. She looked at the sky and felt a spark. She said to her mom, "Mom, I think I can fly today!"

Her mom smiled and said, "I think you can, Lily. You have worked hard and waited long. You are ready to fly. Go ahead, Lily, fly!"

Lily was so happy and excited. She flapped her wings harder and harder. She lifted off the ground and soared in the sky. She felt free and alive. She flew with the other birds and sang with joy. She had done it. She had learned to fly.

Sara and Tom are playing with their toys. Sara has a big box and Tom has a small car. Sara wants to put the car in the box, but Tom says no.

"It is my car. You can not have it," Tom says.

"But I want to play with it. It will fit in my box," Sara says.

They pull and tug on the car. The car makes a loud noise. Sara and Tom are not calm. They are angry and sad.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see. She sees Sara and Tom fighting over the car. She is not happy.

"Stop, stop, stop! What are you doing?" Mom says.

"Sara wants my car. She wants to put it in her box. But it is mine," Tom says.

"I want to play with the car. It will fit in my box. But Tom will not let me," Sara says.

Mom shakes her head. She has an idea.

"Why don't you share the car and the box? You can take turns. Sara can put the car in the box for a while, and then Tom can take it out and drive it. That way, you can both have fun," Mom says.

Sara and Tom think about it. They nod. They agree to share.

Mom smiles. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She also gives them a bowl of cream to eat. Cream is sweet and yummy. Sara and Tom like cream.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. Lily had a red car and Ben had a blue car.

"Look, my car is faster than yours!" Lily said, zooming past Ben.

"No, my car is faster!" Ben said, chasing after her.

They raced around the sofa and the table, having fun. But then, Lily's car hit a bump and stopped. She looked at it and saw that a screw had come loose.

"Oh no, my car is broken!" she cried.

Ben stopped his car and came to see. He saw the screw on the floor and picked it up.

"Here, I have your screw. Maybe we can fix your car," he said.

He tried to put the screw back in the hole, but it was too hard. He couldn't turn it with his fingers.

"We need a tool to fix it. Do you have a tool?" he asked Lily.

Lily thought for a moment. She remembered that her dad had a tool box in the garage. He used it to fix things around the house.

"Yes, I have a tool. Come with me," she said.

They ran to the garage and found the tool box. They opened it and looked inside. There were many tools of different shapes and sizes.

"Wow, look at all these tools!" Ben said.

"Which one do we need?" Lily asked.

They didn't know which tool was the right one. They tried to match the tools with the screw, but none of them fit.

"Maybe this one?" Ben said, holding a big hammer.

"No, that's too big. It will smash the car," Lily said.

"Maybe this one?" Lily said, holding a small knife.

"No, that's too sharp. It will cut the car," Ben said.

They were getting frustrated. They wanted to fix the car and play again.

"Maybe we should ask dad. He knows about tools," Lily said.

"Good idea. Let's go find him," Ben said.

They left the tool box and went to look for Lily's dad. He was in the kitchen, making a sandwich. He was a fat man with a beard and glasses.

"Hi, dad. Can you help us?" Lily said.

"Sure, what do you need?" he said.

"We need to fix Lily's car. It has a loose screw. Do you have a tool for that?" Ben said.

Lily's dad smiled and nodded. He put down his sandwich and followed them to the garage. He looked at the car and the screw.

"Ah, I see. You need a screwdriver for that. It's a tool that can turn screws. Let me show you," he said.

He took a screwdriver from the tool box and handed it to Ben.

"Here, you hold this end and put it in the hole. Then you twist it like this," he said, demonstrating.

Ben did as he was told. He put the screwdriver in the hole and twisted it. The screw went in and the car was fixed.

"Yay, you did it! Thank you, dad!" Lily said.

"You're welcome, kids. You're very smart and brave to try to fix it by yourselves. But next time, please mention it to me first, okay? Some tools can be dangerous if you don't know how to use them," he said.

"Okay, dad. We're sorry. We'll mention it to you next time," they said.

They hugged their dad and thanked him again. Then they took their cars and went back to the living room. They resumed their race and had more fun. They were happy that their car was fixed and that their dad was helpful. They learned a new word and a new tool. They had a great day.

Sara sees what Ben is doing and gasps. She loves her bear and does not want him to get hurt. She runs to catch him, but she is too late. The bear falls on the floor with a thud. He loses one of his eyes and rips his ear. He looks sad and broken.

Sara cries and picks up her bear. She hugs him and tries to fix him. She is very angry and sad. She does not want to play with Ben anymore. She yells at him.

"Bad Ben! You hurt my bear! You are not my friend! Give me back my truck!"

Ben feels sorry and scared. He did not mean to hurt the bear or Sara. He just wanted to have fun. He gives back the truck and tries to say sorry.

"Sorry Sara. I did not know. I was just playing. Please don't be mad."

But Sara does not listen. She turns away and sniffs. She takes her bear and her truck and goes to her room. She slams the door and locks it. She does not want to see Ben ever again.

Ben is left alone in the living room. He feels sad and lonely. He has no toys and no friend. He claps his hands, but there is no sound. He wishes he could take back what he did. He wishes he could make Sara happy again. But he does not know how. He sits on the floor and cries.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Lily had a big teddy bear that she hugged and kissed. Ben had a small car that he zoomed around the floor.

"Look, Lily, my car is very fast!" Ben said, showing off his car. "It can go anywhere!"

"That's nice, Ben, but my bear is very warm!" Lily said, holding her bear close. "It can cuddle with me!"

Ben wanted to cuddle with the bear too. He reached out his hand and tried to grab the bear from Lily. Lily did not like that. She pulled the bear back and said, "No, Ben, this is my bear! You have your car!"

Ben did not listen. He tried to take the bear again. Lily and Ben started to fight over the bear. They both pulled and tugged and shouted. The bear was not happy. It felt the fight in its fur and stuffing. It wished they would stop.

Then, they heard a voice from the kitchen. It was their mom. She had heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily and Ben fighting over the bear. She was not happy. She said, "Lily and Ben, what are you doing? Why are you fighting over the bear?"

Lily and Ben stopped fighting. They looked at their mom. They felt sorry. They said, "Sorry, mom."

Mom said, "You should not fight over the bear. The bear is for sharing. Sharing is good. Sharing makes you happy. Sharing makes the bear happy. Can you share the bear?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, mom."

Mom said, "Good. Now, how can you share the bear?"

Lily and Ben thought for a moment. Then, they had an idea. They said, "We can spread the bear!"

Mom said, "Spread the bear? What do you mean?"

Lily and Ben showed her. They took the bear and spread it between them. They each held one arm and one leg of the bear. They smiled and said, "See, mom, we can spread the bear! Now we can both cuddle with the bear!"

Mom smiled too. She said, "That's very clever, Lily and Ben. You are very patient and kind. You found a way to share the bear. I'm proud of you. And I'm sure the bear is happy too."

The bear was happy. It felt the warmth and love of Lily and Ben in its fur and stuffing. It wished they would always be happy. It closed its eyes and enjoyed the cuddle.

Tom was happy for Lila. He said, "Wow, that is a nice crystal! Can I see it?" Lila gave him the crystal and he held it in his hand. He saw all the colors in it and smiled.

Then, he had an idea. He said, "Do you know how to whistle, Lila?" Lila shook her head. She said, "No, I don't. How do you whistle?" Tom said, "You have to make a small hole with your lips and blow air. Like this." He put the crystal to his mouth and whistled. It made a high sound that echoed in the park.

Lila was amazed. She said, "That is so cool, Tom! How did you do that?" Tom said, "The crystal makes the sound when you whistle. It is like a magic whistle. Do you want to try?" Lila nodded. She took the crystal and put it to her mouth. She tried to whistle, but she only made a puff sound. She tried again, but nothing happened.

Tom said, "Don't worry, Lila. You have to practice. It is not easy to whistle. Here, let me help you." He took the crystal and put it to Lila's mouth. He said, "Now, make a small hole with your lips and blow air. Like this." He whistled with her and the crystal made a sound again.

Miss Rose is very nice. She has long hair and a purple dress. She smiles a lot and sings songs. Lily and Max like her. But they also notice something different about her. She has one green eye and one blue eye.

"Wow, look at her eyes!" Lily whispers to Max. "They are not the same color!"

"I know, they are cool!" Max whispers back. "Do you think she can see different things with them?"

"I don't know, maybe. Let's ask her later."

Lily and Max wait until the end of the class. Then they raise their hands and ask Miss Rose.

"Miss Rose, we have a question. Why are your eyes different colors?" Lily asks.

Miss Rose smiles and bends down to their level. She points to her eyes and says, "These are my pupils. They are the part of the eye that lets me see. Sometimes, people have pupils that are different colors. It is called heterochromia. It is not very common, but it is not bad. It just makes me special."

Lily and Max nod. They think Miss Rose is special too. They recognize that she is a good teacher and a kind person. They give her a hug and say, "Thank you, Miss Rose. We like your eyes. They are beautiful."

"You guessed very well. You guessed exactly what I have for you," Grandma said.

"Please, don't hurt me, Mr. Wolf," Lily said. "I just want to be your friend."

The wolf was surprised by Lily's words. He had never met a human who was not afraid of him. He stopped growling and gazed at Lily with curiosity.

"Why do you want to be my friend?" the wolf asked. "Humans usually hate me and try to hurt me."

Lily smiled and said, "Because you are beautiful and lonely. And I think you are wise and know many things about the woods."

The wolf felt a strange warmth in his heart. He had never heard such kind words from a human. He decided to give Lily a chance.

"Maybe you are right," the wolf said. "Maybe we can be friends. But you have to promise me something. You have to respect me and my family, and never try to harm us. And you have to listen to your brother, who is smart and cares about you."

Lily nodded and said, "I promise, Mr. Wolf. And you have to promise me something too. You have to be gentle and loyal, and never try to harm me or my brother. And you have to teach us some things about the woods."

The wolf nodded and said, "I promise, Lily. Come, let me show you my den and my cubs. They will like you too."

Lily and Ben followed the wolf to his home. They became friends and learned a lot from each other. They also learned to trust and respect each other, even though they were different.

The moral of the story is: Friendship can be found in unexpected places, if we are brave and kind. We should not judge others by their appearance, but by their character. And we should listen to those who love us and want the best for us.
