"No, I don't!" Ben said. "This is a rocket! I am the astronaut and you are the alien. You have to go away."

They both wanted the chair for their game. They started to pull and push each other. The chair wobbled and creaked.

"Stop it!" a voice said. "You are making too much noise."

They looked up and saw their grandpa. He was jolly and kind. He smiled at them and said, "What are you doing here?"

"We found this chair, grandpa," Anna said. "It is a throne for a queen."

"No, it is a rocket for an astronaut," Ben said.

Grandpa laughed and said, "Well, you both have good imaginations. But you know, this chair is very special. It belonged to your great-grandpa. He was a storyteller. He used to sit on this chair and tell me and your grandma wonderful stories. He made us believe in magic and adventure."

"Really?" Anna and Ben said.

"Yes, really," grandpa said. "And I can tell you some of his stories, if you like. But you have to share the chair and listen quietly. Do you want to hear a story?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They stopped fighting and climbed on the chair with grandpa. They snuggled close to him and waited for him to begin. They were ready to believe in anything.

Sam and Ben were brothers who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with many trees and flowers. One day, they found a can of spray paint in the garage. They decided to use it to make art on the lumber that their dad had piled up for a project.

"Look, I can spray a red star on this wood!" Sam said, shaking the can.

"Me too, me too!" Ben said, grabbing the can from Sam. "I want to spray a blue circle!"

They took turns spraying different shapes and colors on the lumber, having fun and making a mess. They did not hear their dad coming home from work.

"Hey, what are you doing?" their dad shouted, seeing the spray paint on his lumber. He was very angry. "That was for the new fence! You ruined it!"

Sam and Ben felt scared and sorry. They dropped the can and ran to their mom, who was in the kitchen.

"Mom, mom, we did something bad!" Sam cried.

"We sprayed paint on dad's wood!" Ben sobbed.

Their mom hugged them and said, "Why did you do that? You know you should not touch things that are not yours."

"We wanted to make art, mom. We did not know it was for the fence," Sam said.

Their mom sighed and said, "I understand, but you still made a big mistake. You have to apologize to your dad and help him clean up the lumber. Maybe he can still use it for something else."

Sam and Ben nodded and wiped their tears. They followed their mom to the yard, where their dad was still fuming. They said they were sorry and asked for forgiveness. Their dad was still upset, but he saw that they were sincere. He hugged them and said, "I forgive you, but you have to be more careful next time. And no more spray paint, okay?"

"Okay, dad," Sam and Ben said.

They helped their dad scrub the paint off the lumber, which took a long time and a lot of water. They learned their lesson and promised to respect their dad's things. Their dad also learned to keep his spray paint in a safer place. They finished the fence together and were cheerful again. They admired their work and their art, which still showed a little bit on the lumber. They agreed that it was not so bad after all.

Ben liked to play with his toy plane. He made it fly in the air and zoom around his room. He pretended he was a pilot and he had to go on a big mission. He put on his hat and his jacket and said, "Ready for takeoff!"

But then he saw his mom was troubled. She had a sad face and a big bag. She said, "Ben, I need to go away for a few days. I have to work in another place. I will miss you a lot, but I will call you every night."

Ben felt sad too. He did not want his mom to go. He wanted to play with her and hug her. He said, "Mom, can I go with you? I can be your pilot and help you fly the plane."

His mom smiled and hugged him. She said, "You are very sweet, Ben, but you have to stay here with dad. He will take good care of you and play with you. You can show him your toy plane and tell him your stories. And when I come back, we will have a big party and celebrate."

Ben nodded and tried to be brave. He said, "Okay, mom, I love you. Have a good trip. Be careful and come back soon."

His mom kissed him and said, "I love you too, Ben. You are my best pilot. I will see you soon."

She took her bag and left. Ben waved goodbye and ran to his dad. He said, "Dad, can we play with my toy plane? I want to show you my mission."

His dad smiled and said, "Sure, Ben, let's play. You are a great pilot and I am proud of you."

Tom and Tim were twins. They looked the same and liked the same things. They always played together and had fun. But they also fought a lot. They fought over toys, books, and snacks. They made each other angry and sad.

One day, their mom told them to rise early and help her with the chores. She said they had to clean their room, wash the dishes, and fold the laundry. Tom and Tim thought that was boring. They wanted to play and have fun. They did not want to help their mom. They said no and ran away.

Their mom was upset. She said they were naughty and selfish. She said they had to learn to share and care. She said they had to do their chores or they would not get any dessert. Tom and Tim did not listen. They hid in the backyard and played with their toys.

But soon, they got bored. They had played with all their toys and read all their books. They had nothing new to do. They looked at each other and felt lonely. They missed their mom and her hugs. They missed their dessert and her smile. They realized they had been wrong. They decided to go back and help their mom.

They ran to the house and found their mom. They said they were sorry and hugged her. They said they wanted to help her with the chores. They said they loved her and each other. Their mom was happy. She said she forgave them and hugged them back. She said she was proud of them and their change. She said they could have dessert after they finished their chores.

Tom and Tim smiled. They felt good and warm. They went to their room and cleaned it. They went to the kitchen and washed the dishes. They went to the living room and folded the laundry. They did their chores and had fun. They learned to share and care. They learned that helping their mom was not boring, but rewarding. They learned that being twins was not a reason to fight, but a reason to love.

Tim and Liz were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's enter the tree!" Tim said.

"OK, but be careful!" Liz said.

They crawled into the hole and found a dark and cozy space. They saw a trunk with a lock on it.

"Wow, what is in the trunk?" Liz wondered.

"Maybe it is a treasure!" Tim guessed.

They tried to open the trunk, but it was too hard. They pushed and pulled, but nothing happened.

Suddenly, they heard a voice.

"Who is there? What are you doing in my tree?" The voice was angry and loud.

Tim and Liz were scared. They saw a man with a beard and a hat. He was the owner of the tree and the trunk.

"We are sorry, sir. We were just playing. We did not mean to bother you." Tim said.

"You should not enter other people's homes without permission. That is rude and wrong. And you should not touch other people's things. That is stealing and bad." The man said.

Tim and Liz felt ashamed. They knew they had made a mistake.

"We are very sorry, sir. We will not do it again. Please forgive us." Liz said.

The man looked at them. He saw they were young and curious. He decided to be kind.

"OK, I forgive you. But you have to promise me to respect other people's property and privacy. And you have to leave now. This is my home, not a playground." The man said.

Tim and Liz nodded. They thanked the man and crawled out of the hole. They ran back to their parents and told them what happened. They learned a lesson that day. They never entered the tree again.

Tom and Sue were twins who liked to play together. They also liked to eat cake, but they had to wait for their mom to bake it. One day, their mom made a big cake for their birthday and put it on the table. She told them not to touch it until she came back from the store.

Tom and Sue looked at the cake and their mouths watered. They wanted to have a slice right now. Tom said, "Let's take a little bit. Mom won't notice." Sue said, "No, that's bad. Mom said to wait. We have to be honest." Tom said, "Don't be silly. It's just a little bit. Come on, it's our birthday." He reached for the knife and cut a small piece of cake.

Sue felt bad and tried to stop him. She said, "Tom, stop! You're being naughty. Mom will be mad." She grabbed his arm and pulled it away from the cake. Tom got angry and slapped her on the face. Sue cried out and ran to the couch. She felt a sting on her cheek and tears in her eyes.

Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He realized he had hurt his sister and disobeyed his mom. He put the piece of cake back on the plate and tried to fix it. He said, "Sue, I'm sorry. I was wrong. Please forgive me." He went to the couch and hugged her. Sue hugged him back and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But we have to tell mom the truth."

They waited for their mom to come back. When she saw the cake, she noticed the cut. She asked them, "Who did this?" Tom and Sue looked at each other and said, "We did. We're sorry. We wanted to eat some cake, but we fought and Tom slapped Sue. We learned our lesson. We won't do it again." Their mom was disappointed, but also proud. She said, "Thank you for being honest. That's very brave and good. But you still have to face the consequences. You can't have any cake today. Maybe tomorrow, if you behave well." Tom and Sue nodded and said, "We understand. We love you, mom." They hugged their mom and said sorry again.

The moral of the story is: Honesty is the best policy. Don't be greedy and selfish. Respect your mom and your sister. Slapping is bad and hurts.

She runs to the slide and peeks behind it. She sees a pair of shoes and a blue hat. She smiles and says, "I found you, Max!"

But when she pulls the hat, she sees a different boy. He has brown hair and green eyes. He looks surprised and scared. He says, "Who are you? Where is Max?"

Lily feels sorry and says, "I'm sorry, I thought you were my friend. He is hiding too. What is your name?"

The boy says, "I'm Ben. I was hiding from my sister. She is mean and takes my toys."

Lily says, "That's not nice. Do you want to play with us? We are nice and we share our toys."

Lily says, "Sure, but first you have to find Max. He is very good at hiding. If you find him, you get a reward. We have cookies and juice in our backpack."

Ben says, "OK, I like cookies and juice. Let's go find Max!"

"Look, Lily, I found a footprint!" Ben said, pointing to the dirt. "Maybe it belongs to the thief who stole the cookies from the kitchen."

"Good job, Ben! Let's follow it and see where it leads." Lily said, holding the flashlight. They walked along the dirt path, looking for more footprints.

Suddenly, they heard a loud bark. A big dog was running towards them, growling and showing its teeth. It was the neighbor's dog, Rocky. He did not like strangers in his yard.

"Run, Lily, run!" Ben shouted, dropping the flashlight. They tried to run back to their garden, but Rocky was faster. He caught up with them and bit Ben's leg. Ben screamed in pain and fell to the ground.

Lily was scared. She wanted to help Ben, but she did not know what to do. She saw the flashlight on the ground, but the bulb was broken. It did not work anymore. She could not use it to scare Rocky away.

She looked around, hoping to see someone who could help them. But there was no one. They were alone with the angry dog. Lily started to cry. She wished they had never tried to solve the mystery of the missing cookies. It was not a fun game. It was a serious problem.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big red wagon near the swings. It had four wheels and a long rope.

"Let's pull the wagon!" Lily said. "We can put our toys inside and go for a trip."

"OK!" Tom said. He grabbed one end of the rope and Lily grabbed the other. They put their dolls and cars and balls in the wagon. Then they started to pull.

They pulled the wagon around the park. They went past the trees and the flowers and the pond. They saw some ducks and some dogs and some kids. They waved and smiled and laughed.

But then they came to a hill. It was steep and bumpy. Lily and Tom tried to pull the wagon up the hill. But it was too heavy and too hard. They pulled and pulled and pulled. But the wagon did not move.

"Pull harder!" Lily said.

"I am!" Tom said.

They pulled harder and harder and harder. But the wagon still did not move. Then the rope snapped. It broke in two. Lily and Tom fell down. The wagon rolled down the hill. It went faster and faster and faster. It bumped into a rock and flew in the air. It landed in the pond with a splash.

Lily and Tom got up. They were dirty and wet and sad. They looked at the wagon in the pond. Their toys were floating and sinking. They felt like crying.

"Are you OK?" a voice said. It was their mom. She had seen what happened. She ran to them and hugged them.

"We're OK," Lily said. "But our wagon is not."

"And our toys," Tom said.

"I'm sorry, sweeties," mom said. "That was a bad trip. But don't worry. We can get a new wagon and new toys. And you can still have fun in the park. Come on, let's go to the slide. It's your favorite."

Lily and Tom nodded. They wiped their tears and followed their mom. They still felt a little pale, but they also felt a little better. They hoped to have a better trip next time.

Anna liked to play in the old barn. She liked to look at the animals and the hay and the tools. But she did not like the cobwebs. They were sticky and scary and made her sneeze.

One day, she saw a big cobweb in the corner. It had a spider in it. The spider was black and hairy and had eight legs. Anna was afraid of the spider. She wanted to run away.

But then she heard a voice. It was a small and soft voice. It came from the cobweb.

"Hello, little girl," the voice said. "Don't be afraid of me. I am not mean. I am just a spider."

Anna was surprised. She looked at the cobweb again. She saw a tiny spider next to the big one. The tiny spider was pale and shiny and had four legs. It looked friendly.

"Who are you?" Anna asked.

"I am Lila," the tiny spider said. "I am the big spider's baby. He is my dad. He is very nice. He makes the cobweb for us to live in. He catches flies and bugs for us to eat. He teaches me how to spin silk and make patterns. He is the best dad in the world."

Anna felt curious. She wanted to know more about the spiders. She asked, "How do you make silk? How do you make patterns? How do you weigh the flies and bugs?"

Lila smiled. She said, "We make silk from our bodies. We have special parts that make the silk come out. We use our legs and our mouths to shape the silk into the cobweb. We make patterns to make the cobweb beautiful and strong. We weigh the flies and bugs by feeling them with our legs. We know how much they weigh by how much they wiggle and how hard they are."

Anna thought that was amazing. She said, "Wow, you are very clever and talented. You and your dad are very good at making cobwebs. I am sorry I was scared of you. Can we be friends?"

Lila nodded. She said, "Yes, we can be friends. You are very kind and brave. You and I are very different, but we can learn from each other. Do you want to see how we make the cobweb?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, I do. Can I come closer?"

Lila said, "Yes, you can. But be careful. Don't touch the cobweb. It is sticky and delicate. And don't make too much noise. We don't want to scare away the flies and bugs."

Anna said, "OK, I will be careful and quiet. Thank you for letting me see your cobweb."

Lila said, "You're welcome. Come on, follow me."

Anna followed Lila to the cobweb. She watched as Lila and her dad spun silk and made patterns. She learned a lot about the spiders and their cobweb. She was happy and amazed. She made a new friend.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big jug under a bush. It was brown and had a funny shape.

"Look, Kim, a jug!" Tim said. "Maybe it has something inside."

"Let's open it and see," Kim said. She tried to pull the lid, but it was stuck. Tim helped her, and they both pulled hard. With a loud pop, the lid came off.

Suddenly, a cloud of smoke came out of the jug. It made them cough and sneeze. Then, a voice spoke from the smoke.

"Who are you, and what do you want?" the voice said. "I am a powerful genie, and I can grant you three wishes. But you must be careful what you wish for."

Tim and Kim were surprised and scared. They had never seen a genie before. They did not know what to wish for.

"Um, hello, Mr. Genie," Tim said. "We are Tim and Kim, and we found your jug. We did not mean to bother you."

"Yes, yes, I know," the genie said. "But you have freed me from the jug, and now I must grant you three wishes. It is the rule. So, what do you want?"

Tim and Kim looked at each other. They did not want anything bad to happen. They thought for a moment.

"Can we wish for more wishes?" Kim asked.

"No, no, no," the genie said. "That is not allowed. You must wish for something else."

"Can we wish for you to be happy and free?" Tim asked.

The genie was silent for a while. Then, he smiled.

"That is a very kind and wise wish," he said. "I have been trapped in the jug for a long time, and I have been lonely and bored. I would like to be happy and free. Thank you, Tim and Kim. You have one wish left. What do you want?"

Tim and Kim thought again. They did not need anything else. They had each other, and they had a lot of fun in the garden.

"Can we wish for you to be our friend?" Kim asked.

The genie smiled again.

"That is a very sweet and lovely wish," he said. "I would like to be your friend. You are very nice and good children. Thank you, Tim and Kim. You have made me happy and free. And you have made me your friend. You can keep the jug as a gift. And you can call me anytime you want to talk or play. I will always be here for you."

Tim and Kim hugged the genie. They were happy and excited. They had found a jug, a genie, and a friend. They had made three wonderful wishes. And they had learned a lesson. Sometimes, the best things in life are not things, but feelings.

Tom laughed and felt happy. He had fun with his laser and the dog. The dog also had fun and forgot to be angry. He wagged his tail and licked the window. Tom and the dog became friends. Tom was not anxious anymore. He liked big dogs now.

Lila and Ben were playing in the pool. They liked to splash and swim and pretend they were fish. Lila saw a big toy wolf on the edge of the pool. She wanted to play with it.

"Look, Ben, a wolf!" she said. "Can I have it?"

Ben nodded. He was a thoughtful boy. He liked to share his toys with his sister. He swam to the wolf and grabbed it. He threw it to Lila.

"Here you go, Lila. Catch!" he said.

Lila caught the wolf and hugged it. She was happy. She thanked Ben and kissed him on the cheek.

"Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. Do you want to play with the wolf too?" she asked.

Ben smiled. He liked to play with Lila. He had an idea.

"Yes, let's play. Let's pretend we are wolves too. We can dive and howl and chase each other," he said.

Lila liked the idea. She nodded. She put the wolf on her head and dived into the water. Ben followed her. They swam and howled and chased each other. They had fun. They were happy. They were wolves.

Lily liked to play with her mirror. She would make funny faces and laugh at herself. She would pretend to be a princess or a monster or a bird. She had a lot of fun with her mirror.

One day, her brother Tom wanted to play with her mirror too. He said, "Give me the mirror, Lily. It's my turn." But Lily did not want to share. She said, "No, Tom. It's my mirror. Go away." Tom got angry and tried to grab the mirror from Lily. They started to pull and tug on the mirror.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. She came into the room and saw them fighting. She said, "You need to share the mirror. It's not nice to be selfish. How about you take turns? Lily, you can play with the mirror for five minutes, and then Tom can play with it for five minutes. OK?"

Lily did not like this idea. She wanted to keep the mirror for herself. She said, "No, mom. I don't want to share. I want to play with the mirror all the time." She held the mirror tight and turned away from Tom and mom.

Mom sighed and said, "Lily, you are being very persistent. But you are also being very rude. You need to learn to share with your brother. Sharing is caring. If you don't share, you will lose the mirror. Do you want to lose the mirror?"

Lily thought for a moment. She did not want to lose the mirror. She liked the mirror a lot. But she also did not want to make mom and Tom sad. She realized that sharing was better than fighting. She said, "OK, mom. I will share the mirror. I'm sorry, Tom. You can play with the mirror too."

Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very nice. I'm sorry for being angry. You can play with the mirror first." He gave Lily a hug and waited for his turn.

Mom smiled and said, "That's very good, Lily and Tom. You are both very kind. You have learned a valuable lesson today. You have learned to share and to be fair. You have both won the mirror and each other's love." She gave them both a kiss and left them to play with the mirror.

One day, she saw her mom sewing a dress. It was a pretty dress with flowers and lace. Lily wanted to help. She was eager to join her mom and learn how to sew a dress. She asked her mom if she could sew with her.

"Sure, honey, you can sew with me," her mom said. "But you have to be careful. The needles are sharp and the thread is thin. You don't want to hurt yourself or make a mess."

Lily nodded. She took a needle and some thread from her mom's basket. She found a piece of cloth that matched the dress. She started to sew a small flower on the cloth. She tried to copy her mom's stitch.

But Lily was not careful. She did not look at the needle. She did not hold the thread tight. She poked her finger with the needle. It hurt a lot. She cried out loud. She dropped the needle and the thread. They fell on the floor.

Her mom heard her cry. She turned around and saw what happened. She was angry and scared. She ran to Lily and took her hand. She saw blood on her finger. She saw the needle and the thread on the floor. She saw the cloth with a big hole and a loose stitch.

"Oh, Lily, what have you done?" her mom said. "You didn't listen to me. You didn't pay attention. You ruined the cloth and you hurt yourself. You can't sew with me anymore. You have to go to your room and stay there until I say so."

Lily felt sad and sorry. She wanted to sew with her mom. She wanted to make a pretty dress. She wanted to learn how to sew a stitch. But she was not careful. She made a mistake. She made her mom angry. She had to go to her room. She did not have any fun. She did not like sewing anymore.

Sara was curious. She liked presents. She nodded and said, "Yes, please. What is it?"

The man opened his bag and took out a doll. It was a green baby. It had a dress and a bow and a pacifier. It looked very pretty. The man said, "This is a special baby. It can talk and sing and dance. Do you want to play with it?"

Sara was amazed. She had never seen a baby like that. She reached out her hand and said, "Yes, please. Can I have it?"

The man nodded and said, "Of course. But there is one condition. You have to give me one of your babies in exchange. Which one will you take?"

Sara thought for a moment. She loved all her babies. She did not want to give any of them away. But she also wanted the green baby. It was so special. She looked at her babies and said, "I will take the yellow baby. It is my least favorite."

The man smiled and said, "Very well. Here you go. Enjoy your new baby." He gave Sara the green baby and took the yellow baby. He put it in his bag and said, "Goodbye, little girl. Have fun." He closed the door and left.

One night, Tom wants to read a new book. It is about a lion and a mouse. He asks grandma to read it to him. Grandma smiles and opens the book. She reads the first page and then stops. She says, "Tom, can you read the next page?"

Tom is surprised. He looks at the print. He sees some words he knows, like "lion" and "mouse". He tries to read the page. He sounds out the words slowly. He says, "The lion was sleeping. The mouse ran over his nose. The lion woke up. He was angry. He roared and caught the mouse."

Grandma claps and hugs Tom. She says, "You did it! You read the page! I am so proud of you!" Tom feels happy and proud too. He wants to read more. He says, "Can I read the next page, grandma?" Grandma nods and says, "Of course, my dear. Let's read the book together." They read the book and find out how the mouse helps the lion. They enjoy the story and each other.

Anna liked to draw with her crayons. She drew many things, like flowers, stars, and animals. She wanted to improve her drawing, so she asked her mom for a book with pictures of different animals.

Her mom gave her a book with many colorful pages. Anna was happy and opened the book. She saw a picture of an octopus. She liked the octopus, because it had eight arms and a round head. She decided to draw the octopus on a big sheet of paper.

She took a blue crayon and started to draw the octopus. She made a big circle for the head and eight long lines for the arms. She added some dots for the eyes and a smile for the mouth. She was proud of her drawing and showed it to her mom.

"Wow, Anna, you did a great job!" her mom said. "Your octopus looks very nice and happy. You improved your drawing a lot!"

"Thank you, mom!" Anna said. "Can I hang it on the wall?"

"Of course, dear," her mom said. "Let's find a good spot for it."

They went to the living room and looked for a place to hang the drawing. They saw a hook on the wall, but it was too high for Anna to reach. Her mom lifted her up and helped her hang the drawing.

"There, now everyone can see your beautiful octopus," her mom said.

Anna smiled and hugged her mom. She was very happy with her drawing.

But there was someone else who was curious about the drawing. It was Spot, the family dog. He was a nosy dog, who liked to sniff and explore everything. He saw the drawing on the wall and wondered what it was. He walked over to the wall and jumped up to get a closer look.

He touched the drawing with his nose and felt the crayon. He thought it was something to eat, so he bit the paper and tore it off the wall. He started to chew the paper and the crayon, making a mess on the floor.

Anna and her mom heard the noise and came back to the living room. They saw Spot with the drawing in his mouth and the paper and crayon all over the floor. They were shocked and angry.

"Spot, no!" Anna shouted. "That's my octopus! You ruined it!"

"Bad dog!" her mom scolded. "Drop it, now!"

Spot dropped the drawing and looked guilty. He wagged his tail and licked his lips. He did not understand why they were mad at him. He thought he was just having a snack.

Anna and her mom picked up the pieces of the drawing and threw them in the trash. They were sad and disappointed. Anna's octopus was gone.

"I'm sorry, Anna," her mom said. "Your drawing was very nice, but Spot was too nosy and hungry. Maybe we can get you another book and some new crayons, and you can draw another octopus."

Anna nodded and wiped her tears. She still liked Spot, even though he was a naughty dog. She hoped he would not eat her drawings again. She wanted to improve her drawing, and maybe draw other animals, too. She loved to draw with her crayons.

One day, a kid named Ben went to the park with his mom. He saw a big slide and wanted to try it. He ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. He was very happy.

But when he reached the top, he saw another kid sitting on the slide. The kid had a big bag of candy and was eating it. He did not want to share or move. He said, "This is my slide and my candy. Go away!"

Ben felt sad and angry. He wanted to slide and have some candy too. He said, "That is not nice. You should share and play with others. The slide is for everyone."

The kid laughed and said, "No, it is not. I have a lot of candy and you have none. I can supply candy to anyone I want. And I don't want to supply candy to you. You are not funny. You are boring."

Ben did not like what the kid said. He thought the kid was mean and selfish. He decided to do something. He looked around and saw a big puddle of water near the slide. He had an idea. He said, "OK, fine. You can have the slide and the candy. But I have something else. I have water. And water is very funny."

He ran to the puddle and scooped up some water with his hands. He threw the water at the kid and hit him in the face. The kid was surprised and dropped his candy. The candy fell down the slide and scattered on the ground. Ben laughed and said, "See? Water is funny. And now you have no candy. And I have the slide."

The kid was wet and angry. He tried to chase Ben, but he slipped on the candy and fell down. Ben slid down the slide and ran to his mom. He told her what happened and she hugged him. She said, "You are very brave and smart, Ben. You taught that kid a lesson. But you should not throw water at people. That is not nice either."

Ben nodded and said, "I know, mom. But he was very mean and rude. He did not want to share or play. He deserved it."

Mom smiled and said, "Maybe he did. But next time, try to use your words, not your hands. And maybe you can find some other kids who are nice and funny and want to play with you."

Ben agreed and said, "OK, mom. I will. Can we have some candy now?"

Mom laughed and said, "Sure, Ben. We can have some candy. But not too much. And we will share and supply candy to anyone who asks nicely."

Ben was happy and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. And you are very funny too."

They ate some candy and played in the park. They had a lot of fun.

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. They saw a shop with a sign that said "Hot Sausages". They smelled the sausages and they wanted to try them.

But the shop was very far from their home. And their mom told them not to go too far. And the sausages were not cheap. They cost two coins each. Lily and Ben only had one coin each.

"Let's go and buy one sausage each," said Lily. "We can share them and they will be enough."

"No, that's too risky," said Ben. "What if mom finds out? What if we get lost? What if the sausages are bad?"

Lily was not scared. She was brave. She said, "I dare you to go with me. I dare you to buy a sausage. I dare you to eat it with me. It will be fun and tasty."

Ben was not sure. He was a little scared. But he did not want to look silly. He said, "OK, I dare you too. But we have to be quick and careful. And we have to hide the wrappers."

So Lily and Ben ran to the shop. They gave their coins to the man. He gave them two hot sausages wrapped in paper. They smelled so good. They ran to a bench and sat down. They opened the wrappers and bit into the sausages.

They were so yummy. They were juicy and spicy and salty. They made Lily and Ben happy. They smiled and said, "Mmm, these are the best sausages ever."

But then they heard a voice. It was their mom. She was looking for them. She was angry. She said, "Lily and Ben, where are you? What are you doing? What are you eating?"

Lily and Ben were scared. They hid the wrappers behind their backs. They said, "Nothing, mom. We are just sitting here. We are not eating anything."

But mom saw the wrappers. She saw the grease on their faces. She said, "You are lying. You ate sausages. You went to the shop. You spent your coins. You disobeyed me. You were naughty."

Lily and Ben felt bad. They knew they did wrong. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were hungry. We wanted to try the sausages. They were so yummy."

Mom said, "I don't care if they were yummy. They were not good for you. They were cheap and dirty and unhealthy. You could get sick. And you could get lost. And you could get in trouble. You should not dare to do such things. You should listen to me. You should be good."

Lily and Ben said, "We are sorry, mom. We will not do it again. We will listen to you. We will be good."

Mom said, "I hope so. Now come with me. We have to go home. And we have to wash your faces. And we have to brush your teeth. And we have to eat some fruits and vegetables. And we have to talk about what you did."

Lily and Ben followed mom. They were sad and ashamed. They learned their lesson. They did not dare to eat sausages again.

Tim and Lily were bored. They had no toys to play with. Their mom said they had to stay inside because it was cold and wet outside.

"Let's pretend we are on a train," Tim said. "We can use these chairs and this blanket."

"OK," Lily said. "But where are we going?"

Tim looked around the room. He saw a black lump on the fireplace. It was coal. His mom used it to make fire sometimes.

"We are going to the coal mine," he said. "We have to get some coal for the fire."

He picked up the coal and put it in his pocket. He covered the chairs with the blanket. He made a whistle sound with his mouth.

"All aboard!" he shouted. "The train is leaving!"

Lily climbed on the chair behind him. She held on to the blanket.

"Choo choo!" she said. "This is fun!"

They moved their feet and pretended the chairs were wheels. They imagined they saw mountains and trees and rivers outside the blanket.

Soon they reached the coal mine. Tim stopped the train.

"We are here," he said. "Let's get some more coal."

He got off the chair and looked for more coal. He found a few pieces on the floor. He put them in his pocket too.

Lily followed him. She saw a shiny thing on the floor. It was a coin. She picked it up and smiled.

"Look, Tim," she said. "I found something better than coal. It is shiny and round and pretty."

Tim looked at the coin. He did not think it was better than coal. He thought it was dull and boring.

"Who cares?" he said. "We need coal, not coins. Coal is black and hard and warm. It makes fire and smoke and steam. It is the best thing ever."

He turned away and went back to the train. He put the coal in a pile on the chair.

Lily felt sad. She liked the coin. She thought it was special and nice. She wanted Tim to like it too.

She went back to the train too. She put the coin in her pocket. She sat on the chair behind Tim.

"Can we go home now?" she asked.

"OK," Tim said. "But first we have to make the fire."

He took some coal from the pile and threw it on the fireplace. He used a match to light it. He watched the fire grow and crackle.

"Wow," he said. "Look at the fire. It is bright and hot and beautiful."

Lily looked at the fire too. She saw the coal burn and glow. She saw the smoke rise and curl. She saw the steam hiss and whistle.

She took the coin from her pocket. She held it in her hand. She looked at it again.

She saw the fire reflect on the coin. She saw the coin sparkle and shine. She saw the coin smile and wink.

She smiled too. She thought the coin was not dull and boring. She thought it was magic and wonderful.

She put the coin back in her pocket. She hugged the blanket.

"Look at the fire," she said. "It is bright and hot and beautiful. And so is the coin."

Sara liked to play with her dolls in the shower. She pretended they were having a tea party or going to the beach. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had long yellow hair and a pink dress. Sara always took Lily with her to the shower.

One day, Sara's mom said she had a surprise for her. She gave Sara a new doll. The doll had short brown hair and a blue dress. She said it was a gift from her aunt. Sara looked at the doll and said, "Thank you, mom, but I don't want it. I want Lily."

Sara's mom said, "But Lily is old and dirty. She has holes in her dress and her hair is falling out. This doll is new and clean. She is much better than Lily. You should replace Lily with this doll."

Sara felt angry and sad. She said, "No, mom, I love Lily. She is my best friend. I don't care if she is old and dirty. I don't want to replace her. Please give me back Lily."

Sara's mom said, "I'm sorry, Sara, but I already threw Lily away. She was too broken to keep. You have to play with this doll now. She is your new friend. You will like her if you give her a chance."

Sara started to cry. She ran to the bathroom and looked in the trash. She hoped to find Lily, but she was not there. She felt very lonely and scared. She did not want to play with the new doll. She wanted Lily back. She wished her mom did not replace her. She wished her mom was calm and nice. She wished everything was different.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play with blocks. They have many blocks of different shapes and colors. They try to build a big tower with their blocks.

"Look, Ben, I have a red block. It is strong and big. It can fit on top of the tower," Sam says.

"Let me see, Sam. I have a blue block. It is strong and big, too. It can fit on top of your red block," Ben says.

They put their blocks on the tower. The tower grows taller and taller. They are happy and proud.

But then, Lily comes. Lily is their baby sister. She likes to grab things and throw them. She sees the tower and smiles. She crawls to the tower and pulls a block.

"Uh-oh, Lily, no! That is our tower. Do not waste our blocks!" Sam shouts.

But it is too late. The tower falls down. The blocks scatter everywhere. Ben and Sam are sad and angry.

"Lily, you are bad! You broke our tower. You made a mess. Go away!" Ben cries.

Lily does not understand. She thinks it is a game. She laughs and claps her hands. She picks up another block and throws it.

Ben and Sam sigh. They know they have to start over. They hope Lily will leave them alone. They love their sister, but they wish she would not ruin their fun.

Tom liked to throw things. He threw his ball, his toy car, his spoon. He threw them high and far and loud. He liked to see them fly and bounce and crash. But his mom did not like it. She said, "Tom, stop throwing things. You will break them or hurt someone. You will be in trouble."

One day, Tom found a big book on the shelf. It had many pages and pictures. Tom thought it was a story book. He wanted to read it, but he could not. He only knew some words, like cat and dog and mom. He was mad. He did not want a story book he could not read. He wanted to throw it.

He took the book and ran outside. He saw a big tree with a hole. He thought it was a good place to throw the book. He threw it hard and fast. He heard a thud and a squeak. He was happy. He threw the book in the hole.

But then he heard a voice. It was a small and angry voice. It said, "Hey, who threw this book at me? It is heavy and hard and it hurts. It is not a nice thing to do. Come out and say sorry."

Tom was scared. He did not know who was in the hole. He did not want to say sorry. He wanted to run away. But he could not. He saw a furry face peek out of the hole. It was a squirrel. It had the book in its paws. It looked at Tom with big eyes. It said, "This is not a story book. This is a diary. It has secrets and memories and feelings. It is not empty. It is full. It belongs to someone who loves it. You should not throw it away. You should give it back."

Tom felt bad. He did not know the book was a diary. He did not know it had secrets and memories and feelings. He did not know it belonged to someone who loved it. He did not mean to hurt the squirrel or the book. He said, "I'm sorry, squirrel. I did not know. I was mad and I threw it. Can I have it back? I will give it back to the owner."

The squirrel nodded. It gave the book to Tom. It said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good boy. You said sorry and you will give it back. That is the right thing to do. But next time, do not throw things. You might break them or hurt someone. You might be in trouble."

Tom nodded. He took the book and ran back to the house. He found his mom and gave her the book. He said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I threw your diary. I did not know. I found it on the shelf. I thought it was a story book. I could not read it. I was mad. But a squirrel told me it was a diary. It has secrets and memories and feelings. It is not empty. It is full. It belongs to you and you love it. I will not throw it again. I will not throw anything again."

His mom hugged him. She said, "Tom, I'm proud of you. You said sorry and you gave it back. That is the right thing to do. And you learned something new. You learned that books are not just stories. They are also diaries. They have secrets and memories and feelings. They are not empty. They are full. They belong to someone who loves them. And you can love them too. You can read them and learn from them and enjoy them. But you have to be careful and respectful. You have to treat them well. You have to not throw them."

Tom smiled. He said, "I understand, mom. I will be careful and respectful. I will treat them well. I will not throw them. I will read them and learn from them and enjoy them. Can you read me a story now?"

His mom smiled. She said, "Of course, Tom. I will read you a story now. Let's go to your room and pick a book. And maybe we can find a nut for the squirrel too. He was a good friend to you and the book. He deserves a treat."

They went to Tom's room and picked a book. They also found a nut for the squirrel. They read the book and enjoyed it. They gave the nut to the squirrel and thanked it. They were happy. They did not throw anything. They learned something. They loved something. They had a good day. The end.

Ben and Mia are friends who like to create things with magnets. They have many magnets of different shapes and colors. They can make animals, cars, houses and more. They have fun playing with their creations.

One day, Ben and Mia find a big magnet in the garage. It is shiny and strong. They want to use it for their creations. But they do not ask their mom or dad if they can take it. They think it is okay to take it without asking.

They take the big magnet to their room and start to create. They make a big robot with the big magnet and some smaller magnets. They are very proud of their robot. It looks cool and playful.

But then, something bad happens. The big magnet is so strong that it pulls all the other magnets in the room. It pulls the magnets from their toys, their books, their pictures and their clothes. It makes a big mess. It also pulls the magnets from their mom's and dad's things. It pulls the magnets from the fridge, the clock, the keys and the phone. It makes a bigger mess.

Ben and Mia hear their mom and dad coming. They are angry and confused. They see the big magnet and the big mess. They ask Ben and Mia what they did. Ben and Mia feel sorry and scared. They tell their mom and dad that they took the big magnet without asking. They say they wanted to create a robot. They say they did not know it would pull all the other magnets.

Their mom and dad are not happy. They tell Ben and Mia that they should not take things without asking. They tell them that they should be careful with magnets. They tell them that magnets can be dangerous and damage things. They tell them that they have to clean up the mess and return the big magnet.

Ben and Mia learn their lesson. They say they are sorry and they help to clean up. They promise to ask before they take things. They promise to be more careful with magnets. They still like to create things with magnets, but they use smaller and safer magnets. They also share their creations with their mom and dad. They are happy and playful.

Lily and Tom stopped and looked at their mother. They both said, "It's my crown!"

"Look, this is Mr. Piggy. He can fly and sing and dance," Tom said, holding a doll with a pig's head and a rag for a body. He threw the doll in the air and made a loud oink.

Lily frowned. She did not think that was a nice way to play with dolls. She thought Mr. Piggy looked silly and dirty. She did not want him to join the tea party.

"Tom, please stop. That is not a doll. That is a rag. He does not belong here. He is not polite or pretty," Lily said, pointing at Mr. Piggy.

Tom did not like what Lily said. He thought Mr. Piggy was fun and cool. He did not care if he was polite or pretty. He wanted to play with him.

"Lily, you are mean. Mr. Piggy is a doll. He is my friend. He can do whatever he wants. He is not afraid of you," Tom said, sticking his tongue out.

Lily and Tom started to argue. They raised their voices and said mean things to each other. They did not want to share or play together. They made a lot of noise and mess.

Their mom heard them and came to the garden. She saw them fighting and frowning. She was not happy.

"Lily, Tom, what is going on here? Why are you yelling and throwing things? Why are you not playing nicely?" Mom asked, looking at them.

Lily and Tom stopped and looked at Mom. They felt ashamed and sorry. They knew they had been bad.

"Mom, we are sorry. We were playing with our dolls, but we did not agree. Lily did not like Mr. Piggy. Tom did not like Lily's dolls. We got angry and rude," they said, hanging their heads.

Mom nodded. She understood. She knew they had different tastes and ideas. But she also knew they had to respect and love each other.

"Kids, it is okay to have different dolls and games. But it is not okay to hurt or insult each other. You are brother and sister. You should be kind and gentle. You should share and listen. You should have fun and learn. Can you do that?" Mom asked, smiling.

Lily and Tom nodded. They agreed. They wanted to be good and happy. They wanted to play and grow.

"Mom, we are sorry. We love you. We love each other. We love our dolls. Can we hug and make up?" they asked, reaching their arms.

Mom smiled. She was proud and glad. She hugged them and kissed them. She gave them a calm and warm hug.

"Of course, you can. You are my sweet and smart kids. You can play with your dolls however you like. But remember to be nice and fair. And to have fun and laugh. Okay?" Mom said, tickling them.

Lily and Tom laughed. They felt better and closer. They thanked Mom and said sorry again. They picked up their dolls and plates and cookies. They decided to have a new tea party. They were about to put them in their mouths, when they heard a loud roar. They turned around and saw a big, scary dragon. It had green scales, yellow eyes, and a long tail. It looked hungry and angry.

"Run!" Lily shouted, dropping her blueberry.

Ben followed her, but he did not want to lose his blueberry. He held it tight in his hand. He hoped the dragon would not see it.

They ran to the house and slammed the door behind them. They were safe, but they were scared. They hugged each other and waited for their mom to come home.

But the blueberry was not a normal blueberry. It was a magic blueberry. It had a powerful spell inside it. As soon as the dragon ate it, it felt a strange feeling in its belly. It felt like it was shrinking and fading. It tried to roar, but it only made a squeak. It looked at its claws, but they were gone. It looked at its tail, but it was gone. It looked at its body, but it was gone. It had vanished.

Tom and Lily were two mice who lived in a big house. They liked to find food and play in the rooms, but they had to be careful of the cat. The cat was big and mean and wanted to catch them.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a shiny thing on a table. It was a crown that belonged to the king. The king was a man who lived in the house and had a lot of money and power. Tom and Lily thought the crown was very pretty and wanted to have it.

"Let's take the crown and make it ours," said Tom. "We can be the king and queen of the mice."

"But that is not right," said Lily. "The crown belongs to the king. He will be angry if we take it. And the cat might see us and chase us."

"Don't be scared," said Tom. "We are fast and smart. We can escape from the cat. And the king will not miss the crown. He has many other things. He is cheap and greedy. He does not share with anyone."

Tom and Lily took the crown and ran to their hole. They put the crown on their heads and felt very proud and happy. They did not see the cat who was watching them from behind a curtain.

The cat waited until Tom and Lily fell asleep. Then he crept to their hole and pounced on them. He grabbed the crown and the mice and ran to the king.

"Look what I have, your majesty," said the cat. "I have caught two thieves who stole your crown. They are cheap and greedy. They do not respect you."

The king was very angry when he saw his crown and the mice. He thanked the cat and gave him a reward. He took the crown and put it back on his head. He ordered the mice to be locked in a cage and never let out.

Tom and Lily were very sad and scared. They wished they had listened to Lily and not taken the crown. They learned that stealing is wrong and that being cheap and greedy does not make you happy. They hoped to escape from the cage and find a new home.

"Help me, Sara, it's stuck!" he said.

Sara came over and helped Ben. Together, they lifted the carpet and folded it. They put it on the sofa, and then jumped off the ship.

"Wow, this island is amazing!" Sara said, looking around. "There are so many things to see and touch!"

They ran to the coffee table and climbed on it. They found some books, a vase, a lamp, and a remote control. They pretended they were treasure, and made a pile on the table.

"Look, Sara, I found a magic wand!" Ben said, holding the remote control. He pressed a button, and the TV turned on.

"Wow, Ben, you're so clever!" Sara said, clapping her hands. "What else can you do with it?"

Ben pressed another button, and the TV changed channels. He pressed another button, and the volume went up. He pressed another button, and the TV turned off.

"This is so fun!" Ben said, laughing. "Let's see what else we can do!"

They pressed more buttons, and the TV, the lamp, the fan, and the stereo turned on and off, changed colors, and made noises. They had a great time, until they heard a voice.

"Hey, what are you doing?" the voice said. It was their mom, who had come back from the store. She saw the mess in the living room, and the carpet on the sofa.

"Sara, Ben, you have to clean up this mess right now!" she said, looking angry. "And why did you remove the white carpet? You know it's very expensive and delicate!"

Sara and Ben looked at each other, and felt scared. They knew they had done something bad. They jumped off the table, and ran to their mom.

"We're sorry, mom, we were just playing," Sara said.

"Yeah, mom, we didn't mean to make a mess," Ben said.

They hugged their mom, and said they loved her. Their mom sighed, and hugged them back.

"I love you too, but you have to be more careful and respectful," she said. "Now, help me put the carpet back, and tidy up the living room. And no more playing with the remote control, okay?"

"Okay, mom," Sara and Ben said. They helped their mom, and learned their lesson. They decided to play something else next time, something that didn't involve removing the white carpet.

Tom and Lily hugged each other. They closed their eyes and hoped it would go away. But it did not. It reached the yard and lifted them up in the air. They screamed and cried, but no one could save them. The tornado took them far away, and they never saw their home or their parents again.

Ben was a lively bunny who liked to hop and play in the meadow. He had many friends, like Lily the mouse and Max the bird. They had fun together, running, singing and finding things to eat.

One day, Ben saw a shiny thread on the ground. He was curious and wanted to touch it. He hopped closer and closer, until he reached the thread. He picked it up with his teeth and pulled it. It felt soft and smooth.

But the thread was not just a thread. It was part of a trap that a hunter had set. As soon as Ben pulled the thread, a big net fell on him and trapped him. He tried to hop and wiggle, but he could not get out. He was scared and sad.

Lily and Max heard Ben's cries and came to help him. They saw the net and the thread and realized what had happened. They felt sorry for Ben and tried to bite the net and free him. But they were too small and weak. The net was too strong and tight.

Soon, the hunter came and saw Ben in the net. He was happy and greedy. He picked up the net and threw it over his shoulder. He did not care about Ben's friends or feelings. He only wanted to take Ben home and make a fur coat out of him. He walked away, leaving Lily and Max behind.

Ben never saw his friends or the meadow again. He was unhappy and cold. He wished he had never touched the thread. He learned a hard lesson: some things are not what they seem, and curiosity can be dangerous.

One day, Lily and Tom went to the park with Mom. They saw many squirrels running and jumping on the trees. Lily and Tom liked the squirrels. They wanted to give them something.

"Mom, can we give the squirrels some nuts?" Lily asked.

"Sure, we have some in the bag. But be careful, don't get too close to them. They might be scared or bite you." Mom said.

Lily and Tom took some nuts from the bag and walked slowly to the squirrels. They held out their hands and waited. One squirrel came closer and sniffed the nuts. It took one and ran away. Another squirrel followed and did the same.

"Look, they like the nuts!" Tom said.

"Yes, they do. They are hungry and happy." Lily said.

But then, a big squirrel came and saw the nuts. It wanted all the nuts for itself. It ran to Lily and Tom and tried to grab the nuts from their hands. Lily and Tom were scared and held the nuts tight.

"Hey, stop it! That's not nice!" Lily shouted.

"Go away! These are our nuts!" Tom shouted.

The big squirrel did not listen. It pushed and pulled and scratched. Lily and Tom cried and ran to Mom. Mom hugged them and checked their hands. They had some scratches, but they were not bad.

"Are you okay, my sweeties?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom. But the big squirrel was mean. It wanted all the nuts." Lily said.

"It was greedy and rude. It did not share or say thank you." Tom said.

"I'm sorry that happened. Some squirrels are like that. But some are nice and friendly. You did a good thing by giving them some nuts. You are kind and generous." Mom said.

Lily and Tom smiled and hugged Mom. They looked at the squirrels again. They saw the nice squirrels eating the nuts and playing with each other. They saw the big squirrel alone and angry. They felt sorry for it, but they did not want to give it any more nuts. They learned that giving is good, but not to everyone.

"Lily, we can't go there," Ben said. "The sign says 'Keep off'. That means it is not for us. It is for someone else."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She wanted to go to the cross. She ran across the road without looking. She did not see the car that was coming fast.

"Look out, Lily!" Ben shouted. He was scared for his friend.

"Lily, why did you do that?" Ben asked. "Why did you not listen to me? You could have died. You were not fair to me. You were not fair to yourself. You were not fair to the cross."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your friends, obey the rules, and respect what is not yours.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big tunnel in the snow. They wanted to go inside and see what was there.

"Let's go, Tom!" Sam said. "Maybe we can find a treasure or a monster!"

"I don't know, Sam," Tom said. "It looks dark and cold. Maybe we should stay here and make a snowman."

But Sam did not listen. He ran to the tunnel and crawled in. Tom followed him, because he did not want to be alone.

The tunnel was long and narrow. It was hard to see and breathe. Tom and Sam felt scared and cold. They wished they had stayed outside.

"Sam, this is crazy!" Tom said. "We have to go back. We might get lost or freeze!"

But Sam did not listen. He wanted to see the end of the tunnel. He kept going deeper and deeper.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was an avalanche! The snow fell on the tunnel and blocked the way out. Tom and Sam were trapped!

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "We are stuck in the tunnel! We can't get out!"

But no one heard them. They were too far away.

Tom and Sam hugged each other and cried. They realized they had made a big mistake. They should have listened to Tom and stayed outside. They should have been careful and not gone into the crazy tunnel.

Moral: Listen to your brother and be careful when you play outside. Don't go into places that are dark and cold. You might get in trouble or freeze.

Ben and Mia were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big box in the garage. Inside the box, there was a toy volcano that could make red bubbles. Ben and Mia were very happy and wanted to try it.

They put the volcano on the table and added some water and powder. Then they pushed a button and waited. Soon, the volcano started to make noises and smoke. Then, red bubbles came out of the top and spilled on the table. Ben and Mia clapped and laughed. They thought it was fun and cool.

But then, the volcano made a louder noise and more red bubbles came out. The bubbles were hot and sticky. They burned the table and the floor. They also splashed on Ben and Mia's clothes and skin. Ben and Mia screamed and ran away. They were scared and hurt.

Mom and Dad heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. They saw the mess and the volcano. They were angry and worried. They turned off the volcano and helped Ben and Mia. They put cold water and cream on their burns. They also threw away the volcano and the box.

Mom and Dad said, "Ben and Mia, you should not play with things you do not know. You could have been more hurt. You should always ask us before you use something new. And you should be careful with things that can make fire or heat. They can be dangerous and hurt you and others."

Ben and Mia said, "We are sorry, Mom and Dad. We did not know the volcano was bad. We thought it was fun and cool. We will not do it again. We will ask you first and be careful. We love you."

Mom and Dad said, "We love you too, Ben and Mia. We are glad you are okay. But you have to learn from your mistake. And you have to clean up the mess. And you have to say sorry to each other. You are friends and you should help each other, not hurt each other."

Ben and Mia said, "Okay, Mom and Dad. We will do that. We are sorry, Ben. We are sorry, Mia. We are friends and we will help each other, not hurt each other."

The end.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play outside and look at the sky. One night, they saw something very bright and fast in the sky. It had a long tail and made a noise.

"Wow! What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a star that is falling," Ben said.

They ran to their parents and told them what they saw. Their parents smiled and said it was a comet. A comet is a big rock that flies around the sun. Sometimes, it comes close to the earth and we can see it.

"Can we touch the comet?" Lily asked.

"No, it is too far and too hot. But we can watch it and learn more about it," their parents said.

They gave them a book with pictures and words about comets. Lily and Ben looked at the book and saw that comets had different colors and shapes. Some were white, some were blue, some were red. The one they saw was yellow.

"Why is it yellow?" Ben asked.

"Maybe it has some gold or sand on it," Lily said.

They discussed the comet and made up stories about it. They imagined that it was a dragon's egg, or a fairy's wand, or a spaceship. They had fun and learned new things. They hoped to see the comet again.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide on the big metal slide. It was shiny and fast. But today, there was a boy on the slide who did not want to share. He said it was his slide and no one else could use it.

"Please, can we have a turn?" Lila asked the boy.

"No, go away. This is my slide. You are ignorant. You don't know anything," the boy said. He was mean and rude.

Lila and Ben felt sad and angry. They wanted to slide too. They did not like the boy. They thought he was ignorant. They knew many things.

"Remember, Lila, we learned about metal in school. It is hard and strong and can make many things. Like cars and planes and slides," Ben said.

"Yes, Ben, I remember. And we learned about sharing and being kind. That is more important than metal. The boy does not know that. He is ignorant," Lila said.

They decided to ignore the boy and play somewhere else. They found a swing and a seesaw and a sandbox. They had fun and made new friends. They forgot about the boy and the slide. They were happy and smart.

Tim and Jen were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big truck with a sign that said "Ice Cream". They ran to the truck and asked for some ice cream.

"What flavor do you want?" the man in the truck said. He had many flavors available in his freezer.

"I want chocolate!" Tim said.

"I want strawberry!" Jen said.

The man gave them each a cone with their favorite flavor. They paid him with their coins and thanked him.

They licked their ice cream and smiled. It was cold and sweet and had a good taste.

"Let's go to the swings!" Jen said.

"OK!" Tim said.

They walked to the swings, holding their ice cream. They did not see the big dog that was running towards them. The dog liked ice cream too. He smelled the cones and wanted a taste.

He jumped on Tim and Jen and knocked them down. He grabbed their ice cream and ate it. He did not care that they were crying and hurt.

He ran away, happy and full.

Tim and Jen were sad and angry. They had no ice cream and no coins. They had scratches and bruises. They wished they had not gone to the park. They wished they had stayed home.

Sara and Ben were playing hide and seek in the big house. Sara was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Ben ran up the stairs and looked for a good place to hide. He saw a door that was open a little bit. He pushed it and went inside. It was a dark chamber with many old things. Ben thought it was a good place to hide because Sara would not recognize it.

He hid behind a big box and waited for Sara to come. He heard her footsteps and her voice. "Ben, where are you? I will find you!" she said. Ben smiled and stayed quiet. He thought he was very clever.

But then he heard another sound. It was a loud click. The door of the chamber had closed by itself. Ben was scared. He ran to the door and tried to open it. But it was locked. He banged on the door and shouted. "Help! Help! I'm in here! Sara, help me!"

Sara heard Ben's voice. She ran to the door and tried to open it too. But it was locked. She could not help Ben. She cried and shouted. "Ben, I'm sorry! I don't know how to open the door! I will get help!"

But there was no one else in the big house. Sara and Ben were alone. They had run away from their parents who were busy. They had not listened to their parents who had told them not to play in the big house. They had been naughty and now they were trapped.

The moral of the story is: listen to your parents and do not go to places you do not know.

Lily and Ben were playing with a football in the park. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away.

One time, the ball rolled into a flower bed. Lily ran after it and tried to get it out. But the flowers were delicate and she broke some of them. She felt bad and said sorry to the flowers.

Ben came to help her. He saw the broken flowers and said, "Uh-oh, Lily, you made a mess. The gardener will be angry. We have to cover the flowers so he won't see them."

He looked around and saw some leaves on the ground. He picked up some leaves and put them on the flowers. Lily did the same. They covered the flowers with leaves and hoped the gardener wouldn't notice.

They took the ball and ran away. They decided to play somewhere else. They didn't want to hurt any more flowers. They learned to be careful with delicate things.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They were popular with the other kids, who wanted to join them.

One day, they saw a big cave near the park. They were curious and wanted to explore it. They took a flashlight and went inside. The cave was dark and scary, but they kept going deeper and deeper.

"Look, there's a shiny rock!" Anna said, pointing to a glittering stone on the wall.

"I want it!" Ben said, grabbing the flashlight and running to the rock.

"No, it's mine!" Anna said, following him and trying to take the flashlight back.

They started to quarrel and pull the flashlight from each other. They were so loud and angry that they did not hear a growl behind them.

Suddenly, a big bear came out of the shadows and roared at them. It was hungry and angry. It saw the two kids and wanted to eat them.

Anna and Ben screamed and dropped the flashlight. They tried to run away, but it was too late. The bear was faster and stronger. It caught them and bit them. They felt a lot of pain and then nothing.

The bear dragged them to its den and ate them. The flashlight was left on the floor, still shining on the shiny rock. Nobody ever found them or knew what happened to them. The end.

Tim and Kim are twins who like to play with blocks. They have many blocks of different colors and shapes. They can make towers, bridges, houses, and cars with their blocks.

One day, they decide to make a network with their blocks. A network is when you connect many things together with lines or roads. They use long blocks to make the lines and small blocks to make the things. They make a network of houses, cars, trees, and animals.

But Tim and Kim are also competitive. They want to have the best network. They start to argue about who has more blocks, who has more colors, who has more things. They get angry and loud.

"Your network is bad!" Tim says. "My network is better!"

"No, your network is bad!" Kim says. "My network is better!"

They start to pull and push each other's blocks. They break their network. They make a big mess.

Then, Tim does something very bad. He bites Kim on the arm. Kim cries out loud. She bites Tim back on the leg. Tim cries out loud too.

Mom hears their cries and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the broken network, the mess, and the bite marks. She is very upset.

"Tim, Kim, what did you do?" Mom says. "Why did you bite each other? That is not nice. That hurts. You should not bite. You should share and play nicely."

Tim and Kim feel sorry. They say sorry to Mom and to each other. They hug and kiss. They promise not to bite again.

Mom helps them clean up the mess. She gives them a band-aid for their bites. She tells them to be kind and gentle. She shows them how to make a new network with their blocks. A network where they can work together and have fun. Tim and Kim smile and nod. They like their new network. They like their Mom. They like each other.

Lily was a very intelligent girl. She liked to read books, draw pictures and play with puzzles. She had a big wish: she wanted to run fast like a cheetah. She thought running was fun and exciting.

One day, she saw a poster for a race at the park. It said: "Come and run with us! Everyone can join. There will be prizes and snacks." Lily wanted to go to the race. She asked her mom: "Mom, can I go to the race? Please, please, please!"

Her mom smiled and said: "Of course, you can go, Lily. But you have to practice first. Running is not easy. You have to be strong and brave and careful. Do you want to practice with me?"

Lily nodded and said: "Yes, mom. I want to practice with you. I want to run fast like a cheetah. I want to win the race. I want to make my wish come true."

So Lily and her mom went to the park every day. They ran around the trees, over the hills and across the bridges. They had fun and laughed a lot. Lily felt her legs getting stronger and her breath getting longer. She felt happy and proud.

The day of the race came. Lily wore her favorite shoes and shirt. She went to the park with her mom. She saw many other kids who wanted to run too. Some were big, some were small, some were fast, some were slow. Lily was not afraid. She was ready.

She lined up at the start. She heard the whistle blow. She ran as fast as she could. She ran like a cheetah. She passed some kids, some kids passed her. She kept running. She saw the finish line. She ran faster. She crossed the line. She did it!

She looked at the clock. She saw her time. She was amazed. She had run faster than ever before. She had run faster than some of the big kids. She had run faster than she had wished.

She heard her mom cheering for her. She ran to her mom and hugged her. She said: "Mom, I did it! I ran fast like a cheetah. I made my wish come true. Thank you for helping me. I love you, mom."

Her mom hugged her back and said: "I love you too, Lily. You are a very intelligent girl. You worked hard and you did your best. You are a winner. I am so proud of you."

Lily and Ben were at the park with their mom. They saw a big fountain with water that went up and down. Lily and Ben liked the fountain. They wanted to play in the water.

"Mom, can we go to the fountain?" Lily asked.

"No, honey, it's too cold today. You will get wet and sick," Mom said.

"But we want to play in the fountain!" Ben said.

"I'm sorry, but you can't. Maybe another day when it's warmer," Mom said.

Lily and Ben were miserable. They did not want to play on the swings or the slide. They only wanted to play in the fountain. They sat on a bench and looked at the water.

A man came to the fountain. He had a big bag of coins. He threw the coins into the water and made a wish. Lily and Ben watched him.

"Why is he throwing money in the water?" Lily asked.

"He is making a wish. He hopes the fountain will make his wish come true," Mom said.

"What do you think he wished for?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe he wished for more money, or a new car, or a big house," Mom said.

Lily and Ben thought about what they would wish for. They wished they could play in the fountain. They wished it was a sunny day. They wished Mom would let them go to the water.

They looked at the man. He did not look happy. He looked sad and lonely. He walked away from the fountain.

Lily and Ben felt sorry for him. They wondered if his wish would ever come true. They wondered if he had anyone to play with.

They looked at Mom. She smiled at them. She hugged them and said, "I love you, my sweeties. You are my best wish."

Lily and Ben smiled back. They hugged Mom and said, "We love you, too, Mom. You are our best wish, too."

They decided they did not need to play in the fountain. They had each other and Mom. They were happy. They went to play on the swings and the slide. They had fun at the park.

Tom and Anna like to play in the garden. They have a big tree with green and black olives. They pick some olives and put them in a basket. They want to make olive oil.

They go to the kitchen and ask mom for help. Mom says they need to wash the olives and smash them with a big stone. Tom and Anna take turns smashing the olives. They see a yellow juice come out of the olives. Mom says that is olive oil.

Mom puts the olive oil in a bottle and gives it to Tom and Anna. She says they can use it for salad or bread. She also gives them some cheese and tomatoes. Tom and Anna make a yummy snack with olive oil, cheese, tomatoes and bread. They eat outside in the garden.

They see the sun shine in the sky. They see the olive oil shine on their bread. They say thank you to mom and to the tree. They are happy and full. They love olives and olive oil.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big poster of a famous clown. The clown had a red nose, a big smile and curly hair. Lily thought the clown was funny and wanted to see him. Tom thought the clown was scary and wanted to run away.

"Look, Lily, it's the famous clown! He is coming to our town soon. Do you want to go and see him?" Lily asked Tom.

"No, Lily, I don't want to go. The clown is scary. He has a big nose and a big mouth. He might scare me or make me laugh too much. I don't like clowns," Tom said.

"But, Tom, the clown is not scary. He is funny and nice. He makes jokes and gives balloons. He might make you happy and not scared. Please, Tom, let's go and see him," Lily said.

Lily and Tom argued for a while. They could not agree on whether to see the clown or not. Then, they saw an old man walking by. The old man had a long beard, a hat and a cane. He looked at the poster and smiled.

"Hello, children. Do you like the famous clown?" the old man asked.

Lily and Tom looked at the old man. They did not know him. They felt shy.

"Hello, sir. I like the clown, but my brother doesn't. He thinks the clown is scary," Lily said.

"Is that so? Well, I have a secret to tell you. Do you want to hear it?" the old man said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They liked secrets.

The old man leaned closer and whispered in their ears.

"I am the famous clown. I just wear this old clothes and beard to hide. But when I go on stage, I put on my nose, my smile and my hair. And I make everyone laugh and have fun. Do you want to come and see me?" the old man said.

Lily and Tom gasped. They could not believe it. The old man was the famous clown. They looked at his eyes and saw they were twinkling. They looked at his mouth and saw it was smiling. They looked at his nose and saw it was red.

Lily and Tom laughed. They were not scared anymore. They were happy.

"Yes, yes, we want to see you. You are not scary. You are funny and nice. You are the famous clown. Thank you for telling us your secret," Lily and Tom said.

The old man hugged them and gave them each a balloon. He winked at them and walked away.

Lily and Tom ran to their mom and dad. They told them the secret. They asked them to take them to see the famous clown. They were excited and curious.

The end.

"Fire is hot and can hurt you," grandma said. "You have to stay away from it and be careful."

They tried to roast the marshmallows over the fire, but they did not know how to do it. The marshmallows got too close to the fire and burned. The fire also caught the sticks and made them smoke. Lily and Tom dropped the sticks and ran away. They were scared and sorry.

"What did you do?" grandma asked. "I told you not to play with the fire. You could have started a big fire and hurt yourself and the house."

The moral of the story is: Fire is dangerous and you should not play with it. You should listen to your elders and follow their rules. They know what is best for you and want to keep you safe and happy.

"Let me get it!" Ben said. He climbed on a stool and reached for the pear. But the branch was hard and did not bend. Ben pulled and pulled, but the pear did not come.

"Let me try!" Mia said. She climbed on the stool and pushed Ben aside. She grabbed the pear and tugged with all her might. But the branch was hard and did not break. Mia pulled and pulled, but the pear did not move.

They were both angry and frustrated. They looked at each other and had an idea. They decided to work together. They both climbed on the stool and held the pear. They counted to three and pulled with all their strength.

She picked a ring that had a blue stone. It sparkled in the light. She put it on her finger and felt happy.

"I was playing with my toys," Sara said.

Her mom smiled and hugged her. Then she saw the ring on Sara's finger. Her eyes widened.

"Sara, where did you get that ring?" she asked.

Sara felt scared. She knew she did something wrong. She tried to hide her hand behind her back.

"I...I found it," she said.

Her mom took her hand and looked at the ring. She recognized it as one of her rarest and oldest pieces. It was a family heirloom that her grandma had given her.

"Sara, this is not a toy. This is a very special ring. It belongs to me and my mom and her mom. You can't just pick it and wear it. You could lose it or break it. Do you understand?" she said.

Sara hugged her mom and said, "OK, mom. I love you too. Can I see your jewelry sometime?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, sweetie. But only with me. And only if you promise to be careful."

Sara promised. She learned her lesson. She never picked her mom's jewelry again without asking. She also learned to appreciate the rare and old things that her mom had. She hoped that one day, her mom would give her one of them as a gift.

His mom saw him and smiled. She was glad he was having fun. She joined him in the hole and hugged him. She said he was a clever and creative penguin. She said she loved him very much.

They played together in the hole until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the ducks and fish and thanked them for sharing their water. They took the bucket and shovel and left the park.
