Lily was very angry. She did not like to listen to her mom. She wanted to do what she wanted. She said, "No, mom, you are terrible. You are mean. You are not my friend. I hate you."

Lily's mom was very sad. She did not like to hear Lily say those words. She loved Lily very much. She said, "Lily, don't say that. That is not nice. I am your mom and I am your friend. I only want what is best for you. I love you."

Lily did not care. She was still angry. She threw her toys out of the bathtub. She splashed the water everywhere. She made a big mess. She said, "Go away, mom. Leave me alone. I don't love you."

Lily's mom did not know what to do. She was very upset. She said, "Lily, stop that. You are making a big mess. You are being very naughty. You need to calm down and apologize. Or else, you will have no toys, no stories and no hugs tonight."

Lily did not listen. She kept throwing and splashing. She did not want to apologize. She did not want to hug her mom. She did not want to get out of the bathtub.

Lily's mom had no choice. She said, "Lily, that's enough. You have left me no choice. I am going to close the bathtub and turn off the water. You will have no more water to play with. You will have to get out of the bathtub and go to your room."

Lily did not believe her mom. She thought her mom was bluffing. She said, "No, you won't. You can't do that. You are lying. I will have water to play with. I will stay in the bathtub."

Lily's mom said, "Yes, I will. Watch me." She reached for the faucet and turned it off. She reached for the drain and pulled it out. The water started to go down the drain. The bathtub started to get empty.

Lily was shocked. She saw the water disappear. She saw her toys sink to the bottom. She saw the bathtub get dry. She realized her mom was not lying. She realized she had no more water to play with. She realized she had to get out of the bathtub.

Lily started to cry. She said, "Mom, mom, please, don't do that. Please, turn on the water. Please, fill the bathtub. Please, let me play. Please, mom, please."

Lily's mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily, but it's too late. You had your chance and you wasted it. You did not listen to me. You did not respect me. You did not love me. You have to face the consequences. You have to get out of the bathtub and go to your room."

Lily's mom took a towel and wrapped Lily in it. She lifted Lily out of the bathtub and carried her to her room. Lily was still crying. She said, "Mom, mom, I'm sorry. I'm sorry I was bad. I'm sorry I said those things. I'm sorry I made a mess. I love you, mom. I love you."

Lily's mom said, "I love you too, Lily. But you have to learn to behave better. You have to learn to listen to me. You have to learn to be nice to me. You have to learn to say sorry when you are wrong. You have to learn to be a good girl."

Lily's mom put Lily in her bed and tucked her in. She said, "Good night, Lily. I hope you have learned your lesson. I hope you will be a good girl tomorrow. I hope you will love me and play with me."

"Yum, yum, yum!" Ben said. He licked his paw and smiled.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben said. He jumped down from the tree and ran away.

"Oh, Ben, you are hurt!" Lily said. She hugged him and licked his wounds.

"I'm sorry, Lily, I was greedy. I should have asked the bees first," Ben said.

"It's OK, Ben, I forgive you. Next time, we can search for honey somewhere else. Maybe we can find some wild flowers or fruits instead," Lily said.

They walked back to their den and cuddled together. They learned their lesson and were happy to have each other.

The man opened his bag and took out a box. He said it was a magic box. He said it could make their dreams come true. He said they only had to open it and wish. Anna and Ben were curious. They wanted to see the magic box.

The man said he had to go, but he would come back later. He said they could keep the box until then. He said they could open it if they wanted, but they had to be careful. He said the box was very powerful. He said goodbye and left.

Anna and Ben looked at the box. It was shiny and pretty. They wondered what was inside. They wondered what they could wish for. They decided to open it. They lifted the lid and saw a bright light. They felt a strange feeling. They closed their eyes and wished.

When they opened their eyes, they were not in their big house anymore. They were in a small room with no windows. They had no clothes, no food, no toys. They had nothing. They were scared and sad. They realized they had made a mistake. They wished they had not opened the box.

They heard a knock on the door. It was the man. He had a big smile and a bigger bag. He said he had come to take the box back. He said he had tricked them. He said he had taken everything they had. He said he was not their friend. He said he was a bad man.

He opened the door and saw Anna and Ben. They were young and successful. They worked hard and had a big house and a nice car. They liked to pass the ball to each other in the park. They were happy.

The man was confused. He looked at the box. It was empty. He looked at his bag. It was empty. He felt a strange feeling. He closed his eyes and wished.

He wished he had not opened the box.

Tim and his aunt went to the park. Tim liked the park. He liked to slide and swing and run. His aunt liked to sit on a bench and read a book. Her book had many gray pages.

"Can I play on the twisty slide?" Tim asked his aunt.

"Yes, you can, but be careful. The twisty slide is very high and fast," his aunt said.

Tim ran to the twisty slide. He climbed up the ladder. He saw a big boy at the top. The big boy had a mean face.

"This is my slide. Go away," the big boy said.

"No, it is not. It is for everyone. I want to slide," Tim said.

The big boy pushed Tim. Tim fell down the ladder. He hurt his knee. He cried.

His aunt heard him. She ran to him. She hugged him and kissed his knee.

"Are you okay, Tim?" she asked.

"No, I am not. The big boy was mean. He pushed me. He did not let me slide," Tim said.

"That is not nice. He should share. Let me talk to him," his aunt said.

She went to the big boy. She said some words to him. Tim did not hear them. The big boy looked scared. He said sorry to Tim. He let him slide.

Tim smiled. He slid down the twisty slide. He felt happy. He thanked his aunt.

"You are welcome, Tim. I am proud of you. You are brave and kind," his aunt said.

They hugged. They went home. They had a good day.

Lily was an independent girl. She liked to do things by herself. She did not need help to brush her teeth, put on her clothes, or eat her breakfast. She also liked to explore new places. She was not afraid of anything.

One day, she found a big, old house in the woods. She wanted to see what was inside. She opened the door and walked in. The house was dark and dusty. She saw many old things, like chairs, books, and pictures. She wondered who lived here before.

She heard a noise. It sounded like someone was crying. She followed the noise to a room. There, she saw a ghost. The ghost was white and see-through. He had a sad face. He looked at Lily and said, "Hello. Who are you?"

Lily was not scared. She said, "Hello. I am Lily. I like to explore. Why are you crying?"

The ghost said, "I am Ben. I used to live here with my family. But they are gone now. I am lonely. No one comes to visit me. No one can see me or talk to me. Except you."

Lily felt sorry for Ben. She said, "I can see you and talk to you. I can be your friend. Do you want to play with me?"

Ben smiled. He said, "Yes, I do. Thank you, Lily. You are very kind and brave. What do you want to play?"

Lily and Ben played together in the house. They had fun. They shared stories, jokes, and secrets. They forgot about the time. They became good friends. Lily was happy. She had found a new adventure and a new friend. Ben was happy. He had found someone who cared for him and understood him. They both learned that being independent does not mean being alone.

Lily did not listen. She found two masks in the trash. She gave one to Tom and put one on her face. She said to Tom: "Come on, it will be fun. Follow me."

They sneaked into the tent and grabbed some toys. They ran out of the tent, but they did not see a man who was watching them. The man was the owner of the toys. He shouted: "Hey, stop! You are stealing my toys!"

Lily and Tom were caught. They dropped the toys and took off their masks. They were very sorry. They said to the man: "We are sorry. We were wrong. We will not steal again."

The man was angry, but he was also kind. He said to Lily and Tom: "I forgive you, but you have to learn a lesson. Stealing is wrong. You have to respect other people's things. If you want to play with the toys, you have to pay for them or ask for permission. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They said to the man: "We understand. Thank you for forgiving us. We will not steal again."

The man smiled. He said to Lily and Tom: "You are welcome. Now, go and play in the park. But remember, be good and honest."

Anna is sad and angry. She says, "No, Tom, it is not fair. The aeroplane is ours. We have to share. Give me the aeroplane, Tom, give me!"

They press the button. The aeroplane makes a louder noise.

ZOOM! ZOOM! ZOOM!

Tom and Anna are shocked. They say, "Oh no! The aeroplane! Come back, aeroplane, come back!"

They run after the aeroplane. They try to catch it. But the aeroplane is too fast. It flies higher and higher. It flies out of sight.

Tom and Anna are sad. They say, "Bye, aeroplane, bye. We miss you, aeroplane, we miss you."

His dad saw the computer. He was angry. He saw all the files that Sam had loaded. He saw that the folder was his work folder. He had to finish a project for his boss. He had to be organized. But now his computer was broken. He could not work. He could lose his job.

He looked for Sam. He found him under the desk. He asked him, "Sam, did you do this? Did you load all these files from my folder?"

Sam nodded. He was sorry. He said, "I wanted to play. I did not know it was bad. I did not mean to break your computer."

His dad sighed. He was still angry, but he loved Sam. He said, "Sam, you have to be careful with the computer. It is not a toy. It is a tool. It has important things inside. You have to ask me before you use it. You have to respect my work. You have to be organized. Do you understand?"

Sam nodded again. He said, "I understand, dad. I am sorry. I will not do it again. I will be organized. I will ask you first."

His dad hugged him. He said, "I forgive you, Sam. But you have to help me fix the computer. And you have to learn how to use it properly. Will you do that?"

Sam smiled. He said, "Yes, dad. I will do that. I love you."

His dad smiled back. He said, "I love you too, Sam. Now let's see what we can do."

The moral value of the story is: respect other people's belongings and work, be careful with technology, and learn from your mistakes.

"I'm looking for some cheese," said the rat.

"I don't have any cheese, but you can stay here and watch me bake some cookies," said Lily.

The rat agreed and watched as Lily put the cookies in the oven. But then, the oven started to smoke and the cookies were burning!

"Oh no!" cried Lily. "What should we do?"

"Don't worry," said the rat. "I know how to fix this. Let's open the window and let the smoke out."

Lily and the rat opened the window and the smoke went away. They took the cookies out of the oven and they were perfect!

"Thank you for your help, little rat," said Lily.

"You're welcome," said the rat. "Now, can we share the cookies?" 

Lily smiled and they both enjoyed the delicious cookies together.

He was so muddy, so he thought he should hide away and not let anyone see him. He hopped and skipped across the garden until he found a hiding spot under some bushes. But then he heard some voices and he saw two kids laughing.

The kids were walking in the famous garden. They were so happy and were enjoying the beautiful flowers and animals.

The little squirrel stayed still and quiet, hoping they wouldn't see him. Luckily they didn't, and the little squirrel walked away after they had gone. He was so relieved!

The little squirrel learned his lesson and now he is more careful when he plays in the garden. He even tells his friends to "watch your step" so they don't slip too!

Once there was a cute little girl. She was always excited to find new surprises. One day, she decided to leave her house and explore. She hopped on her bike and rode around town. Everywhere she went, she found new surprises. She saw a cute bird singing in a tree, a fuzzy caterpillar crawling along a path, and even a butterfly drinking from a flower. She smiled and continued her adventure.

When she got back home, she was in for a big surprise. There was a gift on her doorstep with a pretty bow on top. She opened it and found a new toy inside. She was so excited and hugged it close. It was the best surprise of all! She thanked everyone who had left her the gift and gave them a big smile. 

The cute little girl had the best time that day. She was happy to find so many surprises, big and small. She never wanted to leave.

The sun was shining and it was a beautiful day. So Lucy decided she should go for a walk. 

She walked through the fields and she saw so many things - some cows, some pretty flowers and some unusual trees. But the most amazing thing she saw was a huge garden with lots of radishes growing! 

Lucy had never seen so many radishes all together before and they were so impressive. She had never seen anything as big and red as these radishes. 

Lucy couldn't believe how big and red the radishes were. She wanted to pick one to eat, but a farmer saw her and said no - these radishes were for everyone! So the farmer shared them out, and everyone had delicious radishes for their lunch.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lizzy. She loved to take long walks in the park. One day, she was walking and admiring the trees when she heard a snap in the distance. She looked around and saw nothing. Then she heard the snap again, this time it was coming from a yummy smelling bush.

Lizzy walked closer and saw that the bush was full of juicy beef. She started to snap off pieces of the beef and ate it. It was so tasty!

But then Lizzy noticed some icy cold drops of water on the beef. She investigated a bit more and found a cold creek creeking by. She quickly jumped back, surprised by the icy water. 

Lizzy laughed and thought to herself, this was the best snack ever! From then on she'd always take a walk in the park, just in case she found a yummy beef bush again.

Once upon a time there was a small boy called Johnny. Johnny was 3 years old and he wanted to learn about the world. He was intrigued by all the new things he saw and wanted to know more.

One day, Johnny went to the park with his mother. At the park, he saw lots of different animals that he had never seen before. He wanted to know what they were and where they lived. But Johnny felt ignorant, he didn't know anything about the world. 

His mother saw his confusion and said, "Johnny, don't worry. With patience and a bit of hard work, you will learn all there is to know about the world. One day you will be very knowledgeable". 

Johnny really took this advice to heart, and set off on a journey of discovery. He began to learn more and more each day and soon he was no longer an ignorant 3 year old. He understood so much about the world now and was so proud of himself. 

Johnny continues to learn every day and loves discovering new parts of the world. He knows that learning is one of the most important things he can do.

Bobby was an eager boy. He loved to march all around the house, singing a happy song. One day, he found a special book, just for him. He marched up to his Mom and said, "Look Mom! A book!" His Mom smiled and said, "That looks like a great book for you, Bobby. Let's read it together!"

So, Bobby and his Mom sat together, and Bobby opened the book. He was excited to discover lots of colorful pictures! He marched his fingers across each page, shouting out the words that he recognized. His Mom laughed and said, "Oh Bobby, you are so eager to learn!"
 
Bobby enjoyed the book so much, he decided to take it everywhere he went. He marched outside, carrying the book in his hands. Wherever he went, he pointed out the pictures and told everyone what they said. Bobby was so happy to have found this wonderful book and he was eager to learn more!

Once upon a time, there was a bee who was very compassionate. Every day, he would fly up and down the garden looking for food for himself and all the other bees. 

One day, a wonderful thing happened. The bee noticed something was different in the garden. A big, yellow flower had bloomed! He excitedly flew over and started to eat the sweet nectar the flower had to offer. 

Then he noticed something else, there were little black ant crawling around the petals. The bee felt compassion for the ants and decided to share the nectar with them. The bee and ants happily shared the nectar together, until all the flower was gone. 

The bee and the ants hugged goodbye before the bee flew away. The bee then flew throughout the garden and shared the happy tale of what had happened. The other bees were excited to know that their friend had been so compassionate. 

And they all lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very nervous. She was going to a dance and she wanted to make sure she looked just right. She found a pink dress that she really liked and put it on. She looked in the mirror and smiled.

The girl opened the door and went outside. She was so excited and very nervous at the same time. She got in the car and they drove off. When she arrived at the dance, she opened the door and stepped inside. Everyone was wearing pretty dresses and she felt extra special.

The girl enjoyed the evening, dancing and meeting lots of new people. She opened the door when it was time to leave and went back home. She was so happy she had opened the door of the dress and taken the chance to wear it!

Once there was a little girl who really wanted to improve her swimming skills. She practiced almost every day and she got better. But when the little girl needed help, her parents gave her the most helpful advice of all.

One day, her parents decided to take her to the shower, where they taught her some helpful tips. She learned that she needed to be more patient, and she also needed to improve her technique. She practiced as hard as she could, and with the help of her parents, she was able to make lots of progress.

The little girl was so happy, and she was grateful for all the help she had received. She was able to improve her swimming so much, she couldn't wait to show it off to her parents and her friends. She knew that patience and practice had paid off and she was proud of all her hard work.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who lived in a castle. She had a beautiful long blouse that was her favourite. It was as soft as a cloud and made her look so special.

One day she decided to go to the kingdom at the end of the beach. When she arrived, she saw a group of people who were separated into two sides. They were arguing very loudly and the princess was worried.

So she took out her blouse and waved it in the air. Suddenly, all the people united together and the princess was very happy. Everyone was best friends again!

From that day on, the princess would often wear her long blouse whenever she visited the kingdom. It reminded her of how important it is when people unite.

One day, Daddy was going out to supply the lawn. He took the lawnmower and some other tools. Mommy was very thoughtful and gave Daddy another bag with snacks, some water and her special smiles for good luck. Daddy was so happy!

He said goodbye to Mommy and was off. He mowed the lawn and cut the grass. He worked hard and made the lawn look so nice. Daddy was also very careful with the tools.

When Daddy came back with an empty bag, Mommy was so happy. She hugged Daddy tightly and said it looked beautiful. Daddy smiled and said he was tired, but he was happy because of Mommy's thoughtful treats. They both hugged and kissed each other, and enjoyed a peaceful day.

Sam and his mommy went to the park. At the park there was a big gate.
They walked up to the gate and Sam peeked. He was very excited.
Inside the gate there were lots of animals. Sam wanted to go inside, but his mommy said no. She told him it wasn't safe.
Sam was very uncomfortable. He didn't understand why he couldn't go inside. 
But his mommy said the gate was there to protect the animals. 
So they walked away and went to the playground instead. Sam had lots of fun at the playground and forgot all about the gate.

One day, a boy named Peter was very excited. He was going to work on his new puzzle!

He got the dark blue box out of the cupboard and opened it up. Inside was a big puzzle. It was a picture of the night sky!

Peter got out his chair and placed it in front of the table. He then started working on the puzzle.

First, he put together all the big pieces. Then he carefully placed the smaller pieces next to each other.

When he was done, Peter smiled. He had finished his dark blue night sky puzzle! He was very proud of himself.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sarah. She was three years old and loved to go to school every day. She especially loved the lessons she took in her brown class. Then one day, something terrible happened. A bad man came into the class and tried to steal the toys Sarah and her friends were playing with!

The teacher saw what was happening and shouted at him to stop. The bad man ran away and the teacher made sure everyone was safe. Sarah and her friends were very scared, but they were happy that they still had their toys.

Sarah decided she had to protect her class so she asked her teacher for help. They decided to lock their classroom door and make sure nobody could steal from them again. From that day on, Sarah felt safe in her brown class.

Once upon a time there was a jolly man who loved to make dough. He had lots of special tools to help him make dough and special ingredients that he mixed together to make it just perfect. Everyday he smiled and sang as he mixed and rolled out the dough.

One day he rolled out lots of dough and made the shapes of stars and moons. He took lots of different colours and used them to paint the shapes. Then he put the shapes in the oven to bake.

The shapes all came out so tasty and jolly - but then something even more special happened. A sparkly light started to shine from the stars and moons! The jolly man saw this and was so excited. He looked at the shapes and waved his arms, and the light followed his movements and sparkled even more. It was so beautiful!

The jolly man had made some special magical dough that made the shapes shine with light. From then on, he made these special shapes all the time, and each of them shined so brightly. It was a beautiful sight to see!

Mum was in the kitchen. She was making a cake. She filled a bowl full of flour and sugar. She added some eggs and milk. She stirred it all together. The mixture looked smooth and creamy.

Mum put the mixture into a round tin. She filled it all the way up. Then she put the cake in the oven.

When the cake was baked, it smelled yummy. Mum took it out of the oven. It looked delicious, but it was fragile. She put it carefully on the table. 

Mum cut the cake into slices. She gave a slice to everyone. It was so sweet and tasty. Everyone loved the cake. 

Nobody expected such a fragile cake to taste so good.

Once upon a time, there was a blueberry bush. It was the most brilliant blueberry bush in the land! Every day, it would surprise everyone with how big and juicy it's blueberries were.

One day, three very brave kids came to the blueberry bush. One had red hair, one had blonde hair, and one had black hair. Together, they tried to pick the biggest, most delicious blueberries.

One of the kids was so busy picking blueberries that she didn't notice that something had landed on her shoulder. It was a bee! It was buzzing very loudly, so she got startled and screamed. But then, she saw that the bee had a surprise - it was holding a blueberry in its mouth!

The kids laughed and thanked the bee for its brilliant surprise! They then shared the special blueberry between them and it was the most delicious blueberry ever! They thanked the blueberry bush for its juicy blueberries, and then carried on picking.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to wander. Every day, she would wander through the town, looking for new places to explore. She especially liked the shop, with all its pretty things and yummy sweets.

One day, the little girl found a new shop that she hadn't seen before. She was so excited! The shop was filled with lots of interesting things. But then, a big bossy lady came out of the back and told the girl to leave.

The little girl was sad, but she decided to wander a little further away and find something else to do. Eventually, she found a park and spent the rest of the day playing and having fun. She had a wonderful day, and never forgot the big bossy lady at the shop.

Once upon a time there was a van. It was shiny and full of fun. Inside the van there was a case with a record in it. The record was fake and something was wrong with it.

The van shaked and rattled down the street. Everyone looked to see who was inside but it was much too dark to tell.

A little boy was sitting in the back seat of the van. The record was playing in his hands and he was singing and dancing to the music. He knew it was fake and he wanted to try and make it real. 

He closed his eyes and thought and thought until he came up with an idea. He had found a pencil and some paper in the van and he started to draw and write down the words. Soon he had recorded the new and real version of the song. 

The little boy opened his eyes and beamed with pride. He was so happy he had found a way to make the fake record real!

One day, a mommy and her son went to the store. The store had a lot of things for sale.

The mommy said it was a good choice. The mattress was smooth and comfortable. 

The son liked it very much and the mommy said she would recommend it to her friends. 

They bought the smooth mattress and the son was very happy. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Betty. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad.

Every day, Betty would explore the fields around the house, looking for fun things. One day, she found something that made her very curious. It was a bottle with a strange, green liquid inside.

Betty didn't know anything about the bottle, so she opened it and took a sip. To her surprise, the liquid was very bitter and tasted bad. Her mom told her that it was poison, and Betty felt helpless.

Suddenly, there was a loud noise, and a wizard appeared. He said that he had been searching for the poison bottle and he was very angry. He waved his wand and the bottle got smaller and smaller until it was gone. The wizard said that the bottle was very dangerous and must not get into the wrong hands.

Betty learned her lesson and promised never to experiment with things that she didn't know. From then on, she was extra careful when playing outdoors and always looked before she touched.

Once there was a girl named Jenny. She was very happy and loved to have fun. Jenny's favorite thing to do was make a bicycle. Every day she would find some pieces, like metal and wheels, and put them together. 

One day it was very warm outside and Jenny decided to take her bicycle for a ride. She rode along the street, so happy and having lots of fun. 

When Jenny got home from her ride, she made some adjustments to her bicycle. She added a bell to the handlebars and new pedals to the frame. 

Jenny was so proud of her bicycle and she did more rides. Every day she went further and further, because she was so brave. 

Every time Jenny rode her bicycle, her heart felt so warm. She was so proud that she made her own bicycle.
